# 657: Come On, Fight, Groudon

"Grooo—!!"

Kyogre floated on the sea surface, quietly watching the ancient giants before it, a hint of wariness showing in its eyes.

As a super-ancient legendary Pokémon, it naturally knew the power of these ancient giants.

The previous exchange had indeed proven this point.

Admittedly, it wasn't afraid of these so-called ancient giants. Even if all of them combined, they couldn't possibly be its match.

Unless their "creator" Regigigas appeared, they alone... weren't enough.

But the problem was...

Defeating them wouldn't be easy, and the consumption would definitely not be small, nor would the time required be short.

And more importantly, those humans!

Kyogre's gaze fell on Steven, Wallace and the others standing beside the ancient giants, as well as the Pokémon following at their sides. Each of these Pokémon wasn't weak either.

Originally, the ancient giants met once every few hundred or thousand years, acting like wooden dolls, unable to cooperate and only knowing how to charge forward. But under that person's command, these ancient giants actually started cooperating, becoming even more troublesome.

This gave Kyogre a headache.

As a super-ancient legendary Pokémon, although Kyogre was violent, that didn't mean it had no brains.

In fact, in Kyogre's own view, it was much smarter than that brawn-over-brains brute Groudon.

Spending too much time here would be disadvantageous for seizing that powerful energy with great benefits.

Expending too much energy and stamina would also be disadvantageous for battling that brute Groudon.

Of course.

In Kyogre's view, these were actually "minor problems."

What puzzled it was...

"Grooo..."

Kyogre's gaze lifted, looking past Steven and the others, past the ancient giants, toward the distant sky.

It could sense it.

Its old rival Groudon was fighting humans and had even undergone Primal Reversion, activating "Desolate Land."

Besides itself and Rayquaza, there was actually someone who could make that brute Groudon use its full power?

For Kyogre, this was definitely a good opportunity.

While Groudon was being worn down, while Groudon was being ganged up on—beat the crap out of it!

"Regi!!"

Regieleki, crackling with lightning, stepped forward and roared, one hand transforming into thousands of golden lightning whips.

Having Regieleki deal with the Ground-type Groudon might not be very effective, but against the Water-type Kyogre... it was the main force among the ancient giants this time!

"Eleki—!!"

Regieleki used ancient language to convey its meaning to Kyogre.

[My master said! If you want to find Groudon, this path is blocked!!]

"Grooo..."

Kyogre's fish eyes looked at Regieleki, anger rising beneath its seemingly calm gaze.

Who's your master? You think I'll detour just because you say so?

"Regi!!"

[My master also said! If you want to fight! Then fight!]

While conveying the message, Regieleki was also thinking to itself.

That's what Master Johan said, right?

Seems like it...

Anyway.

That's roughly the meaning!

Mm!

"Eleki!!"

[Come on!]

As loyal ancient giants, they would fulfill their duties, vowing to protect what they were ordered to protect unto death—they were the most loyal guardians.

As long as there were orders, even if they fought to the death, they would never retreat a single step!

Kyogre: "..."

Pop pop pop—

Kyogre blew a few bubbles.

Is this the tone for negotiation?

Even more arrogant than me!

But it also sensed the ancient giants' determination.

Fighting these guys to the death here would waste too much time and energy.

Otherwise... should it flee first?

Kyogre pondered secretly.

After all, it was just a slight detour. There was no need to fight these guys to the death—it was meaningless...

Kyogre's heart began to lean toward retreat.

As the saying goes: the soft fear the hard, the hard fear the reckless, and the reckless fear those who don't want to live.

No need, no need, not worth it, not worth it... Kyogre comforted itself mentally, took a deep look at the ancient giants and Steven's group, then dove underwater.

The sea surface churned with turbulent waves. Kyogre finally changed direction under Steven and Wallace's watchful gaze, attempting to bypass them to find Groudon!

"Success!"

Seeing Kyogre's departure direction, Wallace let out a long sigh of relief. Not caring about maintaining his composure anymore, he plopped down on the ground.

Kyogre had taken the detour!

The plan's implementation was successful!

"No," Steven took off his suit jacket and loosened his tie again, saying gravely: "Kyogre just bypassed us, but it will definitely cause more destruction along the way..."

With that, he leaped onto Metagross's back.

"Steven, you..." Wallace was stunned by his actions.

"I need to ensure it meets Groudon at the planned location!" Steven's lips were somewhat pale as he wiped the sweat from his forehead.

Wallace's eyes widened in disbelief as he looked at him.

Wallace knew best how difficult the previous clash had been. Compared to him, Steven was definitely the one under the most pressure, expending the most energy, mental strength, and stamina.

Commanding four Regis and Metagross simultaneously, making them coordinate reasonably and smoothly—this was definitely a huge drain on Steven.

"You stay and help Sootopolis City deal with the waves and disasters caused by Kyogre's departure. I'll follow!" Steven lightly patted Metagross, then took the four Regis and chased after Kyogre.

Wallace opened his mouth, watching that departing figure, admiration appearing in his eyes.

This sense of responsibility and duty...

"Hey!"

Wallace supported himself on his knees and shakily stood up, then threw out a Poké Ball.

"Gyarados!"

"Roar—!!"

"Wallace!"

Seeing Wallace about to jump on Gyarados and chase after them together, Flannery quickly called out to stop him.

But before Flannery could speak, Wallace turned back and smiled: "Flannery, behind us is all of Hoenn."

After saying this, he said to his master Adam: "Master, I'll leave Sootopolis City to you and Flannery!"

Hoenn wasn't Steven's alone, and it shouldn't be left to him alone!

Johan, Steven...

And me, Wallace!

"Salamence, Double-Edge!!"

Buzz—

Mega Evolution energy erupted once again. The flying Salamence was completely enveloped in Mega Evolution energy, and what emerged from the brilliant evolution light was Mega Salamence!

Elite Four Drake's support had finally arrived!

However, when Salamence used Double-Edge earlier, it was covered in milky white energy, but after Mega Evolution, what enveloped Mega Salamence was sharp light blue energy, like sky-colored energy.

Aerilate!

Mega Salamence's ability was "Aerilate"—all Normal-type moves would become Flying-type and receive a certain degree of power boost!

Similar to abilities like Fairy-type's Pixilate, Ice-type's Refrigerate, Electric-type's Galvanize, etc.

"Roar—!!"

With the "Aerilate" boost, Mega Salamence's speed suddenly increased, charging straight toward the rock spire that Primal Groudon had raised.

Bang!!!

The massive lava rock spire broke under the tremendous impact!

Watching the blood-red wings flash past like crescents, Johan couldn't help but smack his lips.

So brave.

Just keep flying in front of Groudon—the more you fly around... the more you fly around, mm.

"Johan!"

Drake laughed heartily as he stood at the ship's bow, the old man leaping directly from the ship onto the small piece of land created by Mega Tyranitar where Johan stood.

"Old man, watch your safety," Johan said.

Drake swept his robes aside. Although he was getting on in years, his bronze chest still showed distinct muscle definition.

"Men of the sea never grow old!"

Johan nodded. "Alright."

Then he took out his phone. "Glacia, you heard that. I suggest binding Elite Four Drake to his position permanently!"

"Heard it," came Glacia's emotionless voice through the phone.

"You brat!" Seeing this, Drake's eyes widened, immediately getting agitated.

"Old man, business first!"

"Hmph!" Elite Four Drake snorted angrily and immediately called out: "Salamence, Hyper Voice!"

"Roar—!!"

Mega Salamence roared, sound waves immediately causing ripples centered on Primal Groudon to appear on the sea surface, spreading outward.

Loud mouth...

Primal Groudon slowly raised its head, looking at Mega Salamence in the sky, indescribable anger flashing in its eyes.

"Roar—"

So you're the one who can fly, huh? And with Aerilate too?

Immediately, Primal Groudon went all out, lifting its foot to stomp the ground fiercely while roaring viciously.

Rumble rumble—

The sea floor suddenly cracked, and massive rock spires like cliffs, wrapped in scalding lava, instantly shot up from the ground like sharp swords piercing the clouds.

Precipice Blades!

Terrifying impact force, incredibly scalding temperatures, piercing speed at the extreme...

"Roar!!"

Mega Salamence's eyes widened as its abdomen was struck by Precipice Blades, crying out in pain.

"Salamence!"

Drake hadn't expected Precipice Blades to have such fast attack speed, and was there no distance limit?

Mega Salamence was clearly quite far from Primal Groudon.

Seeing this scene, Terastallized Mega Tyranitar's expression showed slight emotion.

This move...

Having just crunched down an Earth Plate fragment, Tyranitar felt... this move was interesting and quite aggressive too.

Stone Edge?

If that was the case...

Terastallized Mega Tyranitar lowered its head in thought.

Johan, who also witnessed this scene, twitched his mouth.

I told you the more you fly around, the higher Primal Groudon's aggro would get, right?

Didn't you see that when we were holding back Primal Groudon earlier, our Dragonite didn't fly at all?

As for why the Ground-type move Precipice Blades could hit the Flying-type Mega Salamence...

This was normal.

Rayquaza was also Dragon and Flying-type, but it still had to dodge Groudon's Precipice Blades.

Was this reasonable?

Very reasonable.

But complaints aside, they were on the same side now.

"Help out!"

Johan called without hesitation.

"Gengar, Phantom Force!"

"Ka-kaah~!"

Gengar grinned, its crimson tongue licking its lips as its form seemed to melt, slowly disappearing into the shadows on the ground.

As Gengar sank in, that shadow visibly expanded and spread at an incredible rate. In just moments, like ink dropped on rice paper, it had stained a large area of the sea.

The thick Ghost-type energy made Primal Groudon feel somewhat uncomfortable.

What move was this?

Drake was quite surprised.

He was from the same generation as Agatha from Kanto, and the two had even battled more than once when they were young. If not for Oak protecting her...

But regardless, Drake quite acknowledged Agatha's "Ghost Legion."

But even Agatha's Gengar couldn't perform such a move, right?

Splash—

Mega Salamence, struck by Precipice Blades, fell into the black "seawater" and was instantly swallowed.

But in the next moment, Mega Salamence emerged from beside Johan's feet.

Hm?

Seeing the suddenly appearing Mega Salamence, Drake was even more surprised.

Space?

"Roar..."

Mega Salamence shook its head vigorously twice, the severe pain in its abdomen making it grimace.

Almost—just a little more and it would have been pierced through.

"Roar!!"

Primal Groudon wouldn't stop its actions because of Johan and the others. Since they dared to block it, then destroy them all—use them all to fill the sea!

"Dragonite!"

"Draaa—!!"

Getting Johan's command, Dragonite excitedly shot into the sky, showing no fear despite witnessing Mega Salamence's encounter with Precipice Blades.

Try to hit me first!

Outrage activated!

Boom!!

Dragonite charging skyward was immediately enveloped in dark red violent airflow, its entire aura and state becoming incredibly savage.

But with Johan's aura soothing and the skillful experience accumulated from multiple uses, the violence in Dragonite's eyes instantly faded, replaced by calm clarity in its bloodshot pupils.

"Roar!!"

Another flying one!

Primal Groudon was furious beyond measure.

The previous one was at least acceptable—its wings were big enough—but Dragonite...

Why could you fly with such a big body and such tiny wings?

Boom!!

Terrifying Precipice Blades instantly shot up from the ground.

"Dragonite, Extreme Speed!"

Whoosh—

Dragonite in the sky immediately became a white streak, dodging the Precipice Blades' impact at incredible speed.

Luck, definitely luck!

Primal Groudon's golden eyes stared fixedly at the rapidly moving Dragonite, using Precipice Blades again.

Rumble rumble—

"Dragonite!" Johan waved his hand grandly. "Dragon Rush!"

"Draaa—!!"

The rapidly flying Dragonite was enveloped in blue-purple dragon energy, which then became blue-purple airflow in its rapid flight. But when its speed reached the extreme...

Outside the blue-purple airflow, a layer of light cyan appeared, that airflow also wrapping around Dragonite to form an arrow shape.

Thud! Thud! Thud!

Terrifying lava spires shot up one after another, but none could hit Dragonite, or rather, none could keep up with Dragonite's speed.

When Primal Groudon saw Dragonite charging straight like a sharp arrow, it unconsciously froze.

"Roar..."

This is...

Boom!!!

The straight arrow struck hard against that mountain-like red-gold figure!

Thunder-like roaring exploded continuously, the entire sea surface rolled up terrifying waves, constantly churning, crashing, and colliding, blooming into spray.

Under the massive impact, Primal Groudon let out a muffled groan, then... its steps staggered backward twice before finally sitting down on the lava land it had created.

Bang!!

The ground crumbled, waves surged, dust mixed with lava and seawater—a shocking sight.

The trainers and news workers on the aircraft all opened their mouths wide.

"Holy shit..."

Someone unconsciously swallowed and cursed.

Primal Groudon... got knocked down?!

Primal Groudon, sitting on the ground, gently touched its undamaged chest. It hurt a bit, but...

Its current expression was so bewildered and clear.

Was that Rayquaza just now? Dragonite? Caterpie?

Honestly.

Primal Groudon was truly caught off guard by Dragonite's attack.

Just moments ago, it almost thought Rayquaza had suddenly appeared without any warning.

Now coming to its senses...

It immediately felt both embarrassed and annoyed.

Actually knocked down by an ordinary Pokémon?

At the same time, Primal Groudon was also somewhat puzzled.

Ninetales, Gengar, Dragonite...

This human's Pokémon—why did each one seem to carry traces of other legendary Pokémon's aura?

Were these all "ordinary" Pokémon?

"Roar!"

Primal Groudon slammed the lava ground, shaking its massive body and standing up with earth-shaking tremors, wanting to find Dragonite but unable to locate it in the sky.

Dragonite had already returned to Johan's side, also withdrawing from Outrage state, holding its reddened head and grimacing.

"Draaa..."

So hard...

Dragonite marveled at Primal Groudon's defensive power.

But fortunately, it didn't hit me.

Johan stuffed a handful of energy cubes into Dragonite's hands, then placed his hand on its arm. Aura!

"Draaa~(ˊˋ)"

Dragonite comfortably squinted, gently flapping its wings.

So comfortable...

Drake, who had witnessed the entire process, finally recovered from his shock.

Johan's Dragonite... knocked down Primal Groudon?

That was truly physical and realistic "knockdown."

"Was that Dragon Rush?" Drake couldn't help asking.

Johan shrugged at Drake: "Old man, didn't you hear me call it? If it wasn't Dragon Rush, what else could it be?"

Drake turned to look at the similarly recovering Mega Salamence. Mega Salamence's wings trembled, its expression suddenly changing.

"Roar!"

Don't look at me! If that was Dragon Rush, I'll eat your ship!

Primal Groudon rubbed its chest, grimacing as it stood up.

That didn't count!

Just now it looked too much like Rayquaza and caught it by surprise!

"Here it comes!" Drake called out in a low voice, taking out a Poké Ball.

"Roar!!"

A surging flame like a volcanic eruption mixed with red-hot lava gushed forth.

Fire Blast!

Changed moves?

"Urshifu, Armarouge!" Johan called.

At the same time, the aura power in his body surged rapidly.

Aura, infuse!!

"Garruu zzZ"

Urshifu, which had been standing quietly to the side with closed eyes, suddenly moved, letting out a low roar and assuming a seemingly ordinary fighting stance.

Splash splash—

Without any extra movements, the seawater around them began to surge.

The seawater seemed to be under Urshifu's control.

Clang!!

Urshifu's eyes suddenly opened!

Its body seemed to emit the sound of taut zither strings, like a drawn bow string's low trembling.

As it threw a punch—

Break!!

The ground beneath Urshifu trembled as it threw its punch. The water flow seemed to take the shape of a fist, carrying unstoppable momentum as it surged forward.

The sea waves on both sides rose like broken barriers, and in the depressed seawater was Urshifu's punch.

"Garruu!!"

Boom!!

Urshifu's incomparable punch combined the flowing continuity of Surging Strikes with the ferocity of Wicked Blow.

Colliding with Primal Groudon's Fire Blast!

At the same time.

Armarouge, whose entire body was wreathed in flames, had red-gold fire swaying around it. When its arms came together to form a golden cannon barrel, the flames around its body instantly extinguished.

All flames, all heat, concentrated in the cannon barrel.

Condensed but not released!

Buzz buzz buzz—

Inside Armarouge's golden cannon barrel, flames and aura intertwined, gradually changing the barrel from gold to red.

Hiss—

Water vapor couldn't even approach the barrel before instantly vaporizing into white mist and disappearing.

Crack crack crack!

Fine cracks appeared on Armarouge's red armor, with signs of growing larger.

That's enough.

"Armor Cannon, fire!"

Boom—

Blinding light burst from the cannon mouth. Armarouge's feet gripped the ground firmly but still uncontrollably flew backward at high speed, carving two deep, charred furrows in the ground!

But following Urshifu's punch, Armarouge's Armor Cannon also collided with Primal Groudon's Fire Blast!

Boom!!!

Violent waves surged again. Primal Groudon's Fire Blast scattered into sparks that finally fell into the ocean.

Meanwhile, Urshifu's punch and Armarouge's Armor Cannon had long since vanished without a trace.

Still blocked it!

Johan breathed a slight sigh of relief, patting his chest to catch his breath, feeling exhausted.

He had already released Tyranitar's Terastallization and Mega Evolution.

Honestly, this was his first attempt at combining Mega Evolution with Terastallization. Whether it was because Tyranitar was too compatible with Terastallization or some other reason, the consumption was... somewhat less than he'd imagined.

But even so, it was still far more draining than pure Mega Evolution.

If it were someone else, a different Pokémon... Johan felt not everyone was qualified to attempt simultaneous Mega Evolution and Terastallization. Maybe a super rookie could.

Additionally.

Heavily consuming aura also left him with considerable temporary aftereffects.

As for the mental and physical exhaustion from commanding battles... let's not even talk about that.

No wonder people could actually exhaust themselves to death commanding Pokémon battles.

Steven commanding the three Regis to fight the Hoenn duo for 22 days before dying of exhaustion in the special manga made sense.

Drake, standing behind Johan and watching him almost single-handedly block Primal Groudon's attack, nodded with satisfaction.

Remarkable young talent.

With such power in Hoenn... he could rest easy.

"You rest for a bit. Leave the next part to this old man temporarily," Drake said.

"Old man, you..." Johan was stunned.

Drake cracked his neck and patted his arms.

"Nothing much to say. If I go all out, I should last about half an hour."

With that, he shrugged his shoulders, letting his wide captain's coat fall, revealing a body comparable to Master Roshi's.

"Tsk..." Johan clicked his tongue.

Elite Four Drake threw out Poké Balls, summoning his "Dragon Guard."

"Speaking of which..."

Drake suddenly turned his head and asked:

"Where are your legendary Pokémon friends?"

Although from the beginning they indeed hadn't counted Johan's so-called "legendary Pokémon friends" in this operation's battle calculations, saying they had no expectations would be false.

Of course, Drake was just asking, slightly lightening the current mood and atmosphere. He could sense Johan's fatigue too.

"Oh, them..." Johan pressed his temples, feeling like there was a vicious creature inside violently throbbing.

"The 'delivery service' isn't home, so they... had flight delays."

Delivery service?

Flights?

What was all this about?

Phew—

Johan exhaled again, his expression slightly relaxed as he said:

"But old man, you're too late. This battle... might not have a chance for you to continue performing."

Hm?

Drake, who was just preparing to go all out, was stunned.

What did that mean?

Grooo—

Suddenly.

In the distance, two black and white dots appeared in the sky, transmitting melodious cries accompanied by crimson that dyed the sky and lightning-flashing blue plasma.

Johan grinned.

Finally arrived.

Giratina's "running away from home" and staying away for so long made many of his "reinforcements" have to come on their own, which was quite inconvenient.

"After this is over, I need to ask Giratina what it's been up to. Abandoning home like this?"

Fortunately, Johan and his little ones had all grown up somewhat. If not comparable to Champions, at least when facing a single legendary Pokémon, persisting for a while wasn't a problem.

It was just that facing Primal Groudon, equivalent to a Mega Evolved first-tier legendary, put relatively more pressure on them.

"They're here."

"Roar..."

Two more flying ones...

Primal Groudon narrowed its eyes, withdrawing its previously surging energy and immediately looking toward the approaching black and white dragons.

From such a distance, Primal Groudon sensed threat from them!

By feeling, was it Truth and Ideals?!

Primal Groudon had an impression of them. These two could be considered... among the most "friendly" legendary Pokémon toward humans. As long as they acknowledged a trainer, they would follow forever.

But when did Truth and Ideals start following the same trainer?

"Grooo—!!"

White dragon Reshiram spread its snowy wings, bringing cyan flames across the sky.

"Roar—!!"

Black dragon Zekrom's turbine spun at high speed, blue lightning wrapping around its entire body, causing its speed to suddenly surge!

Hmph!!

Primal Groudon snorted white vapor from its nose, clenching both fists.

Even facing two legendary Pokémon, when had it ever been afraid?!

But the next moment.

A massive black hole suddenly flew out from behind it—a surprise attack Primal Groudon hadn't anticipated.

Looking back.

It was a cold-faced Darkrai!

"Mere Groudon..." Darkrai's expression was "disdainful" as it glanced at Primal Groudon sideways.

I've even shattered Arceus before—still afraid of you, mere Groudon?

Another one...

Groudon's heart sank.

It could sense that although Darkrai wasn't as threatening as the black and white dragons, that didn't mean it posed no threat.

But even so!!

"Roar!!"

You probably don't know which "reckless" my "Groudon's recklessness" refers to, huh?

Thud thud thud thud—

The entire sea exploded as massive lava-like spikes pierced through.

Isn't it just three legendary Pokémon?

I'll show you how to fight!

Boom!!!!

The vast sea surface rolled up endless waves.

But they quickly evaporated and disappeared under the multi-party energy.

Drake and the trainers and news workers on surrounding aircraft all watched the scene in shock.

What were they seeing?

Legendary Pokémon VS legendary Pokémon!

No, it was legendary Pokémon ganging up on a legendary Pokémon!

Was this Johan's power?

Legendary Pokémon as helpers?

"Damn! The current's too strong—electronic equipment is failing!" The news workers suddenly realized their filming equipment wasn't working.

"Thank goodness we got footage of the black and white dragons appearing earlier..."

"Old man, stop watching and fight!"

Johan advanced on ice with Ninetales' accompaniment.

"Oh, oh, oh, right."

Elite Four Drake came to his senses, looking at Johan with a somewhat complex expression before mounting Mega Salamence to command his Pokémon in coordinated battle!

"Roar!!!"

Primal Groudon roared continuously while fighting and retreating, actually being forced out of the current sea area.

But Primal Groudon was truly strong, enduring the siege of the twin dragons, Darkrai, plus Gengar and the others while still having strength to resist.

But no problem.

We have a "power bank."

"Victini!"

"Vii~(＾＿－)"

Out of energy?

Here's infinite energy!

Mm, energized now!

Primal Groudon's heart was bitter, but it wouldn't say... no, it couldn't take it anymore.

"Roar!!!"

What exactly do you want?!!

"So you can talk," Johan raised his hand, and the surrounding legendary Pokémon and Pokémon all temporarily stopped their actions. "Earlier you didn't respond to me, so I thought you couldn't speak."

Primal Groudon: "..."

"Come on, fight, Groudon."

Fight?

Groudon felt like there was a breath stuck in its chest, stuffy and uncomfortable.

Its golden eyes surveyed the surroundings.

Who would have thought this "little thing" was so strong and could call so many legendary Pokémon?

Legendary Pokémon aside, his individual Pokémon were all quite strong. Perhaps they couldn't deal main damage, but...

Like Tyranitar and Ninetales—as long as they seized its weather control, even for just a few seconds, it was enough to make it suffer.

"Darkrai?" Darkrai crossed its arms, tilting its head up at a forty-five-degree angle as black mist swirled around it, showing some melancholy: "Back when we ganged up on Arceus, Johan only called about a dozen legendary Pokémon... mm, like them, just about a dozen."

Primal Groudon: "(ω)!!!!"

A dozen?

That's all?

Ganging up on Arceus?

You guys?

This human?!

Primal Groudon looked at the "tiny" Johan, shock uncontrollable in its eyes.

Was this human that ruthless?

"Hey, don't listen to its bragging," Johan waved his hand.

Bragging...

Primal Groudon breathed a slight sigh of relief.

"It was just... about eight or nine."

Primal Groudon: "..."

"Alright." Johan clapped his hands, jumping onto Reshiram's back and unconsciously grabbing the twin tails as they flew up to eye level with Primal Groudon.

Mm, much more comfortable for the neck.

"Groudon, shall we negotiate?" Johan suggested.

Negotiate?

The pride in Primal Groudon's heart surged again as it looked at Johan disdainfully.

"Roar?"

Negotiate? Although you're not bad, but negotiating...

"Oh." Johan nodded. "That works too."

He patted Reshiram's neck, slowly retreating under Primal Groudon's wary gaze while muttering quietly:

"We don't need to fight it to the death right now. When Kyogre comes, we'll help Kyogre..."

"Roar!"

Wait a minute!

Hearing "Kyogre," Primal Groudon suddenly jolted.

It could lose to anyone, be beaten by anyone, but it absolutely couldn't lose to Kyogre!

Johan's face showed a smile tinged with mockery.

Thud—

Landing.

"This is..." Drake looked at Groudon, which had released its Primal Reversion and was sitting at the edge of its lava land looking ready for action.

"Negotiated," Johan gently stroked the white fur on Reshiram's neck. The texture was really good, second only to Cynthia's.

Reshiram glanced at him with annoyance but didn't dodge.

"Negotiated?"

"When it fights Kyogre later, we'll help it," Johan said.

"Help it?" Drake was stunned.

So the result was still fighting?

"It's fine." Johan pressed down with his hand, signaling the old man to stay calm. "Later, whoever takes the lead, we'll help the other one beat them up. Just maintain balance."

Drake looked at Johan and unconsciously stepped backward.

"Hm? Old man, you..."

"Stay away from you to prevent being sold out while happily counting money for you."

Johan: "..."

"TYRA."

Tyranitar walked up to Groudon, showing no fear in its eyes, even taking out some diamonds to ask if Groudon wanted any.

"Roar!!"

Groudon snorted hot white vapor from its nose, looking like it didn't want to bother with Tyranitar.

But Tyranitar just continued talking to itself:

"TYRA..."

I learned your "Lava Burst" move from earlier. Don't know if I got it right...

"Roar?!"

Groudon's eyes widened.

Lava Burst? You're the one with Lava Burst! Your whole family—

Swoosh—

Several pairs of eyes looked over.

Tyranitar clapped its hands and blew on its palms twice.

"TYRA..."

I'll try it out. See what I got wrong.

With that, its expression suddenly became serious, a surging Ground-type energy appearing around its body.

There was Tyranitar's own energy, and also... remnant energy from the Earth Plate fragment that hadn't been completely digested.

Stone Edge!

Thud thud thud—

Sharp rock columns shot up from the ground one after another.

Wrong!

Groudon, squinting, rumbled as it stood up, looking at those rising rock spikes with traces of lava flowing on them in disbelief!

What the hell!

Groudon looked at Tyranitar, the surprise in its eyes impossible to suppress.

Really what the hell.

This was just... learned by observation?

Seeming to notice the commotion here, Johan said cheerfully:

"Very normal. Our young... tyrant is just like that. Next time I'll introduce you to Garchomp—it has a lot of experience in this area."

# 658: Teacher Johan Crushed Kyogre's Skull! (Two-in-One Chapter)

"Grooo!!"

The sea surged with turbulent waves as Kyogre emerged halfway from the ocean depths, suddenly turning back to look at Steven, Wallace, and the ancient giants following behind it.

What exactly were these guys trying to do?!

Kyogre became alert.

But when it stopped, Steven and the others also stopped, neither approaching nor communicating, just silently tailing Kyogre with the demeanor of stalkers.

These guys!

"Regi!"

Regieleki stepped forward, then seemed to malfunction as its signal lights flashed frantically. Only after Kyogre waited somewhat impatiently did Regieleki finally seem to remember what Johan had instructed it to say earlier.

"Eleki~"

[We're... going the same way.]

Kyogre: "..."

You could choke a fish to death!

Going the same way?

What kind of "same way" was this? When it didn't move, they didn't move. When it moved, they followed all the way.

Could it be...

Kyogre's heart jumped as a bold guess occurred to it.

Were they planning to take advantage when it and that blockhead Groudon started fighting, reaping the benefits?

That wasn't impossible!

It needed to speed up!

"Grooo—!!"

Kyogre let out a long cry, diving down with a splash—

Raising towering waves, it no longer held back, heading toward Groudon at maximum speed.

At the same time, it made up its mind.

Before fighting Groudon, it would definitely clear out these "small fry" first, so they wouldn't interfere with the fight!

"What did Regieleki say to Kyogre?" Wallace couldn't help but whisper.

Steven rubbed his temples without answering, just giving a "do you think I understand?" look.

Obviously, these were all things Teacher Johan had instructed beforehand.

Wallace came to his senses, somewhat enlightened and amazed:

"Is this Teacher Johan's ability as a 'Pokémon psychologist'? Having complete psychological control over Pokémon, even legendary Pokémon..."

The subsequent development went much smoother than imagined.

To try to shake off Steven and the others' "tracking," Kyogre proceeded at full speed to find its mortal enemy Groudon, not attacking the cities and towns along the way.

But where Kyogre passed without restraint, fierce winds arose, waves reached the sky, and rain poured down.

Although the Elite Four members who were on guard no longer needed to clash directly with Kyogre, they still had to stay in their assigned areas to minimize the "disasters" caused by the giant waves.

Fortunately, everything went smoothly.

"TYRA!!"

Tyranitar roared loudly, dust flying from under its feet as its thick tail slammed down heavily.

Bang!!!

Accompanied by the surge of Ground-type energy, a solid rock spike covered in lava shot up from the ground.

Precipice Blades?

No, Stone Edge!

However... the difference from ordinary Stone Edge was quite significant, and its destructive power was completely incomparable.

After using this move, Tyranitar turned to look at the enormously massive Primal Groudon beside it.

"Roar..."

Primal Groudon snorted lightly.

Boom!!

A terrifying rock pillar dozens of times larger than Tyranitar's spike burst from the ocean, the scorching lava seeming to distort the air itself—clearly much more ferocious than Tyranitar's "Stone Edge."

But...

Groudon's current feelings were very complex, extremely complex.

Was its move... this easy to learn?

This "little thing" had already learned it quite well in just a few hours, and even Groudon had to admit that Tyranitar had... great talent in this move.

But this was clearly its "signature move"!

But why did it feel somewhat gratified?

Like it had found its own kind.

"TYRA..."

Tyranitar nodded thoughtfully, sitting beside Groudon and contemplating its shortcomings.

Seeing this scene, Johan couldn't help but think that Uxie's claw was finally having some effect...

Whether Larvitar or Tyranitar, both were quite excellent at learning.

Turning back.

He gently groomed Reshiram's fur, while Gengar beside him was polishing Zekrom's body.

With Giratina not home and Mewtwo still seemingly "out of service area," the only ones he could call were Darkrai, Reshiram, and Zekrom.

Actually, what surprised Johan most was that he couldn't contact Rayquaza.

Logically, with the rainbow meteorite appearing and Groudon and Kyogre awakening, Rayquaza should also appear. Given his relationship with it... in this situation, it would definitely come help.

"Wonder what it's doing..."

[What?]

Reshiram leaned close to Johan, half-squinting as it enjoyed the massage service.

"Nothing." Johan shook his head. "I'll need your help later."

He took out energy cubes to continue rewarding them.

"Help who?" Darkrai asked.

Darkrai had gotten used to Johan's "trouble-making" ability and even gradually become indifferent to it.

Having even beaten up Arceus, what was there to fear from super-ancient legendary Pokémon?

"Whoever's losing, we help them."

No one could win, or Hoenn would be the one in trouble.

Darkrai nodded.

"I'm good at this."

Back when Dialga and Palkia were fighting, if it had thought as "thoroughly" as Johan did now, it wouldn't have almost been destroyed.

After that battle, plus Johan and Gengar's "influence," Darkrai had completed its "transformation."

Zekrom said nothing, just walked to Reshiram's side and nudged it, pushing it aside.

Under Reshiram's puzzled gaze...

[Bro, it's my turn.]

However, Zekrom didn't get to be "comfortable" for long.

"Johan, it's coming!"

Standing on Salamence's back and observing the distant sea, Drake saw the massive shadow rapidly moving underwater and shouted.

"Roar—"

Groudon also stood up from the lava ground, its sharp eyes staring at the distant sea surface.

"I see it."

Johan also noticed the cloud movement like "Axe Gang's entrance," contending with Groudon's weather.

Kyogre was coming!

Underwater, Kyogre also sensed Groudon's aura, especially its Primal Reversion state, and immediately stopped holding back.

"Grooo—!!!"

Rapidly surfacing, the patterns on its body were quickly replaced by gold.

Primal Reversion!

"Just meeting and immediately going all out..." Johan also sensed Kyogre's change.

No, they hadn't even met yet—Kyogre hadn't fully emerged from the depths.

Buzz—

However, as Kyogre and Groudon approached, a powerful Mega Evolution energy suddenly appeared in the sky above the waters outside Kanaz.

Then, brilliant rainbow light bloomed, and a fist-sized rainbow stone appeared in the sky above this sea area, and this stone seemed to be continuously growing larger.

Rainbow Meteorite!

As expected.

Just as Johan had predicted, once Primal Groudon and Primal Kyogre appeared, this vanished rainbow meteorite reappeared.

It was also the target that Groudon and Kyogre were fighting over this time!

Gurgle gurgle—

Primal Kyogre finally surfaced. It first looked greedily at the rainbow meteorite emitting powerful Mega Evolution energy in the sky, then turned toward its mortal enemy Primal Groudon.

When Kyogre saw Groudon's current bruised and somewhat dejected appearance, it was slightly stunned.

What was going on?

Groudon... got beaten up?

Had Rayquaza appeared?

And there did seem to be some traces of Rayquaza remaining in the air, though not obvious, Kyogre still sensed them.

But clearly, Rayquaza wasn't here now.

Great opportunity!

Primal Kyogre, after only brief bewilderment, joyfully realized this was an excellent chance!

While Groudon was weak, knock it down!

Then steal the rainbow meteorite and escape!

With this thought, Primal Kyogre didn't hesitate at all—thinking was doing!

Splash splash—

Its fins suddenly vibrated as it leaped out of the water.

Then blue light orbs appeared around its body one after another.

"Grooo!!"

Take this, Origin Pulse!!

Primal Kyogre opened its massive mouth and roared, surging energy waves gushing from those light orbs like a thunderous charge!

Instantly, the turbulent sea surface was carved open like a gash, terrifying light cannons skimming the sea surface and rushing toward Primal Groudon.

"Roar!!"

Sensing the threat, Primal Groudon also roared with all its might, massive amounts of lava surging from beneath its feet.

You actually launched a sneak attack!

Boom!!

Primal Kyogre struck first, taking advantage of Primal Groudon's weakness and slow reaction to immediately use its ultimate move without hesitation, not even giving Primal Groudon a chance to warm up or probe.

Probe?

Did old rivals need to probe each other?

The violent impact and terrifying energy exploded on Primal Groudon's body, the massive impact force sending the thirty-plus meter giant flying and even knocking it back a considerable distance!

This showed how strong Primal Kyogre was, and how much force it had used in this attack—saying it wanted to kill Primal Groudon wouldn't be an exaggeration.

"Grooo—"

Seeing that Primal Groudon indeed hadn't reacted in time, Primal Kyogre's face couldn't help but show satisfaction.

However.

It quickly shifted its attention from Primal Groudon to the rainbow meteorite in the sky.

It's mine!

Primal Kyogre flapped its fins in mid-air like a giant bird, opening its massive mouth and lunging toward the rainbow meteorite.

"Tsk..."

Johan, riding on Reshiram's back, clicked his tongue. "Kyogre is indeed a bit more 'cunning' than Groudon... but not by much."

In the original "Pokémon Mega Evolution," it was also Primal Kyogre and Primal Groudon fighting over the rainbow meteorite, then Mega Rayquaza suddenly appeared and started beating up the two idiots.

Originally, two-on-one could still hold out, but then...

Primal Kyogre took advantage of Mega Rayquaza beating up Groudon to try stealing the rainbow meteorite, only to be caught by Mega Rayquaza and instantly destroyed with one "Dragon Ascent."

The current situation... was quite similar.

"Reshiram, Fusion Flare!"

"Zekrom, Fusion Bolt!"

Johan waved his hand grandly.

"Roar—"

Red flames appeared in Primal Kyogre's peripheral vision, that scorching light and dangerous feeling making Primal Kyogre's heart suddenly jolt.

There were still experts?!

It had focused all its attention on Primal Groudon and the rainbow meteorite earlier, not noticing Johan and the others resting nearby.

"Grooo!!"

However, Primal Kyogre's reaction speed was indeed fast enough. Opening its mouth, a massive water column gushed forth.

Hydro Pump!

Boom!!!

The collision of flame and water—undoubtedly Reshiram's Fusion Flare didn't have much effect, and Primal Kyogre inevitably showed some pride.

However.

Bzzt—

Following Fusion Flare was the crackling Fusion Bolt!

Having been triggered and enhanced by Fusion Flare, Zekrom's Fusion Bolt power exploded!

Even more exaggerated than its ultimate move Bolt Strike.

Boom!!!

This time, Primal Kyogre, which couldn't react in time, was directly hit head-on by Zekrom's enhanced Fusion Bolt. Powerful electricity accompanied by intense pain caused Primal Kyogre to roar in agony and crash into the ocean, raising huge waves.

"Grooo!!"

The pained Primal Kyogre flew out again—it was furious.

Buzz—

Blue light orbs appeared around its body once more, powerful energy gathering at incredible speed again.

"Watch out!" came Drake's alarmed shout from behind.

Johan squinted, his heart skipping a beat.

Origin Pulse again!

He gripped Reshiram's twin tails and roared: "Darkrai!"

"Coming!"

Black mist surged as Darkrai appeared between Johan and Primal Kyogre, its expression solemn and stern, showing no fear.

Ridiculous.

Having taken Dialga's Roar of Time and Palkia's Spacial Rend barehanded together, why would it fear one Origin Pulse?

"Ohhhhhh—!!!"

Darkrai howled, spreading its arms as black mist swirled and a massive black hole formed between its hands, just as Primal Kyogre's Origin Pulse shot forth.

"Gengar—"

Although he trusted Darkrai's abilities completely, this was still Primal Kyogre!

Johan shouted loudly.

"Ka-kaah!!"

Gengar appeared beside Darkrai, removing its sunglasses and stuffing them in its mouth as thick black mist surged around its body.

"Mega Evolution!!"

Rainbow light enveloped Gengar, spikes suddenly becoming vicious on its back, a golden eye appearing on its forehead, and the Mega Evolution symbol flashing briefly on its chest.

Mega Gengar!

Black mist flowed from its body like a curtain, seeming to completely shroud the surrounding sky.

The rainbow light from the rainbow meteorite in the air was absorbed by that pitch-black "curtain," as if the powerful Mega Evolution energy within also gave Mega Gengar tremendous enhancement.

Hm?

Johan's heart stirred.

From his pocket, he pulled out a searing hot Z-Crystal.

Marshadow's exclusive Z-Crystal!

Spectral Thief?

He looked at the rainbow meteorite in the sky, seeming to understand why Mega Gengar's power had been enhanced.

Johan gritted his teeth.

Damn it!

Having tried Mega Evolution and Terastallization, he might as well try everything today!

"Gengar!!"

Johan shouted once more, the Z-Crystal gripped tightly in his hand overflowing with irrepressible black radiance through his fingers.

Although he didn't have a Z-Ring, Johan felt he could use it!

The Millennium Wrist on his chest became scorching hot at this moment.

Arceus's power allowed him to bypass conventional rules to some extent!

Johan, who had thought he'd need to do the Z-Move dance, immediately stopped.

He just felt a large portion of his aura power being drained again, becoming a bridge connecting him and Mega Gengar.

"Ka-kaah!!"

Sensing the Z-Crystal power infusion, Mega Gengar also roared, its tongue dancing in the air, saliva splattering.

The "Phantom Force" it had spread earlier instantly converged, forming Mega Gengar's fist as it punched out with all its might!

Take this, Old Ghost Death Punch!

"Ohhhhhh!!" Darkrai beside it was fired up, the power within seemingly excavated once more.

"Victini, now, Help!"

"Vii!!"

Even Victini's emotions were completely stirred by Johan and Gengar, infinite energy madly pouring into both of them!

Boom—!!

Primal Kyogre's Origin Pulse contacted Darkrai's super-enhanced Dark Void.

After brief rumbling.

Buzz—

All power, from Primal Kyogre and from Darkrai, instantly vanished into nothing.

Meanwhile, Mega Gengar's punched fist solidly smashed into Primal Kyogre's forehead.

Bang!!

At this moment.

Space and time in this sea area seemed to freeze.

But the next second.

Primal Kyogre's skull seemed to show some indentation as the airborne creature fell straight toward the sea surface like someone had hammered its head.

Boom!!

Water splashed everywhere, waves surged.

"Holy shit!"

Even the experienced Drake couldn't help but unconsciously curse.

The power of Mega Gengar's attack just now... had far exceeded the strongest ultimate moves of ordinary Champion ace Pokémon, right?

This kid...

"What happened?" came Glacia's nervous, intermittent voice through the earpiece.

With emergency repairs, the signal had partially recovered.

As soon as it recovered, Glacia heard the old man's profanity, which scared her.

"Oh, nothing much." Drake pressed his earpiece, quite "calmly" using an extremely flat tone: "Johan just shattered Primal Kyogre, crushed its skull, juices splashing everywhere."

Glacia: "???"

What was all this about?

But...

Teacher Johan had knocked down Primal Groudon earlier, and now crushed Primal Kyogre's skull?

"Huff—huff—huff—"

Johan, sitting on Reshiram's back, gasped heavily, sweat pouring out like his life depended on it.

If earlier with Tyranitar it was his body being drained, then this time with Gengar was like doing it dozens of times in one night—one more time and he'd be dead...

"Vii~!"

Seeing this, Victini quickly injected some recovered energy into Johan. Don't die suddenly.

With Victini's help, Johan recovered considerably.

He rubbed the little one's head in gratitude.

At the same time.

After using this move, the Mega Evolution energy around Mega Gengar quickly faded. It gasped heavily, its condition... much better than Johan's.

The purple fatty lowered its head, clenched its fist, and was somewhat surprised by its own power just now.

That feeling...

It looked up at the flashing rainbow meteorite in the sky, licked its lips, cunning gleaming in its eyes.

Primal Kyogre ultimately wasn't truly skull-crushed—it hurt quite a bit, but crushing wasn't the case. It wasn't even close to exhaustion. Following the churning seawater, it surfaced, looking at the figures in the sky with strangely clear eyes.

These guys...

"Roar!!"

At this time, Primal Groudon finally stood up again, clenching its fists and roaring excitedly.

Awesome! So awesome!

Nothing was more satisfying than watching Kyogre get beaten up.

If there was, it would be getting beaten twice!

The way it looked at Johan and his Pokémon now was so affectionate, so friendly.

This human really hadn't deceived it!

Said he'd help and helped, said he'd beat Kyogre and beat Kyogre, hitting that fat fish so hard it couldn't find north.

Awesome!

This human was great, worth associating with!

Old Groudon liked him!

Completely forgetting that before Kyogre got beaten, it had been thoroughly thrashed first. Johan beating up Kyogre was just hoping to bring these two idiots' conditions to the same level as much as possible.

It was just that he got carried away and his body was hollowed out.

Primal Groudon walked among Reshiram, Zekrom, and Darkrai, raising its chin toward the surfaced Kyogre.

Come on, fat fish!

At this moment, Primal Kyogre's eyes were full of wariness, deep wariness.

It didn't understand why Groudon could find so many "helpers."

From this perspective, Rayquaza's "departure" was very likely also beaten away.

What now?

With this lineup, unless Rayquaza came to team up with it, wouldn't it just be asking for a beating?

Moreover, besides these guys in front of it, it remembered the ancient giants chasing from behind.

If it got attacked from both sides...

Primal Kyogre's heart trembled slightly.

But that rainbow meteorite...

Primal Kyogre looked toward the rainbow meteorite flashing with colorful light in the sky.

Then it saw—

"Ka-kaah~!"

The purple fatty, hands behind its back, whistling while somehow floating beside the rainbow meteorite, looking left and right with a casual expression.

Then it "sneakily" waved its hand in the air, opening a spatial rift.

Gengar "accidentally" kicked the rainbow meteorite, and the now fully restored massive meteorite, the glowing meteorite, "rolled" right into the crack.

The crack quickly closed.

Most infuriatingly, Gengar put its hands behind its back again, continued whistling, looking left and right as if the previous series of small actions had nothing to do with it.

"Ka-kaah~"

Gengar stretched leisurely.

What nice weather today~

Primal Kyogre: "..."

Fighting Groudon... the other side clearly had more people and power.

Stealing the rainbow meteorite... who knew where the rainbow meteorite had gone now...

"Roar—"

Primal Groudon called out, clenching its fist with a fierce grin.

Come on, hurry up.

Not noticing at all that Johan had taken Reshiram, Zekrom, and Darkrai to distance themselves from it.

Both sides' strength was about balanced now—they'd intervene again when the situation called for it.

However, Groudon didn't notice, and Kyogre similarly didn't notice.

Groudon's posture was typical of using borrowed power, relying on others' strength.

"Grooo!"

Hmph!

Kyogre snorted angrily, flicked its tail to stir the seawater, turned and swam toward the vast ocean outside the Hoenn region.

I'm not like that brainless brute Groudon—charging in under these circumstances?

I'm very smart!

This big skull of mine is full of brains! Full of wisdom!

Following the principles of "a wise man doesn't fight when odds are against him" and "a gentleman's revenge is never too late," Kyogre very wisely chose to retreat.

Not fighting!

Not fighting?

Watching Kyogre swim away, Groudon scratched its head.

Huh?

But it quickly realized—with Kyogre gone, wouldn't the rainbow meteorite be all its?

However.

When Groudon looked up at the sky... where was any trace of the rainbow meteorite?

Huh?

A Slowpoke-style question mark appeared above Groudon's head.

It was truly confused.

Kyogre wasn't fighting anymore, the rainbow meteorite had disappeared too—what... was it supposed to do now?

Forget it, tired. Time to go.

The Primal Reversion energy around Groudon faded as it returned to its original appearance, turning toward the ocean completely opposite to Kyogre's direction.

As the sun set in the west, the sea surface gradually calmed, the sun losing its earlier intensity. On the golden glimmering ocean, the two super-ancient legendary Pokémon each made their exit.

"Hm?"

Seeing this scene, Johan was also stunned.

Just... not fighting anymore?

He had wanted to see if Rayquaza would appear if these two fought more.

And they just stopped fighting?

A scene unconsciously appeared in his mind...

Too bad, couldn't see it.

"Are they... not fighting anymore?" Drake approached Johan on Salamence.

"Probably too tired," Johan said.

Drake nodded thoughtfully.

That made sense.

The two super-ancient legendary Pokémon were tired, and their group was exhausted enough too.

Wait!

Johan looked at the lava land on the sea surface where the high temperature was gradually receding, suddenly realizing something.

"Wait! Groudon!" he called toward the departing Groudon.

Drake was startled.

Looking at Johan in surprise.

What are you trying to do?

"Roar?"

Groudon, already half-submerged in the sea, also looked over puzzledly.

Johan pointed at the piece of land on the sea below.

Drake understood.

Right.

This lava land was indeed troublesome...

But he heard Johan say to Groudon: "Help me remodel it."

Remodel?

Drake and Groudon both looked puzzled again.

Johan smiled slightly.

He'd always wanted to get a small island like Master Mustard, but buying or renting islands was too expensive!

And those unclaimed islands were either too far from Hoenn or had environments that were too harsh.

But with Groudon appearing like this...

Was there any island more suitable than this one in the waters outside Kanaz?

It didn't need to be very big—just process it a bit more.

Moreover, the lava that surged from the sea floor was rich in precious elements and minerals. As long as these cooled and solidified lava rocks were properly processed and turned into soil, it would become fertile land!

Groudon had made the plants in his yard wilt and smoke from the heat—shouldn't it compensate a little?

"Roar..." Groudon thought of Johan and the others' earlier "help" and nodded its massive head.

Oh...

Groudon really did help.

Probably feeling Johan was worth befriending, it reciprocated the favor.

This "remodeling" land process also gave Tyranitar another learning opportunity, following closely beside Groudon to study.

Johan felt somewhat regretful.

Too bad Kyogre ran fast, otherwise... having Groudon and Kyogre cooperate would definitely double the efficiency.

But this was enough.

As the "Continent Pokémon," Groudon's abilities in this area were unmatched.

Soon this lava land gathered into a solid island anchored in the ocean.

The island wasn't actually very large.

Too big and Johan felt he couldn't manage it, completely incomparable to Master Mustard's Isle of Armor.

But...

"Planting some berry trees, flower beds, Revival Herbs and such will be enough, and it'll definitely be fertile enough..."

Plus the invisible power of "Flower Head"...

In the future, the output here wouldn't make Johan wealthy, but at least after Larvitar evolved into Tyranitar, that "economic gap" could be filled.

Not bad, not bad.

Johan was full of beautiful fantasies about the future, unconsciously nodding.

"You're..."

Drake, having witnessed the process, seemed to guess what Johan wanted to do.

"Ahem." Johan coughed lightly and explained: "I have a heart that loves farming."

Farming was truly encoded in his genes.

Farming?

Drake understood.

In the Pokémon world, everyone had their own hobbies and pursuits.

Like how he enjoyed sailing and adventuring on the ocean, Steven liked collecting various stones, and Johan liked farming... that made sense.

Drake laughed heartily. "Haha—then I'll have to buy from you in the future."

"No problem!"

Johan made an "OK" gesture.

There it was.

The first "customer."

"Oh right."

Johan suddenly remembered, quickly pressing his earpiece and saying to Glacia, who had completely relaxed and collapsed in her chair:

"Glacia, quickly send people to search the sea areas where Groudon and Kyogre awakened..."

Reminded by him, Glacia also realized.

"I understand."

Johan added:

"Don't send ordinary ships or submarines. Send Devon's 'Abyssal' submarine, otherwise they won't reach those depths."

"The 'Abyssal'?"

Glacia didn't understand why Johan would know these things, or why other submarines couldn't reach there.

But since he said so...

"I understand."

"Oh right." Johan remembered again. "If nothing unexpected happens, you might also encounter Team Magma and Team Aqua members..."

"I understand. I'll have Sidney and Phoebe, the two Elite Four members who still have fighting capacity, lead the team."

Glacia inexplicably followed Johan's instructions completely, as if he were Hoenn's Champion.

In terms of status, Johan was still just an "ordinary" teacher, albeit with "Master Trainer" qualifications.

But considering what he'd accomplished...

Calling him Hoenn's Champion wouldn't be excessive at all.

The uncrowned king of the Hoenn region.

# 659: Mere Green Caterpillar

Kanaz City, Hoenn League Temporary Operations Command, the department handling post-battle affairs following the Kyogre and Groudon incident.

Also a temporary emergency department established to deal with the even greater disaster to come.

In a nearly sealed room.

"I don't think that was correct, and I made what I believed was the right choice at the last moment. It's that simple."

Looking into the eyes of this tall woman with an ample chest, Johan leaned back in his chair and nodded:

"I believe you, Shelly."

The person across from him was none other than Shelly, one of Team Aqua's three top administrators, and also an ocean current instructor at Kanaz Pokémon Academy, who had once accompanied Johan on the academy students' autumn outing.

Their interactions weren't actually that extensive, as Johan had deliberately avoided contact with her before.

After all, she was one of Team Aqua's three top administrators, and he hadn't had the ability to handle such a character back then.

As for why Shelly was here...

It was naturally because of the anonymous letter she had written that reached Steven and old Joseph Stone.

By informing Steven and the League in advance that Kyogre was about to awaken, she gave the Hoenn League sufficient preparation time, allowing the League to minimize the disasters caused by the collision of the two super-ancient legendary Pokémon.

Johan chose to trust Shelly's explanation.

In fact, as Team Aqua's highest administrator and one of Team Aqua's most intelligent members.

In the original work, when Team Aqua's leader Archie went mad trying to awaken Kyogre, and Shelly and others learned of the destruction Archie's actions would cause, they also tried to stop him, but ultimately failed.

"I just want to know what prompted you to make such a change." Johan leaned forward, hands supporting his chin on the table.

Shelly gently brushed her black hair aside, revealing a delicate face. Her slightly smiling eyes fell on Johan as she chuckled softly:

"Of course it's because of you, Teacher Johan."

"Me?" Johan was stunned.

"Team Aqua has been at sea for years, focusing on only two things: searching for Kyogre and making money. They simply couldn't notice your rapid rise, Teacher Johan..." Shelly said with a calm tone.

Rapid rise?

Shelly continued: "Punching Dialga, kicking Palkia, taming the black and white dragons, subduing Kyurem... I don't know what Team Aqua could use to win."

"Uh..."

Johan rubbed his chin.

Is that me?

Well, that indeed was.

Shelly spread her hands: "And the facts proved this was indeed the case, wasn't it?"

Moreover, since Shelly had always been working at Kanaz Pokémon Academy, honestly, her recognition of Team Aqua was far lower than in the original story.

"So what do you plan to do next, Shelly?" Johan changed the subject.

Although Shelly had made great contributions this time, it couldn't erase her original history as Team Aqua's top administrator. A place like Kanaz Pokémon Academy that educated people... she probably couldn't continue staying there.

"I'll go out and see the world..." Shelly lowered her eyes.

"Good idea."

Johan expressed his support.

Going out to see the world, meeting various people and Pokémon, would make anyone feel more cheerful.

He stood up, took out a piece of paper from his coat pocket, and placed it in front of Shelly. Under her puzzled gaze, he said:

"After you've finished seeing the world, if you have nothing else to do, you might consider this."

On the paper was Johan's phone number.

"I happen to need an assistant... secretary? Something along those lines anyway."

With that, he walked out of the room.

Shelly stared blankly at the number on the paper for a long while, then suddenly burst into laughter and carefully tucked the paper away.

In the temporary operations command rest room.

Steven and Wallace were both collapsed on sofas, looking like they were about to die.

It had to be said that for this operation to succeed, Steven and Wallace's battle against Kyogre and forcing it to detour had played a crucial role.

Seeing Johan enter, both men forced themselves to perk up.

"Teacher."

"Teacher Johan."

Johan waved his hand, also looking exhausted as he sank into the sofa.

He was truly tired...

This was only one day, and he didn't know how Steven had managed to fight the duo for 22 days in the manga, actually dying of exhaustion only after finishing the battle rather than halfway through.

Super Hoenn people, well deserved.

However, Johan's condition was slightly better than theirs.

It wasn't that Johan had exerted less effort or was less exhausted, but purely because he had Victini as a "power bank" for support.

"Teacher Johan, your coffee."

The command staff immediately brought coffee in.

"Thank you."

After drinking some coffee, Johan perked up slightly and said:

"Why are you both still holding on? Get some sleep."

Steven leaned back against the sofa and smiled helplessly:

"Teacher, the trouble isn't completely resolved yet."

He was obviously referring to the meteorite problem.

Speaking of which, Johan also felt it was strange why Rayquaza hadn't appeared this time.

Logically, when Groudon and Kyogre came out to cause trouble, shouldn't Rayquaza appear to "mediate"?

Taking ten thousand steps back, even if not for Groudon and Kyogre, when the rainbow meteorite appeared, Rayquaza should have shown up too...

As a result, when Johan wanted to call Rayquaza for help this time, there was no response at all.

Was it sleeping somewhere?

Or was it because Groudon and Kyogre didn't really fight, so it didn't appear?

Had it already obtained the rainbow meteorite's power, so its desire for the rainbow meteorite wasn't that high anymore?

"Steven, Wallace, tell me again in detail about what happened when you encountered Rayquaza." Johan said.

Hearing this, Steven and Wallace exchanged glances, then recounted everything that happened that day from beginning to end, including what Rayquaza had said.

"Sky Pillar?"

After hearing their account, Johan felt he had grasped the key point.

Like in "Pokémon Omega Ruby/Alpha Sapphire," would an inheritor need to go to Sky Pillar to gain Rayquaza's recognition before it would help?

"Tomorrow then. Tomorrow we'll go to Sky Pillar."

Johan felt it was necessary to take a look.

As for the inheritor...

If worst came to worst, he'd have other Pokémon help solve the meteorite problem, like... Deoxys.

It just might not be as easy as with Rayquaza.

"Alright."

Steven and Wallace naturally wouldn't refuse this.

If they could truly get Rayquaza's help to solve the meteorite problem, then they wouldn't need to use the "Dimensional Transporter" plan.

Too much life energy was needed...

However.

The League would also prepare for both possibilities, and the "Dimensional Transporter" plan was still being prepared.

It was just that Devon was currently trying to collect "life energy" through conventional means, and wouldn't forcibly take life energy from other Pokémon or humans unless absolutely necessary.

"Glacia, I'm also very tired..."

Johan, who had been preparing to rest, was stopped by Glacia who had rushed to the temporary operations command.

Glacia's face also showed fatigue.

Although she hadn't gone to the front lines to fight Kyogre or Groudon, as the overall commander of this plan and operation, stationed at Hoenn League headquarters, her pressure was no less than Steven and the others.

Moreover, she needed to pay attention to even more things.

Disaster relief, personnel evacuation and support arrangements during disasters, as well as the upcoming meteorite crisis—all of these left Glacia physically and mentally exhausted.

In Glacia's view, having a vigorous battle would be much easier than this.

But there was no choice.

The Hoenn League needed her...

However, Glacia had already decided.

Whether it was Teacher Johan or Steven, after this matter was completely resolved, she would definitely push someone to become Champion and share the burden!

Otherwise, she would resign and quit!

"Sidney and Phoebe have returned with their teams." Glacia removed the white gloves from her hands, let down her pinned-up hair, and said with a long sigh.

"Oh?"

Johan became interested, sitting across from Glacia and asking:

"What's the situation?"

Glacia's expression was heavy as she nodded:

"There were indeed traces of Team Magma and Team Aqua, and we successfully captured some important members of both teams, including administrators."

This was quite a significant "achievement."

But Johan also heard the implication in her words.

"So Maxie and Archie escaped?"

"Yes."

They really could run...

In the manga, these two guys seemed to have escaped as well, but later under Sird's plan, Archie ultimately defeated Maxie, survived, and became the "Armored Man."

"They also found this."

Glacia carefully took out two palm-sized fragments and placed them on the table.

"This is..."

Seeing the red and blue fragments, Johan's pupils contracted slightly.

"Red Orb and Blue Orb?"

"More precisely, fragments."

These two precious orbs that contained Groudon and Kyogre's energy and could even control and command the two super-ancient legendary Pokémon to some extent had actually shattered?

But thinking about it...

Rayquaza's Green Orb seemed to have shattered long ago, and he had even obtained a piece before, which he gave to Dragonite.

That was why Dragonite could touch some of Rayquaza's "speed."

"According to our people's analysis, the reason Groudon and Kyogre were able to undergo Primal Reversion... should be significantly related to the shattering of these two orbs." Glacia added.

Probably...

Johan wasn't entirely certain about this either.

Glacia looked at him deeply, pursed her lips, then pushed the two orb fragments toward him.

"Hm?"

"You keep them."

"Is that appropriate?"

Such precious items.

Although they were shattered, but... judging from Rayquaza's shattered Green Orb fragment, possessing these fragments might even allow some contact with the corresponding super-ancient legendary Pokémon.

Moreover...

Dragonite could gain some power from Rayquaza through the Green Orb fragment, so these Red Orb and Blue Orb fragments might...

That was equivalent to Precipice Blades and Origin Pulse!

And these two fragments were much larger than the Green Orb fragment Johan had obtained.

Glacia looked somewhat tired and waved her hand: "In all of Hoenn, there's probably nowhere safer than keeping them with you."

"If you give them to me..." Johan's gaze fell on the two fragments. "Ahem, they might completely disappear in a while..."

Look here.

He was just worrying about what to use as a "substitute" after Larvitar evolved into Tyranitar and crunched down the Earth Plate fragment in one bite. This Red Orb fragment from Groudon was quite suitable.

"Handle them as you see fit."

Glacia added: "Anyway, if something happens later... you'll be the one cleaning up."

Johan: "..."

He immediately felt these two orb fragments were a bit hot to handle.

But thinking carefully...

It seemed like even if he didn't take these two fragments, if something happened, he wouldn't avoid helping out.

"Alright then."

Johan "reluctantly" accepted the two orb fragments.

The Red Orb fragment could be given to Tyranitar to try.

As for the Blue Orb fragment... it wasn't quite suitable for Coach Bear.

But what if he captured a good Water-type Pokémon in the future?

"Oh right, there's also that matter..."

Glacia covered her mouth and yawned lightly: "I helped you investigate."

She took out a file.

It contained personal information about Team Aqua's Shelly.

"Probably because she was 'undercover' outside, this person hasn't done anything too outrageous. At most... she's deceived some innocent young men."

As she spoke, Glacia's gaze toward Johan became somewhat strange.

"That's fine then."

If he wanted to keep Shelly to help him work, it would be best if she didn't have any difficult-to-accept criminal record. Even if she had made great contributions this time, Johan would have a hurdle in his heart he couldn't cross.

Of course.

How Shelly chose to proceed would ultimately be her own choice.

"Finally home."

Upon returning home, Johan immediately collapsed on the sofa, not wanting to move at all.

Too exhausting.

Not just commanding battles, but performing Mega Evolution twice in one day, including Mega Evolution combined with Terastallization, and Mega Evolution combined with Z-Moves—all quite tiring.

He had also infused large amounts of aura into Coach Bear and Armarouge.

"Vii?"

Victini appeared, rotating its small hands to indicate to Johan...

Want another boost?

"No, no, no, enough, enough."

Johan quickly stopped the little one.

What he was tired of now wasn't his body, but his spirit. Although Victini's infinite energy was amazing, it couldn't help with mental fatigue.

"Ahem."

He sat up, took out Poké Balls and threw them out, summoning all the little ones.

"TYRA?"

Tyranitar stood in the room, yawned, rubbed its eyes twice, then looked at Johan in a daze.

Huh? Why did you get smaller?

Johan's mouth twitched.

"I didn't get smaller, you evolved, Tyranitar. Old Ty."

Evolved?

Tyranitar was also stunned, then realized.

Right! I evolved!

"TYRA!!"

Tyranitar, just remembering this fact, clenched its fists and roared with its head raised.

Crack!

In its excitement, as soon as it raised its head, the ceiling light directly exploded, fragments falling everywhere, and the room immediately became pitch black.

Johan: "..."

Clang!

Ceruledge drew its blade, ghostly blue flames rising from its sword, illuminating the entire living room and the little ones gathered around... in an eerie manner.

Especially Tyranitar's ferocious appearance and fierce face...

"Rotom, quickly start the backup lights!" Johan hurriedly called.

"Understood, Rotom!"

The living room was bright again. Johan breathed a sigh of relief, then turned to see Gengar had somehow appeared behind him, pulling at its eyes and sticking out its tongue, looking ready to scare him.

If Rotom had turned on the lights a bit later, Gengar might have delivered a Lick combo.

"Ka-kaah~"

Gengar laughed sheepishly, tilted its head, and started whistling nonchalantly.

"TYRA..."

Tyranitar realized its mistake, scratching its head with an embarrassed, silly expression.

Johan sighed and didn't blame it.

Having just evolved, some inadaptation was normal, especially since Tyranitar had the rare direct two-stage evolution to its final form.

However, Johan had already thought of and even arranged a place and "job" for Tyranitar to better and faster adapt to its post-evolution power.

It was precisely the cooled lava island that Groudon had left behind.

Since Groudon was so large, it could only roughly help Johan tidy up the basics. The island's subsequent series of modifications, repairs, planting, etc., all needed to be handled by himself.

So the entire ground soil transformation of the small island would be left to Tyranitar.

"Oh right." Johan felt around his pocket and took out the Red Orb and Blue Orb fragments.

"TYRA?"

"Ka-kaah?"

"Oowoo?"

The little ones saw these two fragments and seemed to sense the power of Groudon and Kyogre within them, immediately gathering around.

Especially Tyranitar, which immediately focused on the Red Orb fragment.

"You..."

Johan's original intention was to give the Red Orb fragment to Tyranitar, but recalling the scene of it crashing the ceiling light earlier, his heart couldn't help but flutter.

So after much consideration, he still instructed: "Without my permission, don't randomly use or practice moves at home, okay?"

"TYRA!"

Tyranitar pounded its chest with a "thump thump" sound, showing an expression of "don't you trust me to handle things?"

When it was Larvitar, Johan indeed didn't need to worry much.

If he let Tyranitar adapt to its current body state for a month or two, he probably wouldn't worry either.

But now...

He was afraid that if Tyranitar rolled over in its sleep at night, the second floor would completely collapse.

Actually, collapsing would be the least of it. What he feared most was suddenly having a spike shoot up from underground in the middle of the night, sending him flying to the sky.

But fear aside, he still had to give it...

Johan finally solemnly handed the Red Orb fragment to Tyranitar.

Then he saw...

"TYRA!"

Tyranitar joyfully received the fragment and brought it to its mouth.

Crunch—

That incredibly hard Red Orb fragment was like... like a red apple, with Tyranitar forcibly biting off a piece!

This made Johan's heart race wildly.

"TYRA~"

Wow, so hard, but the taste is quite good~

Fortunately...

Tyranitar didn't swallow this fragment whole like it had with the Earth Plate fragment.

Tyranitar's bite wasn't as exaggerated as expected.

Thinking about it, when it had swallowed the Earth Plate fragment in one bite, it was also because it had just evolved and borrowed the power of evolution.

Moreover, the massive energy of the Earth Plate fragment meant Tyranitar couldn't instantly digest it.

It would probably take quite some time before it could completely transform the absorbed plate power into its own ability.

However...

After Larvitar evolved into Tyranitar, its type changed from the original Ground and Rock types to Rock and Dark types.

But during the previous exchange with Groudon, Johan felt...

It seemed his Tyranitar hadn't lost the same-type attack bonus when using Ground-type moves.

Because of the remaining energy from the Earth Plate fragment?

Or...

Did Tyranitar have a hidden Ground type?

A three-type Pokémon?

"Sni?"

Snivy had somehow climbed onto Tyranitar's shoulder and was staring at the Blue Orb fragment in Johan's hand, lost in thought.

Hm?

Noticing Snivy's gaze, Johan was also stunned.

"You're interested?"

"Sni! (#`皿)"

Just a little curious! Even if you don't give it to me, I won't ask for it!

Johan couldn't help but laugh.

"Alright, I'll give it to you."

With that, he stuffed the Blue Orb fragment into Snivy's arms.

He had asked Coach Bear anyway, and it wasn't very interested.

And among his other Pokémon, there really weren't many that could use it.

Before capturing a new Water-type Pokémon, he might as well let Snivy play with it.

Water-type energy probably wouldn't have any negative effects on the Grass-type Snivy anyway.

"Sni!"

You're the one who gave it to me!

Snivy happily put away the Blue Orb fragment.

During this incident, Snivy didn't have the opportunity or ability to intervene, but that didn't mean it wasn't paying attention to the events.

It had seen Kyogre's power.

It was just that the Water-type Kyogre obviously wouldn't help the Grass-type Snivy the way Groudon helped Tyranitar.

What Snivy was interested in was Kyogre's use of energy.

Why could others shoot five or six light beams with one move, but it couldn't?

Origin Pulse?

Then it would reluctantly study it!

Snivy's learning library +1

He patted the little one's head.

With Larvitar evolving into Tyranitar and even competing with Groudon for weather control, it obviously had no chance of participating in any "Baby Cup" anymore.

Johan could only place his "hopes" on Snivy.

He just didn't understand why Snivy hadn't evolved yet.

After this Hoenn matter was completely settled, he'd investigate more deeply.

"Alright."

Johan stretched.

"Get some rest early. If nothing unexpected happens, tomorrow we'll need to go to Sky Pillar, and we might get to see the Pokémon world's biggest green caterpillar."

Green caterpillar?

"Sni~(▼皿▼)"

Snivy clenched its fists, indicating that a mere green caterpillar wasn't worth being serious about.

I'll beat it up for you to see tomorrow!
