# 660: Come, Rayquaza, Tell Me How Many You Want to Fight (Two-in-One Chapter)

The next day.

On Devon Corporation's private jet, heading to Sky Pillar on Glass Island.

Speaking of which, Johan had been coveting this kind of private jet for quite some time, but considering his financial situation, this kind of thing was just something to covet - at worst he could call Steven, and Steven surely wouldn't mind giving him a ride or pickup service.

Having students and not "freeloading" off them - what was the point of being a teacher?

"Bangi! ψ(｀∇´)ψ"

Here I go!

Tyranitar sat on the plane's open space, grabbing a handful of diamonds of various sizes and stuffing them in its mouth, soon producing crisp "crunch crunch" sounds.

If these diamonds were like candy to Larvitar before, then now these diamonds were probably just... rice to Tyranitar.

The way it was wolfing down food, not to mention Johan, even Wallace sitting nearby was watching with trembling heart.

"No wonder Teacher Johan's Tyranitar could compete with Groudon for weather control right after evolution..."

Wallace sincerely sighed.

"The appetite is also quite exaggerated. Teacher Johan really spares no effort in raising Pokémon."

"Haha." Johan, holding a book, gave a bitter smile.

"It's not just about food."

Steven also spoke up.

"There are plenty of wealthy people in the Pokémon world. Even if everyone imitated Teacher's methods of raising Pokémon, how many could actually raise a Tyranitar to Teacher's level?"

Wallace nodded thoughtfully.

That was true.

Teacher Johan's Tyranitar...

Yesterday Wallace witnessed its "friendly" relationship with Groudon, even learning moves from Groudon.

Having learned that move and calling it "little Groudon" wouldn't be excessive.

And how many "little Groudons" could there be in the Pokémon world?

Regarding Steven and Wallace's praise, Tyranitar turned a deaf ear, just focused on eating.

After finishing the diamonds, it took out energy cubes and branches from the World Tree.

Others eat meat without garlic, losing half the flavor.

It eats diamonds without tree branches, losing thirty percent of the taste.

"Bangi~(￣~￣)"

Don't worry, I'll definitely eat you up without wasting a bit!

After Larvitar evolved into Tyranitar, its attributes changed - it became Evil and Rock type, and its original quadruple weakness to Water and Grass types became double weakness.

However, it didn't lose its quadruple weakness entirely - Fighting type became its "fatal" weakness.

But Tyranitar seemed to already have some "experience" with this, finding Urshifu every day for guidance and training to strengthen its resistance.

In this aspect, Tyranitar was quite clever.

"Sni~"

Snivy lay against the plane window, gazing at the sea of clouds below, eyes twinkling.

This was its first time on a plane, and it still felt quite novel - very different from riding Dragonite.

Johan, leaning back in his chair with his head against the headrest, was actually thinking about a question.

Sky Pillar, inheritor, Rayquaza - when these elements combined, would the Draconid Zinnia appear?

In "Pokémon Omega Ruby/Alpha Sapphire," Zinnia was the key to breaking the deadlock.

Johan's deepest impression of Zinnia was her somewhat bizarre Pokémon team.

Five dragons, plus a Whismur named "Aster."

Actually, "Aster" had its own story - she was also a Draconid, an inheritor, and more precisely, she was the true inheritor. Zinnia took over the inheritor position after her unfortunate death.

In fact, Aster had already gained Rayquaza's recognition, while Zinnia still needed to work for it.

However, considering that the "Rayquaza Capture Plan" hadn't been implemented, there probably wouldn't be the sisters Aster and Zinnia.

"But Rayquaza's situation..."

Johan closed his eyes, gently stroking the belly of Dragonite napping beside him, trying to contact Rayquaza through it and aura again, still to no avail.

"Still the same." Johan slowly opened his eyes and sighed softly.

Setting aside their relationship, Rayquaza was essentially a very violent and proud legendary Pokémon. Compared to the black and white dragons and Xerneas, it actually wasn't easy to communicate with.

It could even be said to be difficult to communicate with.

Rayquaza was naturally proud and looked down on everything.

And it indeed had such ability.

"If we need to fight..." Johan silently calculated Rayquaza's battle power.

Compared to other legendary Pokémon... Groudon and Kyogre weren't worth mentioning - two of them together weren't enough for Rayquaza to fight.

Just comparing it to the Sinnoh space-time trio, Palkia and Dialga together facing Giratina would have difficulty determining a winner, let alone one suppressing the other two.

The Unova Tao trio was even more so.

What truly demonstrated Rayquaza's power was its legendary battle that made it famous.

In the movie "Hoopa and the Clash of Ages," a black Rayquaza dominated one against seven, fighting seven legendary Pokémon alone - a feat that was truly awe-inspiring.

Although Johan wasn't sure if the Rayquaza he knew was the same black Rayquaza from the movie, its power was definitely not to be underestimated.

"If worst comes to worst..."

Johan rubbed his temples.

With Giratina not "home," this was really giving him a headache.

Johan couldn't help but complain.

"Giratina? More like Hoopa."

In a desolate desert area on Glass Island, stood a towering spire reaching into the clouds, with strange patterns carved on it that looked quite magnificent.

"This is Sky Pillar?"

Standing at the base of the tower and looking up, Johan could only see patches of white clouds, completely unable to see the top.

"I didn't know Sky Pillar was actually on Glass Island?" Steven was somewhat surprised and curious.

"Usually, this area is filled with high-level wild Pokémon with strong territorial instincts. Without guidance from the 'People of Sootopolis,' it's hard to approach." Wallace explained.

It was also because Kyogre had caused such a disturbance that the wild Pokémon here had all hidden, otherwise approaching would still be troublesome without Wallace's guidance.

Of course, with Johan and Steven's strength, if they really wanted to fight their way through, there weren't many wild Pokémon that could stop them.

"The 'Draconid people' a thousand years ago could build such a tower - it seems they were quite powerful back then." Johan said.

Wallace nodded, "Indeed. Back then, we 'People of Sootopolis' could only be considered vassals of the 'Draconid people.'"

Theoretically, the "People of Sootopolis" only had the qualification to guard Sky Pillar, but not the qualification to climb it. Only chosen "Draconid people" could ascend.

"There might be stones I haven't seen here..." Steven muttered quietly.

Hm?

Johan and Wallace looked at him.

Steven came to his senses and smiled: "Then let's go up."

"Fly up?" Johan craned his neck.

But Wallace said: "Can't fly."

"According to ancient texts I've read, the cloud layer above Sky Pillar belongs to Rayquaza's domain. Flying up rashly would be considered an enemy and would anger it."

Not just ordinary people, even "Draconid people" weren't allowed to fly up before gaining Rayquaza's recognition.

"Tsk."

Johan clicked his tongue.

Such a tall tower, who knew how many floors it had.

Besides being tall, the "Draconid people" had also set up many mechanisms inside Sky Pillar when building it, essentially blocking most people from going up. Only "Draconid people" knew how to deal with these mechanisms.

Moreover.

Sky Pillar housed many Pokémon, such as...

A Claydol blocked Johan and the others' path.

Bang! Bang!

Huge fists collided, echoing dully in the small space.

"Kang!"

Metagross flew out from Steven's waist, faster than Tyranitar, punching the Claydol into the wall with one strike, making it unable to battle!

"Bangi?"

Tyranitar, which had been clenching its fist excitedly, looked confused.

"Uh..." Steven rubbed his nose with slight embarrassment: "Sorry, force of habit..."

He'd encountered guardian Pokémon in ruins so many times while digging for stones that every time he met this kind of Pokémon guarding ruins, Metagross would punch them away.

Cough, a bit too skilled.

Johan patted Tyranitar, standing inside Sky Pillar's base and looking up.

What he could see was just ancient walls covered with patterns and spiral staircases going up, with no end in sight.

He opened his mouth.

"Cynthia would be ecstatic if she saw this place."

But walking up step by step?

Even without mentioning attacks and mechanisms, it would take a whole day just to walk.

"Dragonite." Johan called softly.

"Wu?"

The Poké Ball opened, red light forming into Dragonite as it emerged on its own.

Johan climbed onto its back and grabbed the protective gear.

"Steven, can't fly." Wallace quickly said.

"Rules are dead, people are alive. We'll stick to the stairs and fly." Johan said.

Really walk up?

They weren't "Draconid people," so they didn't need to maintain any pilgrimage mentality. Getting the gist was enough.

Besides, this time they'd come seeking Rayquaza's help, but that didn't mean they had to rely entirely on Rayquaza.

Worst case scenario...

Two Deoxys plus Mewtwo - he didn't believe they couldn't handle that meteorite.

If Rayquaza was willing to help, that was great - give it the honor it deserved. If it didn't want to help... then help it be honored!

Wallace and Steven exchanged glances.

Considering the urgent meteorite crisis, acting expeditiously seemed understandable.

So they both got on Metagross's back and followed Dragonite, sticking to the stairs as they flew toward the upper levels of Sky Pillar.

Along the way, they encountered some Pokémon like Claydol, but clearly, these Pokémon couldn't stop Johan and the others.

In many cases, Johan's Snivy could handle most of the trouble.

"Sni!(▼皿▼)"

Snivy stood on Dragonite's head, its vines lashing out to smack a Baltoy flying.

It had to be said, most of the Pokémon in Sky Pillar were Ground and Rock types, and none could withstand a few hits from Snivy.

Watching this, Wallace and Steven following behind couldn't help but sigh.

Teacher Johan really had leading-edge, unique insights into raising "babies."

"What floor is this?" Johan looked back.

"Forty-eight." Steven answered.

Forty-eight...

Looking at this pace, the fiftieth floor should be Sky Pillar's top level.

Leaning on Dragonite's back and looking down...

Pretty scary.

Johan remembered that in the game "Pokémon Omega Ruby/Alpha Sapphire," Sky Pillar had a level 70 Rayquaza, and after capturing it, you'd encounter a level 80 Deoxys.

So the reason Rayquaza couldn't beat Deoxys was found - insufficient level!

Hm?

Just as Johan and the others were about to reach the forty-ninth floor, they vaguely heard some strange sounds.

"Sounds like... someone?" Steven also noticed this.

Someone?

On the forty-ninth floor?

But how could there be any trace of human activity or passage along the way?

Moreover.

Who would come to Sky Pillar at this time?

Johan and Steven both looked at Wallace, the "guardian" of Sky Pillar.

Noticing their gazes, Wallace's eye twitched as he spread his hands: "I don't know."

"Let's take a look."

Johan ultimately took the lead, flying to the forty-ninth floor.

Then he saw...

A tent made of unknown hide, clearly with a somewhat outdated style, set up in the middle of the forty-ninth floor, with things like a campfire and cooking utensils in front of it.

Most importantly.

Johan saw a figure climbing the stairs from the forty-ninth to fiftieth floor in the corner of the stairwell.

All he could make out was long black hair, and under a wide cloak seemed to be tight clothing. The overall outfit was somewhat reminiscent of ancient people.

Very similar to the Zinnia in Johan's impression.

A Draconid?

"Someone's living here?" Steven and Wallace, who came up next, also noticed the tent and the obvious signs of life.

Wallace looked somewhat dazed.

As a guardian of Sky Pillar, someone was actually living on the forty-ninth floor of Sky Pillar?

And he had no idea at all!

"No, judging by the traces, they've only been living here for a few days." Steven shook his head.

A few days?

Johan frowned slightly.

A strange sense of danger suddenly rose in his heart, and he immediately shouted:

"Be careful!"

At the same time, a sound wave came from the corner of the stairwell from the forty-ninth to fiftieth floor, with ripples of sound waves spreading.

"Wu!"

Dragonite folded its wings, then quickly spread them again, sending two bright white air blades that split the incoming sound waves, making them dissipate.

"Oh?"

A puzzled light exclamation came from the corner.

Then the owner of the voice appeared before Johan and the others - indeed the person Johan had seen, a girl about seventeen or eighteen years old.

Zinnia?

No.

This was Aster?

Beside her was a Noivern, and the earlier attack obviously came from it.

"Humans?" Aster was somewhat surprised.

She had just gone up when Noivern heard movement below and quickly returned.

She thought it might be wild Pokémon from below coming up to the forty-ninth floor again, but she hadn't expected it to be several humans.

And looking at them... they seemed quite capable.

Although her Noivern's attack wasn't at full power, it definitely shouldn't have been so easily deflected.

But soon Aster frowned again.

Besides "Draconid people," no one else should appear here.

And these people, especially Wallace - when she noticed the special markings on Wallace, she understood.

"You're the 'guardian'?" Aster suddenly spoke.

Wallace jumped down from Metagross, placed his right hand on his chest, and made a noble bow: "I am Wallace."

Then he introduced the similarly dismounted Johan and Steven.

"These two are Devon Corporation's Daigo Stone and... 'Pokémon Whisperer' Teacher Johan."

When introducing Steven, it was simple, but when introducing Johan, Wallace racked his brains before finally coming up with "Pokémon Whisperer."

Hearing this, Aster showed no particular reaction, but Johan's mouth twitched.

What the hell is a "Pokémon Whisperer"?

Aster nodded and, like Wallace, placed her right hand on her chest and bowed slightly: "Draconid people, this generation's inheritor, Aster."

Sure enough, it was Aster!

Johan glanced at her, then at Steven...

What a fateful connection.

In the manga, Aster gained Rayquaza's recognition and officially became the inheritor, but coincidentally... the Alliance's "Rayquaza Capture Plan" was implemented.

Led by the Alliance, funded by the Belritz family, with technical assistance from Devon Corporation and Greater Mauville Holdings, Devon's development of the weapon "Flower" using "∞ Energy" and the ultimate weapon was the most crucial part of the plan.

"Flower" could weaken opponents using ∞ energy, including Rayquaza.

But during that operation, Aster used Mega bracelets and large quantities of Key Stones to help Rayquaza achieve Mega Evolution and attempt to break through.

But ultimately the breakout failed, Rayquaza was captured, and Aster died as a result.

That's how Zinnia's story came about later.

After introducing herself, Aster frowned and said:

"Even if you're the 'guardian,' you shouldn't come here, let alone..."

But before she could finish, she shook her head again.

"Forget it. You probably came here because of Kyogre and Groudon's awakening. Don't worry, I'll gain the 'Dragon Lord's' recognition and solve this crisis."

With that, she turned her cloak and headed toward the fiftieth floor again.

She also reminded them:

"You should leave quickly. The 'Dragon Lord's' majesty cannot be violated. Appearing rashly before the 'Dragon Lord' might provoke its wrath."

Having said that, she quickly climbed the stairs.

Kyogre and Groudon's rampage would cause more destruction to the Hoenn continent the longer it continued. She had to gain the "Dragon Lord's" recognition as soon as possible.

She'd already been here for several days.

Today was the final test!

Aster unconsciously touched the scroll in her pocket.

I will definitely succeed!

For Hoenn, for... everyone!

Watching Aster disappear again, Wallace opened his mouth, wanting to say... those two gods had already been taken down by Teacher Johan.

But unfortunately, Aster had already run up.

"This is much gentler than Zinnia..." Johan muttered quietly.

The inheritor Zinnia who inherited her will was like a villain, especially hostile to Devon Corporation people, often striking with deadly force.

But the current Aster was obviously much better in character.

Perhaps it was also because she hadn't experienced the death of her best friend...

"Teacher, should we..." Steven looked at the entrance to the fiftieth floor and asked.

"Go."

Johan lightly patted Dragonite's arm and walked toward the stairs.

Our Snivy said yesterday it wanted to beat up the "green caterpillar," so shouldn't we give it a chance?

Also...

He'd been unable to contact Rayquaza all this time because it was testing the "inheritor"?

Sky Pillar, top floor.

At the top floor in the clouds, one could see the Sky Pillar platform surrounded by endless sea of clouds, with a faint sense of pressure completely enveloping this area.

Aster pulled her cloak tighter, exposing her mouth to breathe out white mist.

The air was too thin near the ozone layer.

If not for her special constitution, just standing on Sky Pillar's top floor would make her dizzy from oxygen deprivation.

Rumble rumble—

With Aster's appearance, the sea of clouds around Sky Pillar's top floor began to churn, and ozone concentration skyrocketed.

Even though this was already Aster's several visits, she still unconsciously showed nervousness, her face paling.

Whether from cold, thin air, or... the great being about to appear in the clouds!

"Dragon Lord!" Aster placed her right hand on her chest and bowed respectfully, awaiting the "Dragon Lord's" descent.

"Wu?"

Behind her, sounds suddenly came.

Aster's heart jumped.

How did those people still come up?

She'd clearly warned them that this would easily anger the great "Dragon Lord." If her test failed because of their appearance, then this crisis in Hoenn...

She should have knocked them out earlier... Aster regretted a bit.

Although those people didn't seem weak, she'd seen Snivy.

Someone who still kept initial form Pokémon couldn't be that strong, right?

Rumble rumble—

The sea of clouds churned again.

"Green caterpillar's coming out. Get ready." Johan said to Snivy with some teasing.

"Sni!(#皿)"

Just a green caterpillar!

But soon Snivy reacted.

Wait.

How could a green caterpillar live in this kind of place?

In the sea of clouds, green light flickered, and an incredibly huge figure appeared in the clouds, accompanied by howling winds and roaring air currents.

Bang!!

The clouds suddenly dispersed.

A green dragon with cold golden eyes appeared before Aster and Johan's group!

The super-ancient legendary Pokémon, Sky High Pokémon, Rayquaza!

"Sni, sni?(∑(O_O;))"

You call this a green caterpillar?

But remembering yesterday's boasting, Snivy gritted its teeth, jumped down from Dragonite's head, and walked toward Rayquaza with a "the wind is howling and the Yi River is cold" attitude, pursing its lips.

Even if I die, I have to do what I bragged about!

Seeing this, Johan quickly grabbed the little one and held it in his arms, struggling as its strength weakened.

"Alright, alright, I was just joking with you."

"Sni!(╰╮o(￣皿￣///)"

Aster didn't pay attention to the changes behind her, only focused on passing the test before the "Dragon Lord" truly got angry!

She quickly said: "Great 'Dragon Lord,' I've come for the final inheritor test!"

With that, she gripped the scroll in her pocket tightly.

Rayquaza looked down at Aster...

This was already the third day.

Since the rainbow meteorite appeared and it gained power from the rainbow meteorite, this "Draconid" girl had come to Sky Pillar, saying she wanted to gain its recognition.

As the deity worshipped by the "Draconid people," Rayquaza had such an understanding with the "Draconid people."

So it accepted the girl's test request.

Honestly.

Rayquaza already had some recognition of Aster, otherwise the so-called test wouldn't have lasted until this third day.

But...

That man appeared.

Rayquaza's gaze briefly stopped on Johan.

This was a choice.

Fragrant, delicious food, or a gentle, lovely girl...

So difficult.

[You.]

Rayquaza's voice rang out.

[Defeat him!]

Its gaze fell on Johan.

Defeat him?

Aster turned around, looking at Johan with considerable surprise.

She hadn't expected this final test to be defeating this suddenly appearing person?

Was the "Dragon Lord" testing my strength?

Aster's expression became serious.

Although she wasn't someone who particularly enjoyed battle, if it was the "Dragon Lord's" request...

"Sorry..." Aster pursed her lips and said apologetically to Johan: "For Hoenn, for ending Groudon and Kyogre's conflict..."

But Johan's behavior far exceeded Aster's understanding.

"Crazy!"

Johan waved his hand quite irritably, holding Snivy as he turned toward Sky Pillar's lower levels.

"I was wondering why you wouldn't respond when I tried to contact you. Turns out you were just bored. If you're fine, that's good. I'm leaving."

Steven and Wallace looked at Rayquaza, then at Johan, swallowing hard.

Teacher Johan was...

They were in this situation and he still acted like this?

Buzz—

The surrounding sea of clouds suddenly churned, and the path back to the forty-ninth floor was blocked by cloud mist.

Seeing this, Johan stopped, raised an eyebrow, and turned back to look at Rayquaza past Aster.

He suddenly broke into a big grin, a Gengar-style smile.

"Fine. Let's fight if you want to fight, Rayquaza."

"Wu—"

"Roar—"

Two figures rapidly approached from Sky Pillar's lower levels, reaching Sky Pillar's top floor in just a few breaths.

Reshiram!

Zekrom!

From Johan's shadow, black mist churned as Darkrai and Gengar also floated out.

Under the strong wind, Johan's clothes fluttered as he stared directly at Rayquaza and said:

"Tell me, how many do you want to fight? Five? Seven? Nine? You name the number."

Buzz—

Auras familiar yet strange appeared around Johan.

Truth, Ideals, Ice, Time, Space, Antimatter, Life, Psychic...

Faintly, even some outlines belonging to them appeared.

On his chest, Arceus's Millennium Wrist radiated heat, seemingly materializing these "representatives."

Aster stared wide-eyed with her mouth agape, blankly looking at Johan.

This, he, Dragon Lord...

Rayquaza's expression also froze.

I was joking, do you believe it or not?

# 661: Teacher Johan, And You Still Say You're Ordinary? (Two-in-One Chapter)

To be honest.

If Johan hadn't quite gotten a handle on Rayquaza's temperament yet, he wouldn't have needed to climb up Sky Pillar step by step with Steven and Wallace - he would have flown straight up long ago.

The main reason was that he couldn't contact Rayquaza, and this guy had the potential to turn hostile without warning.

After all, having gained extremely powerful Mega Evolution, its strength had improved tremendously.

On the other hand, he was also somewhat worried that Rayquaza might have encountered some problems.

For example, when Deoxys descended back then, it was driven to madness by Team Magma. If Team Magma and Team Aqua were well-prepared, it wasn't impossible for them to "control" Rayquaza in advance.

But now it seemed...

This guy was purely busy with "inheritor" testing, plus Groudon and Kyogre hadn't really fought, so it hadn't appeared.

As for Rayquaza...

It was actually quite conflicted.

The "inheritor" was essentially an agreement it had reached with the "Draconid people" who had worshipped it for so long.

Overall, it was quite satisfied with Aster.

She was respectful enough toward it, her strength wasn't bad, and most importantly, she possessed a special constitution that naturally made Dragon-type Pokémon feel close to her, and could even further stimulate Dragon-type Pokémon's potential to some extent.

Of course, such stimulation and influence was negligible for Rayquaza, but it was still a good choice, wasn't it?

But after Johan appeared, it became somewhat conflicted.

After all, this was a human who had once helped it and had befriended it first.

If Rayquaza's relationship with Aster was that of superior and subordinate, then Rayquaza's relationship with Johan could be considered equal.

Therefore, it had the idea of having Johan and Aster battle, then deciding whom to choose.

It's just...

[Only one day has passed, yet your influence...]

While speaking, it glanced at Reshiram and Zekrom beside Johan, sensing those auras that hadn't completely dissipated, and immediately changed its tune.

[Your strength impresses me.]

One day?

Johan blinked, communicating with Rayquaza through aura.

"Hasn't it been a long time already?"

It had been several months since he last saw Rayquaza, right?

[It was just one day.]

Rayquaza was quite certain about this.

[I just took a nap, one nap equals one day.]

Johan: "..."

He opened his mouth.

He was starting to understand Rayquaza's concept of time.

This guy lived in the ozone layer and even beyond the planet, and didn't have any concept of "days" based on sunrise and sunset, so it used "sleeping" as its measurement.

One sleep = one day, no matter how long that sleep was, it was one day.

Moreover, for Rayquaza's incredibly long lifespan, having a concept of "days" was already quite good.

Because calculating this way, Rayquaza's own age assessment... might be about the same as Johan's as a human.

"Alright, you have the final say." Johan didn't want to argue with it about this.

Rayquaza proudly raised its head.

"So, are we fighting or not?" Johan asked, bringing the topic back.

At the same time, he muttered:

"I originally wanted to bring you some food since we hadn't seen each other in a while."

With that, he took out pre-prepared energy cubes, looking like he was shaking his head and sighing.

Rayquaza's proud head lowered again, looking directly at Johan and the black and white dragons, Darkrai and others beside him.

[I was just joking earlier.]

Everyone's friends here - no need to draw swords and fight.

As Arceus's messenger and contractor of the black and white dragons... one should take a long-term view and broaden one's perspective.

This face, even if not given to Arceus, should be given to the food...

It wasn't like Groudon and Kyogre, those two brainless ones.

Hearing this, Johan smiled.

That was fine. Since it was only "one day" for Rayquaza, it hadn't forgotten their friendly relationship.

"There's something I'd like to ask your help with." He said, then glanced at the dumbstruck Aster beside him and added: "How about you finish the test first?"

Anyway, the meteorite's descent was still some time away - at least seven or eight days, at most half a month. There was no rush.

[Don't you want to try?]

Rayquaza asked back.

Johan chuckled softly.

Rayquaza testing the "inheritor"?

When it came to him, it would be him testing Rayquaza.

"Who is this...?"

At this moment, Aster finally snapped back to reality, looking at the handsome black-haired young man who was chatting and laughing with the supreme "Dragon Lord" in her eyes, her heart full of confusion.

Fortunately, Wallace beside her provided the answer.

After all, as the "People of Sootopolis," they had been on good terms with the "Draconid people" for a thousand years. Even though there wasn't much contact now, the old friendship remained.

So Wallace introduced:

"Teacher Johan, the one who calmed the Hoenn twin gods Groudon and Kyogre, the one who resolved the space-time dragon confrontation in Alamos Town, the one recognized by the truth and ideals black and white dragons, Arceus's appointed messenger, Mewtwo's bonded partner, Master Trainer recognized by Professor Oak, fighting master, Pokémon breeder, trainer, Youth World Championship winner..."

Aren't you thirsty?

Listening to Wallace recite like a catalog, Johan couldn't help but complain internally.

But for Aster, such a long string of titles... just hearing them was intimidating.

As everyone knows, regardless of what they represent, long titles are intimidating enough.

What's more, Aster understood the meaning of some of these titles.

Finally, Steven couldn't help but add:

"My teacher."

After hearing all this, Aster looked at Johan with completely changed eyes.

They became incredibly respectful, even reverent.

Never mind anything else.

Just being someone who could calm the Hoenn twin gods' battle without borrowing Rayquaza's power was enough to earn her admiration.

The reason she left "Meteor Village" to come to Sky Pillar seeking Rayquaza's recognition was because the clan sensed the seven-colored meteorite's movement and foresaw disaster, sending her here to quickly save Hoenn.

Who would have thought that before she could fully gain the "Dragon Lord's" recognition, Hoenn's crisis was already resolved!

The pressure in Aster's heart immediately lessened several-fold.

Moreover, as ancient survivors isolated from the world, the "Draconid people" also worshipped strength internally, just like Dragon-type Pokémon - strength deserved respect.

Teacher Johan...

Aster silently etched this name firmly in her heart.

While Wallace was introducing Johan, Rayquaza was also discussing with Johan.

"You want me to help you test her?"

Hearing Rayquaza's meaning, Johan was stunned.

Rayquaza nodded.

[The final test is her strength. If you think she's acceptable, then it's her.]

Giving me validation rights, huh? Johan grumbled internally.

But thinking about it...

If he went, perhaps this little girl Aster would pass more easily.

Moreover, Rayquaza rarely made a "request" of him, so directly refusing wouldn't be very nice.

So after thinking for a moment, he nodded:

"Alright."

[Also...]

Rayquaza pointed at the energy cubes in front of it.

[Could there be more of these?]

"Ask Dragonite for them." Johan waved his hand.

Being the same Dragon and Flying types, Dragonite's energy cubes were the most compatible for Rayquaza.

"Draaa?"

Dragonite immediately crossed its arms, looking somewhat warily at Rayquaza.

Rayquaza: "..."

Johan then walked toward Aster, Steven, and Wallace. He looked at Aster and said:

"You heard what Rayquaza meant, right?"

"Yes!"

Aster immediately stood straight, shouting very seriously and loudly.

"No need to be so nervous."

Johan winked at Aster, indicating she should just go through the motions casually.

But Aster seemed to misunderstand Johan's meaning, her cheeks reddening as she pursed her lips and said:

"I'll definitely give it my all!"

With that, she took out a rather classical-looking Poké Ball, black and gold in color. After rotating the gear-like device on top, she threw the Poké Ball.

Hm?

That Poké Ball...

Black light flashed.

What appeared was a fierce and intimidating Dragon-type Pokémon - Salamence!

Johan's attention was drawn to that special ancient Poké Ball, and he momentarily forgot to remind Aster again that "we're just going through the motions."

So Aster took the initiative to attack.

"Salamence, Flamethrower!"

Nearby, Steven and Wallace couldn't hear Rayquaza's words, so they didn't understand what was happening.

"Why are they fighting again?" Wallace nudged Steven with his elbow and asked softly.

"Seems to be for... a test?" Steven wasn't very certain either.

Meanwhile, Rayquaza and Dragonite seemed quite leisurely, each holding energy cubes and putting them in their mouths one by one. If you didn't know better, you'd think they were eating popcorn and watching a movie.

Oh, it wasn't just Rayquaza and Dragonite, but also Reshiram and Zekrom.

And Darkrai and Gengar hiding in another corner.

"Ka-kaah..." (Such a cool place, finally came up here once. I absolutely can't return empty-handed. Any good stuff?)

Darkrai rolled its eyes irritably, "Stop looking. This place is bare except for rocks. What good stuff could there be?"

"Ka-kaah?" (Then what are you doing picking up that rock?)

Gengar half-squinted, looking at Darkrai crouching to the side, lifting a rock and peering underneath.

"I'm just... cough, look! They're fighting!" Darkrai "bang" put down the rock and immediately changed the subject, shouting.

"Ka-kaah?"

Gengar looked toward Johan's side.

Roar!!

Blazing flames formed a fire column that gushed forth, scattered sparks falling everywhere. The red flames reflected on everyone's faces, turning them red.

It had to be said.

Aster did have some skill, otherwise she wouldn't have gained Rayquaza's recognition.

But the current Johan could resist legendary Pokémon to a certain extent for short periods!

Boom!!

The surging flames suddenly exploded, and Tyranitar, looking even more fierce than Salamence, roared out.

Dust began flying in this high altitude space.

"Bangi!!"

Rumble rumble—

Suddenly.

Aster felt the ground beneath her feet begin to shake, and a fire-red rock spike wrapped in lava immediately shot up from the ground!

Neither Aster nor Salamence, nor even Rayquaza, had anticipated such a change.

Especially Rayquaza - the energy cube in its mouth almost came out uncontrolled. It looked somewhat incredulously at Dragonite for confirmation.

Seriously?

"Draaa~"

Dragonite was quite calm, waving its hand downward.

Normal operation, don't worry~

Precipice Blades?!

That flightless fool's signature move?

For some reason, Rayquaza suddenly felt a sense of "crisis" rising in its heart.

Oh no.

That Groudon fool... was also starting to "influence" Johan?

It had Dragonite, so that fool found Tyranitar?

No, no, no - Rayquaza shook its head, leaving Dragonite confused.

[You need to work harder and not be outdone by it!]

"Draaa?"

Dragonite scratched its head.

What was all this about?

Rayquaza vigorously chewed the energy cubes, starting to have some thoughts.

Even that fool was getting smarter...

"Stone Edge."

Johan calmly stated the name of Tyranitar's move.

When the opponent was a Flying-type Pokémon, it was Stone Edge. If it were another type... it might be Precipice Blades.

Move duality, that was.

Boom!!!

Salamence, caught off guard by the attack to its abdomen, let out a pained cry.

Stone Edge?

Whose Stone Edge could shoot that high and still have lava?

"Salamence!"

Seeing this, Aster cried out in alarm.

"Truly worthy of someone recognized by the 'Dragon Lord'..."

Aster took a deep breath, closed her eyes, then quickly opened them. Determination flashed in her bright pupils.

"Salamence—"

She called out loudly.

Buzz—

On Aster's ankle, what appeared to be a special ankle ornament burst with seven-colored light.

"Mega Evolution!!"

"Roar—!!"

Salamence stopped its fall, quickly completing Mega Evolution while wrapped in seven-colored super evolution energy.

At the same time, Aster crossed her hands left and right, forming claws with all ten fingers. Black pupils slowly gained a hint of blood-red as she shouted:

"Dragon Claw!"

"Roar!!"

Mega Salamence roared again, charging toward Tyranitar at extreme speed.

After commanding Salamence, Aster herself actually swept her cloak aside and charged toward Johan.

Holy crap!

No-rules battle!

Although Johan had always secretly complained that Ash, Red, and Team Rocket were suited for no-rules battles, but...

This was his first time witnessing a trainer going straight for another trainer.

Moreover, Rayquaza had said earlier that it barely recognized Aster because of her special constitution.

Not only could she stimulate Dragon-type Pokémon's potential, but she herself... was the same.

Don't be fooled by her thin arms and legs - her muscle definition was quite distinct, full of wild beauty.

The sudden charge caught Johan off guard. He instinctively raised his arm, trying to block Aster's incoming claw.

Bang!!

Solid contact.

Aster's eyes widened.

Although she hadn't used full force, being blocked so easily by Johan just raising his hand?

Hm?

Honestly, Johan hadn't expected Aster's seemingly powerful strike to have so little strength.

Didn't eat?

She couldn't have misunderstood and thought... she was the one who should hold back? Johan thought.

Aster tried again, pushing off the ground with her foot and sweeping like a Kommo-o.

But Johan easily jumped over it.

Earlier was lack of reaction time, but now in this situation... Johan would be sorry to his deep aura power if he didn't use aura.

Under aura, Aster's attacks were completely exposed.

Whether front, side, or back, whether brute force, technique, or speed - nothing worked.

She couldn't touch Johan.

Moreover, Johan could easily command Tyranitar to deal with Mega Salamence while handling Aster.

Wait, wasn't he supposed to let Aster pass the test smoothly?

And Aster was extremely shocked in her heart.

Although Wallace had mentioned earlier that Teacher Johan was a "fighting master," she hadn't expected someone's fighting skills to be this incredible.

Not just fighting skills - his physical abilities were ridiculously exaggerated.

In the clan, she might not be the strongest in wrestling, but because of her special constitution allowing some "feedback" from Pokémon, despite her young age she was incredibly strong. Yet before Teacher Johan, she still seemed like a little chick.

Only Johan felt that Aster was still holding back - no, holding an ocean back.

"That's enough." Johan muttered to himself, immediately conveying his meaning to Tyranitar.

Understanding, when Mega Salamence charged again, Tyranitar raised its hand to block its Dragon Claw while suddenly staggering backward three or four steps, then falling to the ground with a "bang."

"Bangi~!"

Ah! I lose!

Johan: "..."

Mega Salamence: "..."

Aster: "..."

Rayquaza: "..."

Tyranitar lying on the ground even winked at Johan, as if saying "see how realistic my acting is" before finishing.

White dragon Reshiram covered its face with its wing.

I didn't see anything, I didn't see anything.

Johan didn't care whether Tyranitar's acting was realistic or not, immediately distancing himself from Aster and turning to Rayquaza:

"Mm, not bad. It's her."

Rayquaza, holding an energy cube, stopped its claw mid-air, expression dazed. The energy cube uncontrollably fell.

"Draaa~~ (ω)b"

Nearby Steven and Wallace, seeing Johan's gaze, quickly put away their phones that had been recording.

Next time, who dares say Teacher Johan is "ordinary"?

Tyranitar patted its rear and stood up.

Rayquaza looked at Tyranitar, looked at Johan, looked at Aster, then looked at Steven and Wallace, finally... nodding.

[Acceptable.]

"Stop spacing out." Johan said softly.

"Oh, oh."

Aster snapped back to reality, quickly running to Rayquaza and kneeling on one knee, taking out a pre-prepared scroll.

Rayquaza showed a majestic expression, nodding slightly. Strange power lifted the scroll, slowly floating toward it.

Feeling her hands empty, Aster's anxious heart finally relaxed completely.

It worked!

However, when she looked up at Rayquaza again, she saw...

[Here you go.]

The scroll fell into Dragonite's energy cube box.

Aster: "???"

"Draaa?"

Dragonite was also confused.

What's this?

[Study hard!]

Rayquaza said quite seriously and solemnly.

[Don't lose to it!]

"Draaa?"

Dragonite flew to Johan's side with small wing flaps, handing over the scroll.

"What's this?"

Aster watched the scroll that ultimately ended up in Teacher Johan's hands, even more bewildered.

Could it be that I've been isolated from the world too long?

The outside world has completely changed from what I thought?

However, facing Johan's confusion, Aster quickly explained:

"It's a move scroll, the 'Dragon Lord's' move inheritance scroll."

Johan slowly opened the scroll. Inside... were ancient characters he completely didn't recognize, but the scroll seemed to contain some special power.

Realizing Johan might not recognize these "Draconid people" characters, Aster helped translate:

"This is 'Dragon Ascent'..."

Dragon Ascent?!

Rayquaza's signature move?

Noticing Dragonite's expression, Johan understood.

"So... this is a relatively ancient 'TM,' right?"

The Pokémon world was strange.

You say its technology is advanced and constantly progressing... things it has now, ancient times had too.

Very mysterious.

Speaking of which.

Could there be Groudon's Precipice Blades scroll and Kyogre's Origin Pulse scroll?

No, hard to say.

Johan vaguely seemed to remember there was a remote island where people worshipped Groudon and Kyogre...

[By the way, what was that matter you mentioned earlier?]

Rayquaza asked.

"Oh, right."

Johan snapped back to attention.

"There's a huge meteorite in space, expected to hit the Hoenn region in some time. I'd like to ask for your help intercepting that meteorite before it enters the atmosphere."

[Meteorites are trivial matters.]

Rayquaza waved its claw.

Getting a satisfactory result, Johan was in a good mood.

This trip wasn't wasted.

However, Rayquaza soon raised another question.

[Which area should I wait in?]

The sky was vast.

The ozone layer's range was even vaster.

Steven gave a fairly precise coordinate, and Mossdeep Space Center had even calculated the meteorite's flight trajectory.

Human coordinates and human divisions of sky and space were different from Rayquaza's understanding!

Johan and Rayquaza stared at each other.

The big problems were settled, but they were blocked by such a small coordinate issue?

[How about... you come with me?]

Rayquaza made a suggestion.

"Me? Space?"

Remembering the first time riding Rayquaza, Johan's face paled.

"Not... not very appropriate..."

Johan looked at Steven and Wallace, but before he could speak, Rayquaza proudly raised its head.

[They won't work.]

[Their physical constitution won't hold up.]

Moreover, Rayquaza obviously wasn't someone just anyone could ride.

In the manga...

Johan: "..."

Aster?

Forget it, such a seventeen or eighteen-year-old girl child...

And Rayquaza didn't know coordinates and star regions, so the isolated "Draconid people" probably didn't know either.

"I..."

Nearby Steven put down his phone and gave Johan a thumbs up:

"Teacher, custom spacesuits - Devon will prepare them."

Johan's mouth twitched.

Really something.

"Bangi..."

Tyranitar swallowed and quietly asked Johan.

Meteorites, tasty?

Johan: "..."

Fine, fine, fine.

Go then go!

Just consider it... going to get some meteorites for Tyranitar to eat, indirectly relieving wallet pressure, equivalent to making money.

Since it was making money, Johan's "resistance" wasn't so strong.

Under Rayquaza's watchful gaze, Johan and the others left Sky Pillar.

Also leaving was Aster, who still hadn't recovered.

So the thousand-year prophecy's meteorite was also about to fall during this time?

But fortunately...

With Teacher Johan there, plus the "Dragon Lord," it seemed no longer a problem?

Steven and Wallace also immediately informed the Hoenn League of this news after descending Sky Pillar.

Learning that the meteorite crisis would be jointly resolved by Johan and Rayquaza, all the Hoenn League's upper echelons breathed sighs of relief.

The appearance of the huge meteorite was like a Sword of Damocles suddenly appearing over their heads - one wrong move and they'd all be finished.

Old Joseph Stone also sighed in relief.

Finally didn't need to cause too much destruction for so-called "∞ Energy."

Thus.

All of Devon quickly operated again, striving to create the safest, most secure spacesuit for Johan in the shortest time!

Actually, Johan wasn't very concerned about this.

Because he'd already decided.

This trip to space, bring Darkrai!

On one hand for safety, on the other hand naturally also for safety - safety above all.

If worst came to worst, have Gengar and Darkrai simultaneously open spatial rifts and flee.

After all, life was precious.

Additionally.

He also tried contacting Deoxys through his phone.

His phone had once been "inhabited" by Deoxys, so he could contact Deoxys through special signals plus signal amplifiers.

With these multiple safeguards, this space journey should be safe.

After leaving Sky Pillar, Johan didn't leave Glass Island quickly, but went to Sootopolis City.

He remembered his agreement with King AZ.

If nothing unexpected happened, AZ's eternal Floette should be under that tree on Sootopolis City's central island.

Last time when he and Cynthia came together they didn't find it. He didn't know if he could successfully find that eternal Floette this time.

"You still have business?"

Before entering Sootopolis City, Johan couldn't help asking this question, looking at Aster who had been following behind them since leaving Sky Pillar.

Aster kept a straight face, pursing her lips, seemingly having made some decision.

The next second.

Whoosh—

Aster's cloak fluttered as she knelt on one knee before Johan.

This stance startled all three of them.

"What are you doing..." Johan sweated, quickly helping Aster up.

Aster wanted to resist, but found... she wasn't as strong as Johan.

Surrounding people all cast strange looks.

"It's Teacher Johan!"

"And Mr. Steven and Mr. Wallace!"

Originally wanting to quietly enter Sootopolis City, Aster's outburst caused the three to be recognized anyway.

Quickly escape!

To calm the anxious hearts of Hoenn residents after the disaster, the Hoenn League hadn't hidden this super-ancient twin god destruction incident.

The commotion was too big to hide anyway.

Although specific details weren't widely known... rumors had already spread about "Teacher Johan taking down Groudon and blowing up Kyogre's skull."

He was already quite famous.

With this incident...

Wanting to appear quietly in crowded places was too difficult.

Quickly pulling the bewildered Aster along, they ran.

They finally ran into what seemed like a quiet house.

"Check if people are gone. Don't let us be mistaken for thieves." Johan said.

"It's fine, Teacher. This house is mine."

Johan: "..."

Randomly running into a house in Sootopolis City and it's yours?

"I want to apprentice myself to Teacher Johan!" Aster finally stated her purpose.

Similarly, she had also taken Steven's words to heart, gaining some understanding.

So it could be done this way...

# 662: Rayquaza, Launch! (Two-in-One Chapter)

Hoenn region, Sootopolis City.

Under the towering tree on the central lake island.

Although the appearance of Groudon and Kyogre had brought considerable destruction to all of Hoenn, fortunately the League's plan was implemented quite smoothly, and with Steven, Wallace and others' desperate protection, Sootopolis City hadn't become complete ruins like in the manga.

Coming alone under the tree.

Rustle—rustle—

A gentle breeze passed through, and the lush tree made rustling sounds.

Listening carefully, it seemed like there was pleasant laughter.

"Floette."

Johan gently placed his hand on the tree trunk, closed his eyes, and slowly spread his aura outward, trying to find traces of the Eternal Floette.

"Sni~"

Snivy stood at the edge of the small island, head lowered, admiring its own "peerless beauty."

It truly was beautiful.

Today's sunlight was gentle, with a light breeze. Snivy's body constantly emanated a faint glow—it was photosynthesizing.

"Sni?"

Looking and looking...

Snivy suddenly noticed that in the water's reflection, a Floette holding flower stems appeared behind it.

But this Floette looked somewhat special...

Other Floette, regardless of what flower form they took, at most only differed in the color of the flowers they held—red flowers, orange flowers, blue flowers, white flowers, etc.

But this Floette—its body showed a deep blue color, and the flower it held was also very different.

Crimson stems and petals, black spike-like stamens, giving a mysterious yet eerie feeling.

"Sni?"

Snivy immediately turned to look behind itself—nothing there.

It clenched its little hands into fists and rubbed its eyes vigorously.

Looking at the reflection again.

It was still there!

"Yiiin~"

A gentle voice, like silver bells, like spring water tinkling.

The Floette seemed to be greeting it, eyes curved into crescents, with crystalline petals dancing in the air, like cherry blossoms, like peach blossoms...

"Sni..."

So beautiful...

Snivy murmured.

Johan suddenly appeared beside Snivy, smiled and crouched down, looking at the Floette in the reflection with it, saying softly:

"It's the Eternal Floette."

Due to the influence of the "Ultimate Weapon," the Eternal Floette actually couldn't be considered a Floette anymore. Its appearance, abilities, base stats, etc., had all undergone tremendous changes.

Even, in a sense, the Eternal Floette could be considered a legendary Pokémon.

Eternal Floette?

Snivy was stunned. Besides its appearance, it didn't understand how this Floette differed from other Floette.

"Yiin~"

The Floette in the reflection gently blinked at Johan, seemingly greeting him.

Johan also smiled and waved at it, then sat beside Snivy, slowly telling the little one about the story of King AZ and the Eternal Floette.

Snivy hadn't met AZ, nor experienced the Xerneas and Yveltal incident, so it didn't know about the Eternal Floette.

But under Johan's narration, Snivy unconsciously nestled into Johan's arms, its little hands gripping his clothes tightly.

To be honest.

Snivy didn't quite understand the Eternal Floette's actions.

Although what King AZ did had an element of... self-satisfaction, if it were the Floette at that time, it would definitely be moved.

As for the sins AZ committed... they could bear them together.

Together was better than being apart for thousands of years without meeting.

Johan was somewhat surprised by Snivy's such "awareness."

He smiled and said: "It's like when you see a river, you're already outside the river. When you see a mountain, you're already outside the mountain."

"Sni?" Snivy tilted its head looking at Johan.

What was all this about?

Johan continued: "When you see anger, it means you're already outside anger. When you see dissatisfaction, it means you're already outside dissatisfaction... Those in the situation are confused, bystanders see clearly. You haven't experienced it, so naturally you'd find it incomprehensible."

"Sni..."

Snivy seemed to understand somewhat, nodding thoughtfully.

Johan looked again at the Eternal Floette in the reflection, which also showed a thoughtful expression, and said:

"Clinging to one thought, fixed on one thought. Let go of one thought, peace in the heart. Floette, King AZ has already let go. What about you?"

"Yiin..."

The Eternal Floette was stunned, showing reminiscence and deep longing in its eyes.

Obviously.

Although they hadn't met, the Eternal Floette's feelings for AZ hadn't changed. Even because they hadn't seen each other for so long, it had fermented into something even more intense.

"You've felt it too, haven't you? AZ's change."

Otherwise, the Eternal Floette probably still wouldn't appear.

Even though Johan's aura, after Arceus's "blessing," had become many times stronger.

"Yiin..."

In the reflection, the Eternal Floette disappeared.

"Sni?"

Snivy pointed at the reflection.

It left?

Johan picked up the little one and stood, patting the grass off his pants:

"Let's go."

"Sni?"

Just leaving like that?

"After we finish dealing with Hoenn's affairs, we'll come back. It will come with us to Kalos."

Snivy nodded as if understanding.

Nestled in Johan's arms, looking up to see his defined features, it couldn't help speaking up.

"Sni?"

You just said all that so reasonably—can you "see" your true self?

Hearing this, Johan grinned.

"Of course."

"Sni?"

Then what did you see? What did you step outside of?

Johan's answer was quite simple.

"I saw poverty."

Poverty?

Johan's smile contained some helplessness.

"But seeing poverty doesn't mean I'm outside poverty. Haha—"

Snivy's expression was dazed.

After a long while, it slowly reacted.

So you just said all that about clinging to thoughts and clarity—you were talking big!

Snivy noticed Johan's somewhat teasing and mocking gaze, and its cheeks immediately reddened.

Vine Whip dance!

"Sni! (▼皿▼)"

Hoenn region, Kanaz City.

"Teacher Johan, this..."

A League staff member stood at the café door, holding a thick stack of reimbursement forms, sweating profusely.

This Groudon and Kyogre incident, while not causing devastating destruction, obviously still had impact. So the League received numerous disaster relief "reimbursement forms" from various towns and cities.

But the problem was...

Wasn't this a bit... too much?

Café coffee cup reimbursement, quantity... 1000!

What café would have 1000 coffee cups!

And they all broke at once?

Johan, carrying coffee, walked over and glanced at the reimbursement form, seemingly also finding something wrong.

"Sorry, since there were so many forms, some were written by Gengar. This coffee cup quantity..."

The staff member was about to sigh in relief when he saw Johan take out a pen and add a stroke, changing the "1" to "4."

"Gengar is still too naive. How could it be 1000? It's 4000. It made a mistake."

"This..."

The staff member was drenched in sweat.

"Ka-kaah?"

Gengar, cleaning glass nearby, blinked and pointed at itself.

Me?

Naive?

"Vii~"

Don't forget my cookies.

Even Victini couldn't help running out to remind Johan.

"I wrote you down for 500 boxes. Any more would spoil before you could eat them."

"Vii~(＾＿－)v"

After spending so much time together, Victini had gradually taken on Johan's "shape."

"Our café has some sweets. Very reasonable, right?" Johan looked at the staff member with a smile.

"Rea—reasonable..." The staff member nodded repeatedly.

He was about to cry.

Really.

If it were just coffee cups and cookies, that would be one thing.

The problem was...

This was just the "small stuff" among all these reimbursement forms. This thick stack... was Teacher Johan planning to establish a nation?

Seeming to see the staff member's difficulty, Johan patted his shoulder and said:

"It's fine, all small matters. You're just responsible for helping deliver documents. Just hand these to Elite Four Drake."

"Y-yes..."

Thinking of this, the staff member also relaxed.

That's right.

Anyway, he wasn't the one approving them—that was Elite Four Drake and Elite Four Glacia. Just hopefully these two Elite Four members wouldn't start fighting over this...

Watching the staff member leave, Johan took out his phone and called Elite Four Drake.

"Old man, what percentage do I get again?"

"As agreed, thirty percent." Drake's hearty voice came through the phone.

Regarding Johan, Drake couldn't say much about other things, but just in terms of filling reimbursement forms... probably no one in the entire League could match him. Truly worthy of being the legendary "Reimbursement King."

This incident was so big that the entire League across all regions knew about it. Many people even thought the Hoenn region was going to be flattened. Now only being affected this little, without even any death reports, just some accidental injuries.

But with such a major incident, they weren't claiming from the Hoenn League, but from the main League headquarters.

The main League was so rich. With Hoenn needing "reconstruction," this was already quite "modest."

"Alright." Johan nodded and asked: "Is this enough? If not, I can print another hundred copies?"

"That's about enough. Any more and the main League will start complaining."

"Got it."

Getting confirmation, Johan happily hung up the phone.

Another benefit of not being an Elite Four member or Champion was that reimbursement forms... could be filled freely!

Anyway, there were people above taking the pressure.

If he became an Elite Four member or Champion, he couldn't do this anymore.

"Teacher."

At this time, Aster came in from outside carrying bags, asking with some confusion:

"That person just now... was the weather very hot? He was sweating so much?"

"Maybe." Johan turned to Ninetales resting on the booth: "Ninetales, it's too hot."

"Oowoo..."

Ninetales responded softly, its fur gently swaying as the café's temperature immediately dropped several degrees.

In summer, Ninetales' "usefulness" was fully displayed.

A few days ago when facing Groudon, under that blazing sun and lava heat, Johan felt no discomfort at all, precisely because of Ninetales' presence.

"Teacher, should I take these to the kitchen?" Aster indicated the bags in her hands, all filled with ingredients.

"Thank you for the trouble."

"No trouble at all!"

Aster skipped toward the kitchen, where the Indeedee siblings, Alcremie, and Rotom were already preparing.

Watching her cheerful manner, Johan smiled helplessly.

"Now she's acting more like a kid."

Previously, in Sootopolis City, Aster had proposed wanting to apprentice herself to Johan, not just for Pokémon training, but also for martial arts.

But Johan expressed that... he didn't run a fighting gym and didn't take disciples.

Wallace and Steven at the time indicated that Teacher Johan didn't take disciples, but students were possible.

And now, who didn't call Johan "Teacher" when they met him?

Some out of respect, some due to his position, and some were students addressing their teacher.

So, regardless of whether you were actually Teacher Johan's student, if you considered yourself his student and called him teacher, then you were a student.

Aster had an epiphany at the time, then... became like this.

However, as a "Draconid," living in the isolated "Meteor Village," many of Aster's behaviors and consciousness hadn't aligned with the outside world, so she seemed particularly respectful toward Johan, even more respectful than disciples to masters.

But as they spent time together, Aster discovered Johan was easygoing, without airs or strict rules, so she gradually relaxed.

Look, with Reshiram, Zekrom, and Darkrai still not having left, Aster proactively took on the "heavy responsibility" of grocery shopping.

It's just...

"Somehow gained another student..."

Aster had special constitution and abilities, essentially existing for Dragon-type Pokémon.

"Feels like... I can 'show off' to Lance in the future."

Thinking of this, the pressure of having a student immediately lessened.

Moreover, current Aster already had considerable strength. After growing for some time... surpassing the "prodigy" Steven might be unlikely, but catching up to Wallace was hopeful.

At minimum, she had the potential to become an Elite Four member, perfectly suited to take over Elite Four Drake's Dragon-type Elite Four position.

"Lost out!"

Johan struck palm with fist.

"Should have asked for one more percent commission earlier, solving such a big 'problem' for old man Drake."

Ding ding—

Phone ringing.

Taking it out, Johan's heart immediately jumped.

Caller ID: Cynthia.

Answering the call.

"Johan." Cynthia's voice immediately came through the phone, but just two words, and sounding somewhat flat.

Hearing this tone, Johan's mind unconsciously conjured an image.

Holy crap!

So cool!

"Cough, let me explain..." Johan coughed lightly.

No choice.

This incident was too big. There were many news helicopters at the scene, and though later the commotion was so large it caused signal and network problems, preventing the most shocking scenes from being filmed...

But...

The scene of Johan alone facing Groudon, intercepting Groudon, was still captured.

On the vast ocean, the towering massive Groudon churning lava all the way, Johan riding a bicycle on an ice path coming before Groudon, raising his hand to indicate: This road is blocked!

This image made countless people instantly become fans, supporters of Teacher Johan, and turned many casual fans into devoted followers.

But being cool was cool.

But in Cynthia's eyes...

"I've already had people build a signal tower on Mt. Coronet." Cynthia interrupted Johan's words.

Mt. Coronet?

Signal tower?

That largest mountain range in the Pokémon world?

Building a signal tower in the polar cold constantly covered by ice and snow...

"Hired Devon's construction team. Three days to completion."

Johan was sweating.

Though if this job were given to Team Rocket, it would probably take at most two days...

Hm?

At this thought, Johan suddenly realized.

Seemed like... he'd found another path for Team Rocket?

"...call me. We'll do it together, okay?"

"Okay?"

"Okay..."

"Good boy."

"Draaa..."

Good thing Cynthia wasn't here to "demand an explanation," letting Johan sigh in relief.

Mt. Coronet had poor signal, so he couldn't contact Cynthia. How could Johan be blamed for not calling for "backup"?

Moreover, after building the signal tower on Mt. Coronet, calling his little cabbage would be much more convenient in the future. Johan was overjoyed.

"By the way, are Flint and the others with you?" Johan suddenly asked.

Thanks for your sacrifice, good brother Flint!

Location...

This was the key point.

In the movie "Giratina and the Sky Warrior: Shaymin," Giratina trapped in the Distortion World escaped because of Shaymin, this mythical Pokémon, establishing a connection between the fierce legendary beast and the cute, weak mythical beast.

Then they lived together shamelessly ever after (crossed out).

Cough.

In his previous life, there were quite a few fanart of Giratina and Shaymin.

But in this world, Giratina had long escaped the Distortion World's constraints because of Johan, so Shaymin... probably had never been contacted.

But the world's convergence... hard to say.

Could it really have gone to find Shaymin?

"Perhaps... Gracidea?" Johan said somewhat uncertainly.

"Gracidea? Gracidea flower field?"

Cynthia seemed to have heard of it, then said: "I understand. When Flint finishes climbing, I'll have him and Aaron go take a look."

"Mm."

After that, Johan honestly "confessed" about going to space with Rayquaza to destroy the meteorite.

And he said Darkrai would go with him, and he'd contacted Deoxys, so it was very safe.

Going to space...

This was something Cynthia really couldn't help with.

Countless words finally converged into one sentence...

"Be careful... I'm here waiting for you..."

"Okay!"

Two days later.

Hoenn region, Mossdeep Space Center.

Wearing Devon Corporation's highest-tech spacesuit, Johan stood on the top floor of Mossdeep Space Center, listening to instructions from nearby staff and Steven.

"...This is the signal receiver. Eighteen total installed. We can definitely receive Teacher Johan's voice." The staff member said.

Rare opportunity.

Space...

In his previous life, how many children made wishes as kids to become astronauts when they grew up, only to learn as adults how difficult it was, having to struggle with life instead.

Never expected... to have a chance to fulfill this "dream" in the Pokémon world.

Would he encounter Pokémon from space that he'd never seen before?

"Teacher?" Steven asked quietly.

"Cough, nothing." Johan waved his hand.

"So, what's this situation?"

"Ka-kaah~ヽ(●＾▽)ノ"

Through the spacesuit's transparent visor, Gengar was grinning and waving at Johan.

The purple fatty in a dark red spacesuit... was still a fatty.

In Gengar's own words—

Such a cool outfit, I gotta try it!

Having waited so long for armor that never came, a spacesuit was "reluctantly" acceptable.

"No wonder it's been so quiet these past few days..."

Moreover, with Gengar's constitution, did it really need something like a spacesuit?

Sure it wouldn't end up with Rayquaza carrying the spacesuit in front while Gengar chased behind?

However, thinking about needing to get some meteorites for Tyranitar, having Gengar would undoubtedly be much more convenient. Johan let it be.

The appointed time arrived.

Rumble rumble—

The sea of clouds above Mossdeep City began churning, accompanied by a loud, imposing roar.

"Roar—!!"

A green dragon pierced through the clouds, arriving with a domineering attitude.

"It's Rayquaza!"

"Alive!"

"It's—it's not here to attack, right?"

The staff on the top floor of Mossdeep Space Center couldn't help being intimidated by Rayquaza's presence.

Even with Teacher Johan's guarantee, this Rayquaza's demeanor... didn't look easy to get along with.

It wouldn't just ram the entire space center, would it?

Obviously, such dangerous thoughts were somewhat excessive. Rayquaza finally stopped beside Mossdeep Space Center, its sharp gaze also softening slightly.

[I have arrived!]

Johan smiled and said: "Thanks for the trouble, Rayquaza. After this is over, I'll treat you to a meal."

[Truly?]

"Of course."

"Roar—!!!"

Rayquaza seemed even more energetic.

Then.

[?]

"For safety."

"All set."

Somehow, Gengar had already drilled into Johan's shadow, poking out half its head.

Waving its claw at Rayquaza.

"Rayquaza, launch!" Johan called out.

"Roar!!"

Rayquaza roared, its body suddenly shaking as it immediately became a straight green arrow, flying toward the dense clouds, destination—outer space!

This was... Rayquaza's speed?

"Signal normal!"

"Video transmission normal!"

"Navigation information transmission normal!"

It felt like... the person flying in front while the soul desperately chased behind.

The Mossdeep Space Center staff wanted confirmation when they heard—

"Ka-kaah~!"

Gengar's exclamation came through.

"Audio transmission normal! Navigation beginning!"

Johan and Gengar's spacesuit helmet visors displayed their current position, then showed the meteorite's location.

"Breaking through troposphere!"

Incredible silence.

As if arriving at the world's end.

Looking back.

As Rayquaza flew past, these small meteorites immediately split to both sides.

Occasionally, one or two "meteorites" cracked, becoming small meteors.

"Ka-kaah..."

Somehow, Gengar had conjured a "black hole" in its hands, like pulling a net, just scooping up meteorites.

One scoop, a whole bunch.

[These meteorites are mediocre quality. If you really want some, I'll take you to a place I often eat at later.]

"Ka-kaah?"

Gengar's eyes lit up.

[Of course, some meteorites carry cosmic viruses and can't be eaten casually.]

After reaching space, Rayquaza seemed to talk more, no longer using that archaic tone.

Don't know how long they flew.

The target meteorite, the incredibly huge meteorite, finally appeared in their sight.

"Found it!"

Johan said softly.

[Hm?]

But Rayquaza suddenly stopped, showing some hesitation.

"What's wrong?"

[There's something on that meteorite.]
