# 663: A Request from Space (Two-in-One Chapter)

In the vast universe, having some things around was quite normal.

Look, nearby floated numerous small meteors that would explode like dandelions at the slightest touch or approach, leaving behind scattered hard meteor shells while their colorful cores took the opportunity to escape.

What interested Rayquaza were the meteor shells left behind by the small meteors—to Rayquaza, they were like little candies.

Just like how Tyranitar used to eat diamonds.

Gengar had also scooped up quite a few of these meteor shells.

But in the vast universe, there weren't many things that could make Rayquaza wary.

"Is it Deoxys? Or..."

[No.]

Rayquaza shook its head. Of course it would recognize Deoxys.

Moreover...

Rayquaza glanced not far away, where two Deoxys—one purple, one green—were watching from a distance. They were the helpers Johan had called.

"It can't possibly be Clefairy, right?" Johan's expression was strange.

Rayquaza looked back at Johan with an utterly speechless expression.

"Just kidding."

Patting Rayquaza's scales, Johan also began to think.

In the Pokémon world, there were actually quite a few Pokémon in space. Setting aside those never seen or registered, and excluding Clefairy which was somewhat of a joke, that left...

Deoxys, Minior, Beheeyem, Solrock, Lunatone...

And there were more.

If you really counted them.

Unova's Tao trio also came from space, Galar region's Eternatus likewise came from space, and there was also...

Suddenly.

Johan paused, seemingly remembering something. "The legendary space Pokémon?"

[?]

"Necrozma?"

This was originally just wild speculation, but when Johan said this name, Rayquaza fell silent, its expression becoming particularly serious.

Seeing this attitude, Johan's heart skipped a beat.

"It can't... really be Necrozma, right?"

That didn't make sense.

The Blinding One Necrozma should still be sleeping somewhere underground in the Alola region at this time, shouldn't it?

Could this be another one?

The Pokémon world was vast, with even multiple universes existing. The appearance of the same legendary Pokémon wasn't impossible.

Rayquaza came in black and green varieties too.

If it really was Necrozma, that would be big trouble.

Among the many legendary Pokémon in the Pokémon world, Rayquaza's strength was definitely among the more outstanding, and with its Mega Evolution ability, there weren't many opponents who could face it head-on.

Even Reshiram and Zekrom wouldn't work.

Perhaps Kyurem after fusing with Reshiram or Zekrom could, but that would count as two-on-one.

And the legendary "Blinding One," Ultra Necrozma, was one of the few beings capable of a direct confrontation with Mega Rayquaza.

His thoughts flashing, Johan lightly patted Rayquaza in comfort:

"It's okay, you're not alone."

He had called two Deoxys, plus Darkrai who came along.

Four against one—advantage was his.

[It's somewhat similar, but I'm... not certain.]

Rayquaza suddenly said.

Hearing this, Johan stumbled.

Somewhat similar?

Not certain?

Then why were you being so serious?

Rayquaza steadied itself, looking back at Johan with an inexplicable gleam in its eyes.

From the time Rayquaza had memories until now, this seemed... to be the first time someone told it "you're not alone."

This feeling was strange.

Even for a being as proud as Rayquaza, after being lonely for an incredibly long time with perhaps its greatest pleasure being beating up Groudon and Kyogre, it now actually felt a sense of... friendship?

An indescribable, subtle feeling.

"Forget it." Johan shook his head, his tone becoming resolute. "No matter what, this huge meteorite must be destroyed. As for what's on it... we'll deal with that after destroying the meteorite!"

[Good!]

Rayquaza also felt this way.

At worst... they'd just have a fight!

Buzz—

With Gengar and Darkrai supporting him, Johan flew off Rayquaza's back, while the two Deoxys in the distance also approached.

Riding Rayquaza to crash into the meteorite at this point?

Johan wasn't looking to shorten his lifespan.

"Long time no see."

Seeing the two Deoxys, Johan smiled and greeted them.

Buzz buzz buzz—

The signal lights on the green and purple Deoxys's faces flashed—this was them greeting Johan.

"These are gifts I brought for you."

Johan opened a portable pouch specially installed on his spacesuit by Devon, taking out two crystal Deoxys sculptures. Besides different poses, the two sculptures had green and purple diamonds embedded in their chests respectively.

Gifts?

The two Deoxys seemed very surprised, looking at each other before gazing at the two crystals... the angular features on both Deoxys seemed to soften.

Gifts...

We can have gifts too?

Moreover.

Obviously these gifts corresponded to each of them respectively.

He gave the crystal Deoxys with the green diamond to the purple-core Deoxys, and vice versa.

If their companion disappeared again in the future, at least they'd have something to remember them by.

"They're not very valuable things. I hope you like them." Johan said.

Zzz—zzz—

[Thank you.]

Deoxys's voice rang in his mind.

"Ready, Rayquaza!"

Johan looked at Rayquaza again, indicating it could begin.

"Roar—!!"

Rayquaza roared, its body beginning to emanate blazing, brilliant light.

Hoenn region, Mossdeep Space Center.

Steven, Wallace, Glacia, Drake and other high-ranking Hoenn League officials were all gathered here, assembled in Mossdeep Space Center's command center.

Everyone was watching Johan and Rayquaza's every move.

If the operation encountered any uncontrollable factors and failed, Devon's "Dimensional Transporter" could serve as a backup plan for emergency activation.

"Meteorite locked on!"

Mossdeep Space Center researchers reported the situation.

"Why did they stop?" Elite Four Drake looked at Rayquaza hovering in space, somewhat curious.

"After all, it's such a huge meteorite." Old Joseph Stone sighed.

Honestly.

When they learned the meteorite would impact Hoenn, they didn't have a clear concept of just how large this so-called "huge meteorite" was.

But seeing this scene, watching the comparison between the massive Rayquaza and that meteorite, they finally understood—if such a large meteorite crashed down, forget about Hoenn, even other regions would suffer extremely severe damage.

Even...

"Wonder if it can be successfully destroyed..." Elite Four Sidney said worriedly.

"Here it comes!" Steven said gravely, eyes fixed on the screen.

Although the image was somewhat blurry due to distance and unstable signal transmission, they could clearly see brilliant Mega Evolution light appearing around Rayquaza.

"Mega Rayquaza..."

Everyone in the control center had only serious expressions.

"Hm?"

Wallace suddenly noticed.

"Teacher Johan, he..."

Why did Teacher Johan also have Mega Evolution energy fluctuations?

"Key Stone?" Steven also noticed this.

The two looked at each other.

Wait.

Teacher Johan could help Rayquaza Mega Evolve?

Didn't Rayquaza autonomously Mega Evolve?

"As expected." Aster's eyes flickered.

Even though Teacher wasn't a so-called "inheritor," he could still do what "inheritors" could do, and even... much more easily than "inheritors"!

"This is Teacher..."

Under everyone's gaze, Mega Rayquaza became an incredibly sharp arrow, charging straight toward that huge meteorite.

In space.

Hm?

Watching Rayquaza prepare for Mega Evolution, Johan paused, feeling something strange about the Key Stone on his body.

Rayquaza?

Rayquaza seemed somewhat surprised by this as well.

Previously, only "Draconid" "inheritors" could assist its Mega Evolution, giving it stronger power, but now...

Gengar nearby seemed to understand something, remembering the seven-colored giant stone it had "taken."

With so many recent events, it hadn't had time to properly study it with Johan.

Johan took a deep breath.

Legendary Pokémon Mega Evolution—this wasn't his first time.

He immediately used aura and called out gravely:

"Rayquaza—"

"Mega Evolution!"

"Roar—!!"

Seven-colored rainbow light burst forth. Rayquaza's internal "Delta Symbol" or rather "Mikado Organ" scattered countless golden particles, forming ribbon-like bands extending from both sides of its face.

The patterns on Rayquaza's body also blazed with dazzling golden light, its skin gleaming like brilliant green emerald. What appeared before it wasn't the Mega Evolution symbol, but Rayquaza's exclusive "Delta Δ"!

Boom!!

Though this was airless space, with Rayquaza's transformation, Delta Stream spread outward from it as the center.

Johan watched Rayquaza's transformation—no, it should now be called Mega Rayquaza!

Sometimes being cool really was a lifetime thing...

"Rayquaza!"

Johan called out again, "Dragon Ascent!"

"Roar—!!"

Mega Rayquaza seemed to become a golden arrow, bathed in brilliant golden light, gathering all its power at one point as it charged straight toward that incredibly huge meteorite.

Golden light cut through the pitch-black universe.

Boom—

In an instant.

The entire world seemed to contain only one thin, bright line. The brief silence felt as long as a century.

The next second.

Boom!!

Mega Rayquaza burst through from the other side of the meteorite!

And the incredibly huge meteorite exploded at that moment!

An extremely powerful impact spread from the meteorite's explosion point, forming invisible shockwaves.

The two Deoxys and Darkrai shielded Johan, creating barriers that blocked the impact's aftershocks.

Countless large and small meteorites struck the barrier, ultimately turning to powder and scattering.

At Mossdeep Space Center, everyone felt like the huge meteorite had been cut in half, then the already blurry camera lost signal.

When signal was finally restored, only numerous meteorite fragments remained floating around.

"So incredible..."

After a long while, Wallace voiced everyone's thoughts.

It really was incredible.

Such a huge meteorite was just... pierced through and destroyed by Mega Rayquaza.

Was this Rayquaza's true power?

Whether human or ordinary Pokémon, they were truly... too small before such power.

But the next second, everyone in the control room instinctively closed their eyes.

Because this was uncontrollable—a natural reaction.

The blurry screen suddenly flashed with extremely blinding light.

Fortunately, because the light was too intense, Devon's special camera was destroyed!

"What's happening?!"

The people who finally recovered looked at the now signal-less screen, everyone confused and somewhat surprised.

Even the huge meteorite's explosion hadn't destroyed the camera, but the sudden blinding light actually destroyed it?

Then everyone's hearts tightened.

Oh no!

Teacher Johan wouldn't be in danger, would he?

In space.

Johan, as the closest eyewitness to what everyone in the control room saw, naturally witnessed it as well.

But compared to the control room's shock, he was slightly better off.

Because Rayquaza had given warning from the start, and because Deoxys and Darkrai had reacted in time.

Deoxys's psychic barriers, plus Darkrai and Gengar's black holes, prevented this intense light from harming Johan.

But...

"It can't really be the 'Blinding One' Necrozma, right?" Johan thought.

This level of intense light, besides Necrozma, probably only...

"Roar!!!"

A commotion came from within the shattered meteorite fragments.

There, a being emanating sun-like blazing light, shaped like an ordinary golden lion, stood on a relatively large meteorite fragment, its sharp eyes locked firmly on Mega Rayquaza!

"Solgaleo?"

Seeing that creature, even though Johan had some mental preparation, he still couldn't help being stunned.

The Sun God!

Or it could be called the "Emissary of the Sun," "Beast that Devours the Sun," the Sunne Pokémon, Solgaleo!

A legendary Pokémon from the Alola region, also called a "legendary space Pokémon."

Though it had the word "space," didn't this refer to the "space" from "other universes"?

But it really appeared in outer space?

However, this did explain why Rayquaza had vaguely sensed Necrozma's aura from the huge meteorite earlier.

Others might not know, but Johan was quite clear that the legendary space Pokémon Solgaleo and Lunala actually had extremely deep connections with the "Blinding One" Necrozma.

It's just...

Why would it appear here?

Buzz—

The dazzling light on Solgaleo gradually faded as it slowly changed from "Radiant Sun phase" back to its original appearance.

Resembling a giant lion, entirely white with azure blue eyes that seemed to contain brilliance, while the blue area on its forehead contained what looked like a starry sky with constantly changing stellar formations.

"Solgaleo!!"

Solgaleo roared, its body blazing with light again as it charged toward Mega Rayquaza like a meteor or comet!

Meteor Rush!

"Roar—!!"

Facing Solgaleo's direct attack without any words, Mega Rayquaza also didn't want to waste time talking, immediately becoming an arrow and charging straight out.

Dragon Ascent!

Meteor Rush VS Dragon Ascent!

A century collision Johan had never imagined.

Like a battle between meteors and comets.

Boom!!

Terrifying impact aftershocks swept out again.

"What is that thing?"

Darkrai, blocking the aftershocks, couldn't help glaring at Johan questioningly.

"Don't glare at me—I didn't bring it here."

Johan was also helpless about this.

This time really couldn't be blamed on him, right?

Who knew a Solgaleo would be sleeping on the huge meteorite?

Bang—

The two great legendary Pokémon separated after one clash.

The Mega Evolution energy around Mega Rayquaza faded as its chest heaved.

After all, it had just shattered such a large meteorite—even Rayquaza couldn't help feeling fatigued.

But even so, Solgaleo hadn't gained any advantage from Rayquaza.

[This one's not weak.]

Rayquaza's voice rang in Johan's mind.

[But that's all it amounts to!]

"Solgaleo!!"

In the vast universe, a mysterious power gradually gathered around Solgaleo, granting it stronger power.

Cosmic Power!

Solgaleo looked deeply at Rayquaza, but Johan suddenly felt its peripheral vision seemed to be watching him too.

But given the current situation...

"Rayquaza, don't use Dragon Ascent anymore—Fire Blast! This guy's weak to fire!"

The legendary "Sun God" being afraid of fire, the legendary "Moon God" being afraid of ghosts—if word got out, probably not many would believe it.

Rayquaza didn't believe it.

This guy had been like a sun earlier—how could it be afraid of fire?

But trusting Johan, despite his confusion, Rayquaza still spat out terrifying flames!

Even though Rayquaza wasn't a Fire-type Pokémon, its flames were extremely powerful.

At the same time.

Johan gave another command: "Gengar, Spectral Thief!"

Gengar, busy collecting meteorites, immediately dropped what it was doing upon hearing Johan's words, put on sunglasses to block the intense light, and grinned wickedly at Solgaleo.

"Ka-kaah~! ┏('_')ノ"

Give it here!

Solgaleo: ?

It felt the power it had accumulated was rapidly draining away.

No way.

How could an ordinary Pokémon steal power from it?

But sorry, their Gengar... was just this unreasonable.

Moreover, the Sun God Solgaleo was also afraid of "ghosts."

As everyone knows, the tougher the guy, the more afraid of ghosts (not really), this was very reasonable.

The sudden power loss caused Solgaleo to lose focus briefly. Rayquaza didn't waste such an opportunity—massive flames instantly engulfed Solgaleo.

Boom!!!

But soon.

Solgaleo emerged from the raging flames, cloaked in dazzling light and looking majestic.

Rayquaza immediately looked at Johan irritably.

This is what you called afraid of fire?

However, before Rayquaza could speak, the light around Solgaleo dimmed again as it staggered, nearly falling onto the meteorite fragments.

Rayquaza: ?

Wait, you really are afraid of fire?

Solgaleo didn't pay attention to Rayquaza. It tilted its head looking at Johan, its azure eyes filled with confusion and bewilderment.

It didn't understand why this human... seemed to know it so well?

But its time was running out.

"Roar—!!"

Finding Solgaleo's weakness, Rayquaza excitedly roared.

"Wait, Rayquaza!" Johan quickly stopped it, halting its pursuit, while using aura to communicate with Solgaleo:

"Solgaleo, what do you want to do?"

Ride a meteorite to crash into the planet?

Or was it purely unintentional?

Or perhaps...

[I slept for a long time... I was hiding... I want to ask you for something...]

Fragmentary thoughts belonging to Solgaleo came back through aura.

Sleeping?

So the meteorite impact wasn't caused by Solgaleo?

As for hiding... Johan could probably guess who it was hiding from.

And the matter...

[Please... target... Altar of the Sunne...]

Buzz—

As these words ended, Solgaleo appeared before Johan at a speed that surprised everyone and every Pokémon.

"Ka-kaah!"

Gengar, Darkrai, and the two Deoxys were startled, almost simultaneously preparing to attack Solgaleo, but Johan raised his hand to stop them.

His aura sensed no malice from Solgaleo.

Solgaleo slowly lowered its body, its forehead flickering with stellar formations slowly approaching Johan.

Looking into it, Johan seemed to see a starry sky, a nebula dotted with countless stars.

[Please...]

Buzz—

Solgaleo's body suddenly became like a mirage, like a sand sculpture, quietly dispersing without leaving a trace.

"Ka-kaah?"

Gengar rubbed its eyes with its fists, mouth agape.

That move was so cool... can I learn it?

Johan opened his eyes.

"Strange, when did I close my eyes?"

He looked down at his hands, still wearing the thick dark red spacesuit.

"Just now... was that a dream? Or reality?"

He turned to look at Rayquaza, Deoxys, and Darkrai.

But none of them—whether Rayquaza, the Psychic-type Deoxys, or the nightmare god Darkrai—could give a definitive answer.

Such a huge golden lion, gone just like that.

And Johan, quite knowledgeable about dreams, couldn't give a definitive answer either.

Dream? Reality?

Regardless.

Besides adding some complications, everything went quite smoothly.

The meteorite was successfully destroyed!

"Teacher? Teacher! Can you hear me, Teacher? This is Steven!"

At this time.

Steven's voice came through the spacesuit.

"I hear you." Johan paused, then said.

"Whew—"

Steven clearly sighed in relief. "Teacher, you..."

"I'm fine." Johan slowly floated toward Rayquaza, standing on its head. "Meteorite crisis, resolved!"

After brief silence.

Enthusiastic cheers came through the communicator.

This was the release after facing consecutive disasters and intense pressure. Everyone in the control room, including Elite Four Drake, smiled from the heart.

Listening to the laughter in the communicator, Johan gazed at the distant planet, lost in thought.

[What's wrong?]

Rayquaza asked.

"Suddenly want to cause some trouble."

[What trouble?]

Rayquaza looked curious.

Darkrai nearby immediately became alert.

Oh no.

Without causing trouble, you already encounter this and that. If you actually cause trouble... are you planning to beat up Arceus again while your "power is at its peak"?

"Rayquaza, Deoxys, help me out." Johan's mouth unconsciously curved upward.

Since Giratina had "run away from home" on its own, he couldn't be blamed.

However.

The Distortion World was big enough anyway. Adding a few hundred million meteorites shouldn't matter much to it, right?

Since it didn't object, that meant it agreed.

The Groudon and Kyogre disaster ended!

The meteorite disaster ended!

The two mountains pressing down on the Hoenn region were finally moved aside one by one by Johan.

When he rode Rayquaza back to Mossdeep Space Center, numerous people had already gathered to welcome him.

This time.

The Hoenn League similarly didn't suppress the news.

Even.

The Hoenn League shared some footage captured by Mossdeep Space Center to networks and live streams.

Teacher Johan wanted to keep a low profile?

Not allowed!

Hoenn wouldn't allow anyone not to know Teacher Johan's contributions to all of Hoenn.

At the same time, it was telling those other regions with "ill intentions"—Teacher Johan was a Hoenn person!

But other League officials who understood Hoenn League's intentions scoffed at this.

As if Teacher Johan hadn't helped other regions.

As long as he hadn't become a Hoenn Elite Four member or Hoenn Champion for even one day, they all had opportunities!

Moreover, even if he did become one...

Who said a trainer could only serve in one region?

Teacher Johan belonged to everyone!

Regarding this kind of "turbulent" high-level maneuvering, Johan naturally didn't care nor had much mind to care. After bidding farewell to Rayquaza and Deoxys, he immediately called Cynthia to report his safety.

Then...

Then he went home to sleep.

So tired.

Riding Rayquaza at that speed was no joke—ordinary people's physical constitution absolutely couldn't handle it.

Moreover, he had inexplicably helped Rayquaza complete Mega Evolution.

But Johan wanted to sleep, yet some people wouldn't let him.

For example...

"Elite Four Drake, Elite Four Glacia, are you two planning to sleep at my place tonight?" Johan yawned deeply, looking at these two current pivotal figures in the Hoenn League's upper echelons.

"Johan."

Elite Four Drake was hot-tempered, so he got straight to the point:

"When will you challenge the Champion's Road?"

Johan: "!!"

"When did I say I'd challenge the Champion's Road?"

Glacia said: "Johan, you should know our Hoenn Champion position has been vacant for three years."

"Then find Steven. Steven's strength and ability—I think they're sufficient."

Current Steven would have some difficulty clearing the Champion's Road, but... nowadays, what decent person actually walked the Champion's Road?

Look at Lance.

Completely dominated by Lorelei.

"But you are Steven's teacher after all..." Glacia said again.

"What does being a teacher matter? 'Those who achieve come first'—have you heard this saying, Elite Four Glacia?"

After becoming Champion, how could he still file reimbursements?

File reimbursements for himself?

If word got out... people would think Teacher Johan was embezzling.

Moreover, don't think Johan couldn't see through this.

Current Hoenn, after experiencing the Groudon and Kyogre disaster, had many places needing attention. This was precisely when there was a pile of work—they were recruiting able bodies to their doorstep.

Even if he really wanted to do it... that would have to wait until after this period!

Mm!

Glacia and Elite Four Drake exchanged glances.

Finally, Glacia sighed.

"We have a mission..."

Johan immediately showed a wary expression.

Looking at the two Elite Four members, he asked: "Why do I feel like you two are scheming against me?"

First propose something difficult to accept to get a refusal, then present the real objective to achieve smooth success.

"You brat."

Drake was amused.

Weren't you very tired?

How could you still react so quickly?

Is this what studying psychology does?

"Don't worry, it's not a difficult mission. You, Steven, Wallace, even Norman all have one." Drake said.

So many people?

Johan relaxed his guard slightly.

Thinking carefully.

Hoenn region temporarily didn't seem to have any other particularly big troubles, right?

Not to mention Rayquaza and Deoxys—now even Groudon had a pretty good relationship with him. Team Magma and Team Aqua could hardly cause trouble anymore. At most, there was just one Kyogre...

"Really not difficult?"

"Of course." Drake kept a straight face, nodding solemnly.

"Alright, I..."

Johan sat up straight, just about to negotiate, when he saw Elite Four Drake and Elite Four Glacia both stand up simultaneously.

"Then it's decided." Drake said.

Johan: "???"

Wait.

He hadn't even finished speaking.

"This is part of the reward the League secured for you."

Elite Four Glacia tossed down a box and turned to leave.

As for Elite Four Drake... he was already outside preparing to ride Salamence.

"Wait, what exactly is the mission? At least tell me." Johan called out.

"You'll know in a while."

Elite Four Glacia's voice came from far away.

Running so fast?

"Why do I still feel like I got schemed?" Johan rubbed his chin lightly.

"Ka-kaah~"

Gengar nodded in agreement.

"So, did I just agree?" Johan looked at Gengar.

Gengar paused, then quickly shook its head.

"Right. I didn't agree."

"Ka-kaah~" Gengar crossed itself on its chest, then raised its hand to swear.

I didn't see those two people today.

"Exactly."

Opening the box Elite Four Glacia left behind.

An Ice-type Z-Crystal, a Flying-type Z-Crystal, a Rock-type Z-Crystal.

Johan's mouth twitched.

"I'm almost collecting a complete set..."

Besides the three Z-Crystals, there were also four "Rare Candies"!

Good heavens!

Had the Hoenn League's inventory been almost emptied?

"These are good stuff though..."

Johan happily put away the "Rare Candies."

"I'll make you candied fruit in a couple days."

Four "Rare Candies" weren't enough to share, but making them into food would solve the problem.

"Ka-kaah..."

Gengar immediately drooled.

That night.

Johan slept very deeply and had a very long dream.

In the dream.

Ultra Necrozma battled numerous deities, fighting until the sky was dark and the sun and moon lost their light...

Johan murmured in his sleep.

"Somehow seems like I set up a flag..."

# 664: Congratulations Teacher Johan on Your New Ride! (Two-in-One Chapter)

"Go, Dugtrio."

Johan threw out Poké Balls, summoning two Dugtrio.

Red light flashed.

Two Dugtrio, six heads total, appeared on this completely cooled lava island left behind by Groudon.

"Trio trio trio~"

The multiple heads of the two Dugtrio looked at each other, gazing around at the completely barren surroundings with bewildered expressions.

These two Dugtrio were temporarily borrowed by Johan from Steven's family.

Diglett and Dugtrio weren't commonly used by many trainers.

It wasn't that these Pokémon had any flaws, but rather that Diglett and Dugtrio often represented an entire region's ecosystem.

Johan vaguely remembered when he was young watching the original series, there was an episode where Diglett and Dugtrio caused upheaval, blocking many trainers' paths. Quite a few people wanted to use their own Pokémon to clear a route, but...

The moment those trainers threw their Poké Balls, the Pokémon inside wouldn't even emerge, returning to their balls on their own, unwilling to battle Diglett and Dugtrio.

Of course, being rarely used didn't mean they weren't used at all.

Steven's family had cultivated quite a few Diglett and Dugtrio for mineral surveying, land excavation, and other work.

After Dugtrio and Diglett loosened the soil, mining work would undoubtedly become much easier.

It's just that when Johan went to borrow them, Steven's family's Diglett and Dugtrio had all gone to "work," leaving only these two, which he borrowed.

As for what to have the Dugtrio do...

Naturally, it was to cultivate this barren little island.

"I'm counting on you." Johan said with a smile.

The six heads of the two Dugtrio looked at each other again, then surveyed the area, scanning this island sitting in the vast ocean.

"Trio trio trio!"

The Dugtrio were very "professional." After understanding their "work scope," they buried their heads and began cultivating.

"Bangi..."

Tyranitar sat to the side, looking somewhat listless.

I thought this cultivation work was mine...

Johan glanced at it, his smile unchanged.

Let Tyranitar do the cultivation?

Heh.

The island would either sink or completely disappear in the end.

Did he not understand his own Pokémon's nature?

"Gengar brought you lots of meteorites from space to change up your diet."

"Bangi?"

Tyranitar's eyes lit up as it rolled up from the ground, quickly looking toward Gengar.

"Ka-kaah~ヽ(●▼▼)"

Gengar, wearing sunglasses, grinned and lightly gestured beside itself. The space nearby tore open, and meteorites of various sizes came tumbling out with a "crash."

"Bangi!"

Tyranitar was overjoyed, not caring about anything else as it rushed over to grab a meteorite and stuff it in its mouth.

Crunch crunch—

"Bangi..."

Diamonds were incredibly hard, and Tyranitar's teeth had long been honed to a fearsome degree, so meteorites were naturally no problem.

However, unlike diamonds, meteorites mostly had irregular shapes—some covered in holes, some black as charcoal, others harder than diamonds and rich in rare metallic elements.

The flavors immediately became much more diverse.

"Alright, everyone say what you'd like on the island."

Johan clapped his hands, calling all the little ones over.

This island was Groudon's "gift," saving Johan the astronomical cost of buying an island, and the Hoenn League had tacitly approved that this island "belonged" to Johan.

Anyway, while this island was technically in the waters off Kanaz City, you actually couldn't see Kanaz City from standing on the island—you could only vaguely see a thick black line on the horizon.

Johan had already decided the island's general direction—farming.

But this didn't prevent the little ones from voicing their own ideas.

"Ka-kaah!"

Gengar lifted its sunglasses to its forehead and was the first to bounce up with its suggestion.

I want a hot spring!

Back in the day, both it and Johan were very fond of hot springs, but recently due to too many events, they hadn't soaked in one for who knows how long. It missed them dearly.

"This place was originally formed from cooled lava, so there's definitely still lava activity below. Setting up a hot spring... probably wouldn't be difficult." Johan nodded.

"Draaa~(ˊˋ)" Dragonite waved its small wings.

How about planting a flower field?

In Johto's "Dragon's Den," there were large flower fields, and Dragonite quite liked flowers.

"Of course no problem. Even if you didn't mention it, I'd plant the most beautiful flower field in the entire Pokémon world." Johan smiled.

He had promised Cynthia he'd show her the world's most beautiful flower field, and this promise would be fulfilled on this little island.

So the little ones spoke up one after another.

The Indeedee sister wanted to plant some coffee trees, perhaps achieving self-sufficiency for the café in the future.

Garganacl expressed that having a rocky area would be perfect, with Tyranitar and Tinkaton agreeing.

Just wondering how long the rocky area could exist with Tyranitar around...

Coach Urshifu wanted a waterfall for training.

Ceruledge felt... this island wasn't small, perhaps they could make it more lively by inviting some Pokémon to live on the island.

Mm, it would be responsible for management when free.

Hearing that many Pokémon would be invited to the island, Jigglypuff immediately suggested building a stage.

Everyone could light bonfires in the evening and enjoy beautiful songs together.

This suggestion immediately got Gengar's support—it felt Jigglypuff performing alone might be too monotonous, so it could reluctantly perform together with Jigglypuff.

Hearing this, Johan broke out in a cold sweat.

Jigglypuff and Gengar singing together?

One would put everyone to sleep after singing, the other... sleeping Pokémon probably wouldn't wake up again after it sang.

Was this a performance?

It was quite "humane" though, knowing to put them to sleep first then finish them off.

But with everyone brainstorming, they quickly enriched the island's construction goals.

However, there was actually one major problem still facing Johan and them.

Travel between the island and Kanaz City... was very inconvenient.

They couldn't completely rely on the sea bicycle, right?

So this was a problem.

Johan didn't have a good solution for now either.

There was no rush anyway, since there was still a long time before the island would be "completed."

Wait for the Dugtrio to finish cultivating the island, then scatter lots of grass seeds first to give this island some life, then worry about other things.

"Let's go, time to head back."

Johan called to the little ones.

He now had a feeling... like when he'd just bought a new rough house in his previous life, with the family looking at the bare house and planning what room this would be, what could be installed there.

How to put it...

It felt pretty good.

"Later, larger buildings can have Devon do the construction—they should be able to meet most requirements. As for some smaller ones..."

Johan suddenly looked forward to the feeling of tilling and planting the fields hoe by hoe himself.

Life would definitely be very leisurely...

Living a retired life early was what he most yearned for.

Moreover, once the island was completely perfected, calling over legendary Pokémon in the future would be much more convenient.

"Snivy, let's go." Johan called to Snivy, who was standing by the shore photosynthesizing.

"Sni!"

Snivy lifted its foot, and you could see root-like things rapidly retracting from its feet. The glow on the little one gradually faded as it leaped onto Johan's head.

Photosynthesis!

Speaking of which, the "photosynthesis" Johan had been thinking about—Snivy did it every day, just like Gengar and the others' daily training.

But the problem was this photosynthesis didn't seem to achieve the self-sufficiency level he'd envisioned for Snivy.

Even more, the longer photosynthesis continued, the bigger Snivy's appetite became.

While it hadn't reached Tyranitar's jaw-dropping level, it... was already comparable to Tinkaton.

This left Johan quite puzzled.

But fortunately, as long as it wasn't like Tyranitar, he could grit his teeth and still afford it.

After Snivy left, small grass sprouts had actually grown around where it had been standing, like down feathers, particularly tender.

"Maybe... we could have some Grass-type Pokémon come improve the environment?"

He was just about to take Eternal Floette back to the Kalos region to reunite with King AZ, and could conveniently ask Ramos for advice.

Ramos, the Gym Leader of Coumarine Gym in the Kalos region, and Yarrow of Turffield Stadium in the Galar region, were among the most skilled farmers in the Pokémon world.

He could also inquire about issues and experiences regarding Snivy and raising Grass-type Pokémon.

Two days later.

"Yiin~"

Eternal Floette danced gracefully in the café's backyard garden, circling around the lifelike "Flower Head" wooden carving, seemingly quite fond of it.

"Looks like you really like it."

Johan, dressed neatly, also came to the backyard, looking at this garden that had quickly returned to lush greenery after Groudon's departure, quite satisfied.

Eternal Floette had originally been in Sootopolis City. Johan initially planned to pick it up when going to the Kalos region.

However...

Considering that Eternal Floette had waited lonely under the tree in Sootopolis City for thousands of years, he thought to bring it out to play for a couple days before finding AZ, to get acquainted with the outside world.

"Yiin~"

Eternal Floette nodded repeatedly.

"Ready? We're about to depart."

"Yiin..."

Eternal Floette's expression froze slightly, various complex emotions flashing through its eyes before finally becoming resolute.

"Yiin!"

Looks like it had finally thought things through.

"Teacher Johan—"

Just as Johan was about to board the plane borrowed from Steven's family, a familiar shout suddenly came from outside the door.

"Hm?"

Looking toward the sound.

He saw that quite conspicuous red explosive hair, and the Infernape following alongside.

Flint?

Seeing who it was, Johan was stunned.

Why did this guy suddenly come to Hoenn?

"Finally caught up." Flint supported his knees, breathing heavily.

"Ka-kaah~"

Gengar grinned mischievously as it quietly appeared behind Flint, holding a water cup.

Hey, have some water~

Johan's expression was strange.

"Thanks." Flint didn't think at all, reaching out to take it and gulping it down, then—

"Pffft—"

He spat it out, which Gengar nimbly dodged, but it splashed Infernape instead.

"Garrr╬!"

"What the hell is that?" Flint looked at the cup in horror—the liquid inside was clearly transparent like water.

"Ka-kaah..."

Gengar rubbed its chin lightly.

Seems like it really can't be eaten...

As for what was in the cup...

Cough.

This had to do with Johan's search for Giratina, and what Gengar discovered when dumping meteorites into the Distortion World.

It found that some of the diamonds they'd left in the Distortion World for Giratina to safeguard had an unknown liquid on them.

Gengar had been very curious at the time... and tasted it, then felt something was off.

Now having Flint try it, it was indeed not edible.

Infernape wiped its face, looking quite disgusted as it wiped its hands on Flint, feeling... like it smelled of saliva.

And Johan just wanted to say—you dare eat anything Gengar gives you?

Even he would think twice.

"Why did you come to Hoenn?" Johan asked.

Wasn't Flint assigned to go to Gracidea to look for Giratina?

Could there be results?

"Hey."

Flint waved his hand.

Ruffling his hair, head tilted slightly up, "It's not a big deal."

Speaking, he rather smugly raised his eyebrows at Johan: "Teacher Johan, from now on I'll call you Teacher Johan, you call me Elite Four Flint, each of us calling our own..."

Before finishing, Flint noticed Johan looking down for something.

"What are you looking for, Teacher Johan? This Elite Four will help you find it..."

"Where's that Red Orb fragment the League gave me a few days ago?"

"What—what for?"

"Contact Groudon, have it fire a Precipice Blades this way."

Flint: Σ(дlll)

"Hey—hey, I was just joking with you, Teacher Johan." Flint quickly said.

Although he enjoyed battles and liked challenging strong opponents, but... the Groudon and Kyogre incident had made such a big commotion, Flint still had some idea of Groudon's strength.

Even having become a Sinnoh Elite Four member, facing Groudon he'd probably still get one-shotted.

Johan snorted twice.

Little brat~

Can't kill you, but can't scare you either?

"Alright, speak up, what's really going on?"

"Catching a ride on your plane. Teacher Johan, aren't you going to Kalos? Give me a lift."

"Kalos? What are you going to Kalos for?"

Finally waiting for Johan to ask this question, Flint raised his eyebrows, hands on his hips:

"Hey, some city in the Kalos region, which city was it... anyway, it's a big city holding a festival, inviting me, this Sinnoh Elite Four member, as a guest to attend and have an exhibition match."

"You?"

This time Johan was genuinely surprised.

Could the fire-wielding explosive head really be famous?

"That doesn't make sense..."

Actually inviting Flint but not him?

His status shouldn't be unable to afford an invitation, right?

"Hehe~"

Flint rubbed his nose, looking quite proud.

"So..."

Johan was starting to catch on, looking Flint up and down.

Flint immediately felt uncomfortable under Johan's gaze.

"So you came here specifically to show off?"

Otherwise why not fly directly from Sinnoh?

A proper Elite Four member shouldn't be unable to afford plane tickets, right?

Though if it were Flint, that might be questionable.

After all, he was one of the few who, like himself, was "self-made," spending all his money on Pokémon once he had any.

Moreover, Flint liked battles, inevitably consuming more on healing medicine than himself.

"How could that be?!"

Flint immediately suppressed his guilty conscience, eyes wide:

"Didn't you and big sister have me go to Gracidea to check for anything unusual? I'm here to report..."

"Oh? Then tell me, what did you discover."

"Let's... talk about it on the plane?"

Seeing his expression, Johan knew exactly what was going on, rolling his eyes irritably.

But he didn't stop him either, since...

He was also freeloading Steven's family plane, cough, ultimately not much different from Flint.

"So... you never actually went to Gracidea?"

On the plane, after listening to Flint's rambling account, Johan found the key point in his words.

"Ha—"

Flint scratched the back of his head awkwardly, "I went! I just got lost halfway, must have helped too many old ladies cross the street and lost my way."

Johan rolled his eyes irritably.

"But Lucian already went. If there's anything unusual, he definitely would have discovered it." Flint quickly added.

Johan couldn't help sighing softly.

Not because of himself, but feeling sorry for Lucian.

Lucian really... wasn't easy.

Lucian: Pouts, covers face.

"Speaking of which, Teacher Johan, you were pretty cool this time."

As they talked, the topic returned to the Groudon and Kyogre disaster, as well as the huge meteorite crisis.

These two incidents had now spread throughout all regions of the Pokémon League.

"Teacher Johan's" name, if not known by absolutely everyone, was definitely widely renowned.

Although Johan wasn't a Champion yet, many people actually already regarded him as one.

Perhaps only a region's Champion could stand up when that region was about to suffer devastating damage.

Turning the tide when it was falling, supporting the great mansion when it was about to collapse!

A Champion was nothing more than this!

Invisibly.

Johan had actually added some "pressure" to Champions from various regions.

After all, the stronger someone was, the clearer they were that what Johan could do... didn't mean Champions could do it.

At least, they couldn't call upon so many legendary Pokémon.

Kalos region, Oraure Forest.

"Speaking of which, what are you here for this time, Teacher Johan?" Flint curiously looked at the lush forest around them.

"Fulfilling a promise."

Johan said while walking ahead.

Tyranitar walked at the very front, clearing the path.

"Bangi~"

"A promise?"

"Aren't you supposed to attend a festival?" Johan didn't answer, instead glancing at him and asking back.

"Actually..." Flint scratched his head, "It's not time yet. I came a bit early."

Johan: "..."

No longer bothering with this dummy, Johan led Eternal Floette and Snivy, following behind Tyranitar toward the depths of Oraure Forest.

"Yiin~"

Eternal Floette, which had remained calm throughout the journey, obviously became much more active after entering this forest.

Perhaps even thousands of years ago, it had been anticipating this moment.

At the same time.

In the depths of Oraure Forest, in front of the tree stump that Xerneas had become, AZ sat beside the stump, eating berries and gently wiping his forehead.

Looking at the forest around him once again full of life, he couldn't help showing some smile.

Yveltal's destruction of the forest had mostly recovered under Xerneas's power, and he had done his best to help as well.

Though not much, he enjoyed it.

"Trainers..."

Leaning gently against the slope, AZ looked at the sun in the sky, his expression slightly dazed.

Hm?

AZ looked blankly at the sky. Sunlight scattered down, and a familiar yet strange figure stepped on the light path formed by sunlight, accompanied by floating petals everywhere, descending.

It was an exceptionally beautiful, sacred and pure Floette, the being of his dreams.

AZ's pupils trembled, a crystal drop falling from his unbelieving eyes.

Until Eternal Floette stood in AZ's palm and he felt that familiar touch, he realized... this wasn't a dream.

Nearby in the forest.

Johan's face showed a smile.

"Bangi..."

"Sni..."

"Draaa..."

"Ka-kaah..."

"Garruu..."

"..."

The little ones beside him also smiled warmly watching this scene.

So wonderful.

There were many beautiful things in the world, but... reunions after long separation definitely deserved a place among them.

"Don't know why." Flint sniffled, wiping his eyes, "I'm inexplicably moved."

"Let's go."

Seeing this scene was enough. Johan said softly.

"Johan!"

But just as he was about to leave with the little ones, AZ came chasing after them with Eternal Floette.

"AZ, Floette, congratulations." Johan said sincerely.

Flint gaped with his mouth open, craning his neck to look at the "giant" before him.

Earlier when AZ was sitting he didn't feel much, but now standing up...

Though Floette looked thin and weak, seemingly not very good at battling?

"Thank you, and thank your Pokémon." AZ said from the heart.

"Yiin~"

Standing on AZ's shoulder, holding flowers, Floette also sincerely expressed gratitude.

"This is the result of your own efforts. We... just did what every trainer would do."

But AZ and Eternal Floette still expressed their thanks again.

"Johan..."

After expressing gratitude, AZ hesitated before speaking.

"Hm?"

After organizing his words, AZ said: "During this time, I've thought a lot. Floette's return has strengthened my resolve. I want to open an inn with Floette."

"An inn?"

Johan was stunned.

AZ nodded, "We want to meet more trainers like you, understand trainers, and understand the relationship between trainers and Pokémon. At the same time... help trainers who need help."

"Yiin~"

Eternal Floette swayed its body, seemingly quite enthusiastic about helping others.

"That's not a bad idea." Johan said after thinking.

Hearing this, AZ sighed in relief, then continued: "But I... my identity and..."

"I understand."

Johan also understood AZ's concerns.

Obviously, even if not many people remembered the history from three thousand years ago, AZ's height was still too distinctive among ordinary people. Appearing rashly in crowds would inevitably attract unnecessary attention, even League attention.

But for Johan, this wasn't much trouble.

"I'll arrange it later."

He could still speak to the International Police and Officer Jennys.

"You choose a location and tell me. I'll handle the League side, but the money for opening the inn..."

"Don't look at me."

Flint pulled his hands out of his pockets, revealing pockets cleaner than his face.

AZ immediately smiled: "Don't worry about money. I still saved some things from before."

Johan realized.

Right.

Don't look at AZ now dressed raggedly like a wild man, but he was a king three thousand years ago.

Moreover... anything casually left from three thousand years ago would be antiques now!

Tsk...

Maybe he was the richest of the three.

"Then alright, here's my phone number. Contact me when the time comes." Johan gave AZ his contact information.

As for what a phone was... AZ wasn't so ignorant as to not know that.

"By the way, I have a gift for you." AZ suddenly said.

"A gift?"

Under AZ's guidance, the three soon came to a corner of the forest. In a place with thick tree branches, AZ pushed aside some lush foliage, revealing his so-called "gift."

An aircraft?!

"This is..."

"Left behind by that father-daughter pair." AZ explained.

Johan finally realized.

That stealth aircraft from the father-daughter thieves Argus?

This thing had been turned to stone by Yveltal's "Deathwing" back then, and no one dealt with it afterward because everyone thought it was probably broken and didn't know where it went. AZ had found it?

And the petrification had been removed.

Just didn't know if it could still operate.

Seeming to see his confusion, AZ smiled: "I've repaired it and made some improvements in places. It should... be fine now."

"Repaired? Improved?" Flint looked at the wild man-like giant before him in disbelief.

Seriously?

But Johan didn't question it at all.

Joke.

Three thousand years ago, this person had built the "Ultimate Weapon" that shocked the entire world. Current people wanting to replicate it couldn't even do it, only choosing to restart the "Ultimate Weapon."

A mere aircraft...

This was the magical aspect of the Pokémon world's tech tree.

Whether ancient, modern, or super-ancient, some technologies... were just superior.

"But the energy box should have been damaged in the crash back then. There's no fuel now, so it probably can't fly temporarily." AZ said.

Energy?

"Can it be modified to use electricity as energy?"

He didn't have much else, but electricity... plenty!

AZ smiled: "As long as it's not soda, it should be fine."

After a pause he added: "But I only have a rough understanding of this thing, so you might need to wait a while."

No problem...

He was really afraid AZ would say even cola could be used as energy...

"Then I'll trouble you."

"Small matter."

Getting a free aircraft that no one was using?

And one that could turn invisible at that.

Although the speed definitely couldn't compare to Dragonite, it won in safety.

This kind of aircraft, even with the Pokémon world's tech level, probably couldn't be gotten with eight figures.

At the same time, this solved it.

The transportation problem between himself and the island seemed perfectly solved...

After AZ finished modifying it, Johan planned to have Team Rocket's trio improve it further.

With those three's technical level... as long as funding was sufficient, they could probably perfect it to the extreme!

This way.

With both the ancient most advanced technology owner (AZ) and modern most advanced technology owners (the trio) gathered, this aircraft... maybe even Tyranitar could pilot it.

An unexpected windfall!

Wasn't this much more reliable than Z-Crystals?

Click—

Flint pressed the shutter, quickly sending the picture to the "Teacher Johan's Little Classroom" group chat.

[Elite Four Flint]: Picture.jpg

[Elite Four Flint]: Teacher Johan has made it big too. Congratulations Teacher Johan on your new ride!

# 665: Do You Have Any Slightly More Reasonable Pokémon?

Kalos region, Coumarine City.

This was a small city located in the northwestern part of the Kalos region, yet it also had a reputation as a leisure resort destination.

Ocean, mountains, and forests all coexisted here, plus the rich natural cultural atmosphere made this small city filled with a tranquil, comfortable feeling everywhere.

Spring grass and flying orioles.

On Coumarine City's vast grasslands, gentle breezes passed by, immediately stirring up green waves. Hoppip floated with the wind, eventually colliding with Cottonee in mid-air.

"How do you have time to come to Coumarine City?"

A short, elderly man wearing dark green work clothes with large shears at his waist, around fifty or sixty years old, looked cheerfully at this "big customer" before him.

While speaking, he was also trimming excess branches from a nearby Trevenant.

This person was precisely the Gym Leader of Coumarine City in the Kalos region, known as "an old tree that still blooms," Ramos!

And sitting on the grass in front of him resting was naturally Johan, along with Flint who had come along for the journey.

"Recently caught a Grass-type Pokémon." Johan smiled as he threw out a Poké Ball, summoning Snivy.

"Sni!"

As soon as Snivy appeared, it crossed its arms, glanced sideways at the smiling Johan, pursed its lips, then...

Climbed onto Johan's head.

Seeing Snivy, Ramos's eyes brightened slightly as he couldn't help but praise:

"What an excellently raised Snivy..."

Before Johan could speak, Snivy wrinkled its nose and called out to Ramos.

"Sni~!"

Even if you praise me, I won't be happy!

Then it jumped down on its own and ran to the side to photosynthesize, but seeing its body gently swaying with the grass, it was obviously in quite a good mood.

"The photosynthesis is also quite good." Ramos's smile remained unchanged.

For Grass-type Pokémon, mastering photosynthesis was very important.

"Ramos, please continue with your work. I'll ask for your guidance after you're finished." Johan said while passing his hand over his waist, summoning all the little ones.

"Ka-kaah!"

Gengar floated out from Johan's shadow, seeing the group of Sunflora not far away, its mouth corners immediately couldn't help drooling.

Slurp—

The Sunflora, who had originally been enjoying the sun contentedly, suddenly felt a chill, cold air rising from their feet to their heads.

Who?!

Which scoundrel wants to harm us?

"Garruu—"

Coach Urshifu took a deep breath, his expression becoming somewhat intoxicated.

Ah—great nature, this is the scent of bounty—

"Goka!"

Ceruledge suddenly raised the blade in its hand, pointing at two Victreebel and Vileplume arguing over a berry not far away.

Hey! Release that berry, let me handle this!

Whoosh—

Ceruledge moved extremely fast, its form becoming a streak of ghostly blue flame, flashing between the Victreebel and Vileplume.

Crack!

The plump, juicy Sitrus Berry was immediately split in half, falling into the hands of Victreebel and Vileplume respectively.

The two Pokémon stared blankly at the berries in their hands. After brief bewilderment, they became delighted.

This division was very fair!

However, before they could enjoy the berries...

Clang!

Ceruledge, with its back to them, slowly placed its blade at its waist, head tilted forty-five degrees skyward as the blade went into its sheath!

Sizzle—

A small path constructed of ghostly blue flames slowly appeared on the ground.

Seeing this scene.

Vileplume and Victreebel almost simultaneously swallowed, cold sweat slowly trickling down their foreheads.

Then...

Vileplume and Victreebel very tacitly split their respective berries in half again, sheepishly offering half to Ceruledge, "thanking" it for its "assistance."

Ceruledge politely declined briefly, then accepted this half berry, couldn't help closing its eyes and taking a deep breath.

"Goka..."

Such a familiar feeling of having face...

Of course, while his own Pokémon were "messing with" the Pokémon on Ramos's farm, naturally some Pokémon from Ramos's farm were also eyeing the Old Johan Family's, such as...

A Chesnaught that seemed to have considerable "prestige" on the farm.

After hesitating in the distance for a long time, it seemed to gather courage and walked to Tyranitar's side, who was sitting on the ground single-mindedly wolfing down food.

Shyly...

"Ches..."

Chesnaught blushed as it offered Tyranitar a pink, tender flower, with a friendly gesture.

This action.

Not only attracted the originally farm-dwelling Pokémon, but also made the Old Johan Family's little ones unable to help but look sideways.

A Pokémon actually took a liking to Tyranitar?

Johan was also quite surprised.

On one hand, he was surprised that his own Tyranitar, having evolved not long ago, seemed to have some appeal.

On the other hand, he was surprised this was actually a female Chesnaught.

After all, as the final evolution of the Kalos region grass starter Chesnaught, the ratio of male to female was... seven to one, a typical "bachelor-type" Pokémon.

Female Chesnaught were quite rare.

"Bangi?"

Tyranitar, who was stuffing meteorites in its mouth, twitched its nose, seemingly smelling the flower fragrance, and looked up at Chesnaught in confusion.

Chesnaught's expression immediately became even more shy, the blush on its face more obvious, but it didn't lower the hand holding the flower at all.

Seeing this, Tyranitar understood.

It scratched the back of its head and grinned.

"Bangi~"

Thanks~

Then "chomp" in one bite.

It ate the flower Chesnaught was holding, along with part of the stem.

Tyranitar thought: The Pokémon on this farm are really nice, knowing I was getting tired of just eating meteorites, even bringing little snacks. Mm, tastes pretty good~

Chesnaught looked at the bare stem in its hand, completely petrified.

Ate, ate it?!

Similarly witnessing the entire process, quite a few Pokémon directly stumbled, nearly falling over.

Johan also couldn't help but facepalm.

This time he didn't blame Uxie.

After all, Uxie was the "God of Knowledge," and Uxie's Claw... while making Tyranitar's intelligence points go "askew," this obviously should be the fault of Mesprit, the God of Emotion.

But looking at this situation, Tyranitar finding a partner in the future would probably...

"Come, have some tea, all grown by myself."

Ramos, having finished trimming Trevenant's branches, sat with Johan on the field ridge.

"Ka-kaah?"

Tea?

Hearing about tea, Gengar, who had been searching for something in the grass nearby, immediately raised its head and floated over first.

"Ka-kaah, Ka-kaah?"

It pointed to its own mouth with both hands.

Could you, give me some too?

"You want some too?"

So Ramos happily poured Gengar a cup as well.

Then they watched.

Ramos, Johan, and Gengar—two people and one Pokémon—sitting on the field ridge, enjoying sunshine, warm breeze, wave-like grasslands, and mellow green tea...

Peaceful times.

"How is it?" Ramos suddenly asked.

"Pretty good."

Johan liked coffee, but he wasn't completely averse to tea. If it was particularly mellow and sweet tea, he was still quite willing to try it.

"Ka-kaah..."

However, Gengar smacked its lips, shaking its head with a "no good, no good" expression.

Seeing this, Ramos wasn't angry, just smiled and asked:

"Don't like it?"

"Ka-kaah?"

Gengar waved its hand, then...

Pulled out its exclusive "tea canister" from its mouth, pinched out some, added hot water, and handed it to Ramos.

"Ka-kaah!"

Come! Try mine! This has flavor!

"Ramos..." Johan's mouth twitched as he was about to warn him, but Ramos looked quite expectant as he... blew on it and took a sip.

The next second.

Johan could clearly see Ramos's complexion change from its original healthy color to red...

"Cough." The red-faced Ramos quickly coughed twice, "Mm... good tea..."

This is way too bitter!

"Ka-kaah! (▼O▼)"

Gengar put its hands on its hips, nodding with satisfaction.

This old man... understands tea. Not bad.

"Cough cough, well, Johan, after watching for so long, do you have any feelings?" Ramos quickly changed the subject.

Johan nodded thoughtfully.

"I learned some things."

He had indeed learned some things.

For example.

While Grass-type Pokémon were called Grass-type, they actually had some branches.

Such as directly promoting plant growth, like Gogoat and Vileplume.

There were also those that assisted ecological digestion to indirectly promote plant growth, such as Trevenant, Victreebel, and Gloom—these accelerated the conversion of decaying vegetation into nutrients in the soil.

And there were Grass-type Pokémon that could produce some fruits themselves, like Sunflora, Gogoat, Tropius, etc.

These different types of Grass-type Pokémon had very different effects on farms.

Ramos smiled with squinted eyes, stroking the white goatee on both sides of his chin, nodding with satisfaction.

"I heard you have a large collection of books?" Johan asked.

"Mostly books about various farm matters, plus some of my experiences and insights..." Ramos waved his hand dismissively.

However, for Johan, this held great appeal.

"Could I... borrow some to read?"

"Of course." Ramos smiled in agreement.

After a brief pause, he added: "But before that... Johan, would you like to try a battle?"

"A battle?"

Johan was stunned.

Seeing Ramos looking healthy and rejuvenated, even becoming somewhat excited, Johan couldn't help but look at Gengar questioningly:

Did you put stimulants in your Revival Herb tea?

Gengar shrugged.

No way.

It was pure Revival Herb tea, just made by grinding Revival Herb into powder. One sip refreshes the mind, two sips never tire, three sips grants immortality! Yeah!

Johan: "..."

"Don't you also want to ask about some insights regarding Grass-type Pokémon, or Snivy specifically?"

Ramos said.

"In Pokémon raising, or Pokémon battling, and hard power, this old man definitely can't compare to you..."

"But honestly, when it comes to just Grass-type Pokémon, this old man thinks he has some insights."

That was true...

Ramos's age... was probably similar to Professor Oak and Elite Four Agatha.

While his strength might not be particularly outstanding, but... having conscientiously served as Coumarine Gym Leader for decades, managing such a large farm, saying he had no skills would be impossible.

Moreover.

Collecting others' experiences in Pokémon raising was definitely not wrong.

"Pokémon battles are always the best way to test everything."

As Ramos stood up, a Gogoat had already quite tacitly run to his side.

"An elder's invitation—naturally I wouldn't dare refuse." Johan also stood up, calling: "Snivy."

"Sni!"

Snivy immediately came to Johan's side, looking at Ramos across from them and the robust Gogoat beside him, its little eyes slightly brightening.

This was a formidable opponent!

Since it was just sparring and sharing experiences, there weren't any particularly strict rules—just a simple one-on-one.

Flint served as temporary referee.

Gogoat VS Snivy.

"Since that's the case, let this old man attack first." After Ramos finished speaking, he immediately gave commands.

"Old buddy, Grassy Terrain!"

Bang!!

Ramos's Gogoat raised its front hooves high, then landed lightly.

Buzz—

A emerald green energy immediately spread outward from Gogoat as the center. The already green grass seemed covered with a layer of emerald fluorescence, with wisps of energy floating up.

[Grassy Terrain: Pokémon on the field can receive the terrain's blessing at regular intervals, recovering stamina while also boosting the power of Grass-type moves.]

"Sni!"

Snivy squinted, trying hard to memorize the scene of Gogoat using Grassy Terrain.

Another move it hadn't learned, and it looked quite useful... even it felt a faint boost in power.

Of course.

The Gogoat using this move naturally gained a much greater boost.

Not only because Gogoat was the user of Grassy Terrain, but also because... Gogoat's ability was "Grass Pelt."

[Grass Pelt: When a Pokémon with this ability is on Grassy Terrain, its Defense increases by 50%!]

Indeed.

As Grassy Terrain spread, the already dense leaf-like green fur on Gogoat's back quickly grew again, giving it a considerable defensive boost.

But for Johan and Snivy, this was actually good news.

At least Gogoat's ability wasn't "Sap Sipper," otherwise there would be no point in fighting at all.

"Snivy, Leer." Johan also gave commands.

"Sni! (#皿)"

Snivy's body curled slightly, like a snake ready to strike, its eyes glaring at Gogoat, bringing its increased physical defense back to normal levels.

At the same time, Snivy's pupils revealed the coldness of being targeted by a snake.

Ramos smiled slightly.

"Gogoat, Grass Slide!"

In an instant.

Gogoat, which had been some distance from Snivy, actually rode the lush grass like surfing, rushing toward Snivy at extremely high speed.

So fast that in the blink of an eye, it was already in front of Snivy.

[Grass Slide: When used on Grassy Terrain, this move's priority +1]

A priority move!

As everyone knows.

In Pokémon battles, move priority was a very unreasonable hidden attribute.

Although in the real Pokémon world, priority wasn't exaggerated to the point of directly determining turn order, it could still largely determine advantages and disadvantages.

Johan quite liked having Tinkaton use Fake Out, a priority +1 move, as an opening.

However.

When Gogoat confidently rushed to Snivy's front at high speed, what greeted it was Snivy's suddenly raised... disdainful, proud, cold gaze.

"Sni!"

Snivy sent out two vines, braced against the ground, and directly lifted its body up!

"Hm?"

Ramos was stunned.

This... could a priority move be dodged so easily?

Pat—

Snivy landed lightly, vines retracting. Though it was a little one shorter than Gogoat, at this moment it gave Gogoat the feeling of... looking up at a queen...

Queenly presence?

Did Snivy, this type of Pokémon, have this ability?

Whether Ramos or Gogoat were clearly somewhat confused.

And Johan was... already quite familiar and accepting of this.

Our little tsundere having some queenly presence—what's wrong with that?

Totally normal!

"Snivy, Quick Attack!"

"Sni! (`ε´)"

Time for my counterattack!

Snivy's speed instantly reached its peak, while also gaining further speed boost through Quick Attack.

In terms of speed, this was Snivy's advantage, so naturally it had to maximize its own advantages.

"Gogoat, Razor Leaf!"

But Ramos, worthy of being Kalos region's eldest Gym Leader, quickly recovered after brief confusion and made the most correct command.

Rustle rustle rustle—

Gogoat's body swayed slightly, immediately sending out emerald green leaves wrapped in fluorescence from its back.

But these sharp leaves didn't shoot out, just circled around its body, forming a barrier.

This was Ramos and his Gogoat's specialty move.

In the original series, when Ash challenged Ramos, Frogadier's moves were easily countered by Gogoat's technique.

But Johan wasn't Ash, and Snivy wasn't Frogadier.

"Vine Whip." Johan half-closed his eyes.

Whoosh—whoosh—

Snivy ran while watching the barrier formed by Razor Leaf, while also sending out Vine Whip.

In its view, Gogoat's technique... coincided with its understanding of certain moves.

However, this was still a battle.

"Release it!"

Seeing Snivy still trying to break through the Razor Leaf "barrier" with Vine Whip, Ramos took advantage and counterattacked, seizing the gap when Snivy was attacking!

Whoosh—

In an instant.

The original protective "barrier" immediately became an emerald leaf tornado, sweeping toward Snivy.

Obviously, Ramos and Gogoat's signature move combined offense and defense!

Bang!!

Gogoat's Razor Leaf hit Snivy before Snivy's Vine Whip could connect.

The little one was sent flying.

Ramos was indeed experienced... Johan thought, but wasn't too worried about Snivy.

Because at the last moment before being hit by Razor Leaf, Snivy had still managed to retract part of its vines with its extremely fast reflexes, blocking the biggest impact of the Razor Leaf "tornado."

Moreover...

As fellow Grass-type Pokémon.

The damage wasn't very high.

But...

"Sni!! (▼皿▼)"

The flying Snivy immediately got back up, looking fierce.

It actually got sent flying!

Since following Johan, it had good food and drink every day, training hard—it wasn't like it had made no progress at all. Moreover...

Snivy raised its hand.

A small cluster of emerald fluorescence appeared in its hand!

Looking carefully, one could clearly see countless leaves forming a small tornado inside.

Then it threw it out—

Becoming a surging leaf tornado!

Leaf Storm!

Hm?

This time.

Not just Ramos, even Johan was somewhat surprised.

Because in his [Pokédex], Snivy clearly didn't know Leaf Storm, but when he looked again... "Leaf Storm" was clearly listed in the [Learned Moves] section.

Learned it at this moment?

No!

Johan quickly noticed something different.

It seemed Snivy's Leaf Storm also contained other moves...

It was Razor Leaf!

Gogoat used Razor Leaf to form a tornado, so Snivy used Razor Leaf to create Leaf Storm?

For a moment.

Johan was somewhat confused.

Was this still the Snivy he remembered—one with perhaps average talent but quite hardworking and a bit tsundere?

Leaf Storm + Razor Leaf—this was "mediocre talent"?

More importantly...

Johan also noticed that behind Snivy, two light green orbs faintly appeared, with glimmering green light flowing from them into the Leaf Storm...

"This is..."

Johan's heart trembled, then his expression became even more confused.

Kyogre's Origin Pulse?!

No, Origin Pulse was a Water-type move, and this was clearly Grass-type energy, so... it used its own way to understand Origin Pulse, then made improvements to suit itself?

This learning ability... wasn't inferior to their Gengar, was it?

No wonder, no wonder Snivy clearly photosynthesized every day, but its food consumption still didn't decrease...

Good heavens.

Did Tyranitar's "Uxie's Claw" get put on you instead?

Boom!!!

The massive Leaf Storm swept out, directly enveloping Gogoat, then... similarly sending it flying.

"Sni!"

Snivy put its hands on its hips, head tilted up slightly, looking down at Gogoat with its gaze.

How's that?

"Cough..."

Ramos raised his hand to stop Gogoat, looked at Snivy across from him, then at the calm-faced Johan.

No wonder... no wonder others said Teacher Johan liked to "suppress evolution" in Pokémon to maintain baby forms. Larvitar evolving directly into Tyranitar to face Groudon head-on, and this Snivy... probably wasn't far behind.

"Johan..." Ramos said slowly.

"Do you have any slightly more reasonable Pokémon?"

With such a Snivy... you're here asking for guidance?

This old man should be asking you for guidance instead!

Johan: "..."

This time it really can't be blamed on me—I'm also a "victim"...

Flint on the side laughed heartily: "Ramos, you'll get used to it. Teacher Johan's Pokémon are like this."
