# 685: Experience Proves Truth! (Two-in-One Chapter)

Glastrier!

Calyrex had just entrusted Johan with capturing its two beloved horses, and Glastrier, representing ice and snow, appeared before his eyes on its own.

They didn't even need to use "Ice Radish."

It saved effort, though it was somewhat unexpected.

"Neighhhh——"

Glastrier neighed and stepped forward happily toward those standing ice blocks, not really thinking about how these seemingly delicious ice blocks had suddenly appeared in this place that usually only had grassland.

However, when Glastrier got closer, it finally saw the figures behind those translucent ice walls.

Hmm?

Not the Butterfree colony?

After a brief moment of confusion, anger rose in Glastrier's heart.

How dare they touch my food in my territory?

In Glastrier's view, the tender grass in this grassland was naturally its exclusive domain, territory it had claimed after competing with Spectrier.

As for how to determine whether Johan and the others came to steal its grass...

Need you ask?

Such delicious grass was rare in the vast Crown Tundra. The Butterfree were fine—they were "guarding" the grassland for it. But this group of suddenly appearing Pokémon, especially that human, weren't they here to steal food?

Just humans setting foot in its territory was something Glastrier couldn't accept.

Sensing the hostility from Glastrier, Johan's Pokémon immediately became alert.

"Neighhhh——!"

Glastrier raised its front hooves high, its already snow-white body looking even more crystalline.

Starting a direct attack without any discussion?

No wait.

The two sides hadn't even exchanged a single word!

However, facing the incoming attack, Johan wasn't panicked. He grabbed the eager Gengar by the spike on its head, then shouted:

"Tinkaton!"

With Gengar's current strength, even without borrowing Mega Evolution or similar enhancement methods, wrestling with the "third-tier legendary" Glastrier should be no problem.

Even with the blizzard's assistance, combined with Mega Evolution and Johan's commands, beating up Glastrier should... also be no problem.

But since they already had a relatively reliable ace in the hole, shouldn't they let other Pokémon practice with this opportunity?

Everyone was fired up inside.

As soon as he finished speaking.

"Cha!!"

A huge hammer came spinning out from behind Johan, directly smashing through a standing ice wall and flying toward Glastrier.

Whoosh—Bang!!

Though Glastrier was a horse, its biggest weakness was slow speed.

The hammer hit Glastrier square in the face, striking the ice crystal mask it wore with a crisp sound.

Glastrier, which had reared up on its hind legs, also became briefly rigid at this moment.

Fake Out!

Already slow, combined with a priority move...

Seizing the initiative!

However, while Glastrier's weakness was slow speed, its advantage was outstanding defenses, combined with the blizzard's physical defense boost for Ice-type Pokémon...

The damage dealt wasn't significant at all.

But it was enough.

For Johan and his Pokémon, who were rich in battle experience, this firmly seized the initiative and advantage.

"Urshifu, Coach!"

"Ceruledge, Bitter Blade!"

"Tyranitar, Rock Slide!"

Three commands fired out like bullets from Johan's mouth in steady succession.

The three Pokémon acted as if they already knew what to do, as if they already understood what commands Johan would give, starting to move before his words had completely finished.

"Garruu~zzZ"

Urshifu, with a snot bubble, called out lowly, but a mysterious aura spread out from it as the center. Tinkaton, Ceruledge, and Tyranitar all seemed to be inspired, their momentum rising as their Attack and Defense abilities were significantly boosted.

Whoosh—

Ceruledge flashed and disappeared from Johan's side. A blue-black arc of light swept through the pale air, quickly crossing the distance between their side and Glastrier.

Sizzle!!

A tiny blue flame flickered briefly on Glastrier's body, as if extinguished by the wind and snow, but after a brief moment, the flames suddenly blazed up. No matter how fierce the wind and snow, that blue flame clung like a bone maggot, burning freely.

Ceruledge's figure also reappeared in the snow behind Glastrier, glancing coldly at Glastrier before turning around and completely disappearing into the blizzard.

At the same time.

As Ceruledge swept past Glastrier, a huge rock came from nowhere, accompanied by a "Bangi" roar, arriving almost in perfect timing with Ceruledge.

Bang!!

The massive rock struck Glastrier squarely on the head.

"Neighhhh!!!"

Glastrier, which had been preparing to retaliate, was hit by this series of attacks before it could make any significant moves, truly seeing red with fury.

"Tsk."

Johan clicked his tongue.

Rock Slide hit, but it didn't flinch Glastrier again.

This luck... he was used to it by now.

Buzz—

A massive ice spear formed almost instantly. Glastrier, having recovered from Fake Out's cowering state and feeling tremendous pain, changed its neighing tone and immediately prepared to counterattack!

The enormous ice spear hung suspended at an angle, its point aimed directly at Johan!

Though Glastrier was angry, as someone who had followed Calyrex and galloped across this snowfield for a thousand years, having seen quite a few trainers large and small, it clearly understood that in this situation, the human was its greatest enemy.

So it directly ignored the several Pokémon that had attacked it, locking onto Johan as its target.

Whoosh—

The ice spear broke through the air with bone-chilling cold.

Icicle Crash!

But facing this massive ice spear, Johan stood in place without even moving.

The next moment.

A figure carrying fierce winds swept out from behind him, directly facing the ice spear and throwing a punch!

Boom!!!

Crack crack crack—

The ice spear's downward diagonal thrust stopped abruptly, even producing harsh scraping sounds.

"Garruu!!"

Bang!!

With a furious shout, the massive ice spear shook violently. A huge crack actually appeared on its solid surface, then it completely shattered, turning into countless fragments of various sizes that scattered down.

Glastrier was stunned. Its gaze passed through the falling ice crystals and snowflakes to see Urshifu slowly raising its head and a pair of now-opened, extremely sharp eyes!

That gaze made Glastrier's heart suddenly jump in alarm.

Whoosh whoosh whoosh—

Suddenly, a hammering sound came to its ears. It seemed to sense a threat and quickly turned to look.

It saw a metal hammer, already huge, growing larger and closer in its vision!

Gigaton Hammer!

Bang!!

The heavy hammer struck directly down. The terrifying force actually made Glastrier, already known for its strength and endurance, stagger heavily, its head nearly buried in the snow.

Boom!!

A terrifying shockwave spread out with Glastrier as the center. The ground beneath its feet suddenly collapsed and sank, with cracks spreading densely.

"Neigh, neigh..."

Glastrier neighed in pain, but before it could finish venting, the sound stopped abruptly.

Because numerous rock spikes rose from underground, perfectly positioned against it as it was being hammered down.

These two forces, one from above and one from below, almost made it into a sandwich.

Was Glastrier stronger in blizzard weather? But in blizzard weather, were Johan's Pokémon weak?

You have to know.

From the very beginning, Johan had established a tactical system centered on Ninetales's Snow. Tinkaton, Urshifu, Ceruledge, and even Tyranitar—which one hadn't long since become accustomed to and adapted to snowy conditions?

Even utilizing and borrowing from snowy weather was part of their daily training.

Secondly.

Steel-type Tinkaton, Fighting-type Urshifu, Fire-type Ceruledge, and Rock-type Tyranitar—which one didn't completely overwhelm Ice-type Glastrier in terms of type matchups?

Ice-type had four weaknesses total: Fighting, Rock, Steel, and Fire. They had assembled all of them at once.

Not to mention the synergy between the four Pokémon under Johan's coordination, their mutual understanding bringing benefits far beyond simple four-on-one.

How many hits had Glastrier taken after using just one move?

Even if each hit wasn't particularly fatal, which one could be completely ignored?

However, at this moment, Glastrier was truly beside itself with rage.

This was intolerable!

"Neighhhh!!"

Wind and snow swirled, air currents spun, bloodshot eyes filled its icy crystal pupils, and an unrestrained, wild horse's violent aura was displayed without reservation.

Thrash!!

Glastrier directly started galloping, no longer caring who its target was, just charging and ramming completely without any strategy.

Johan's eyes grew cold, but he relaxed slightly in his heart.

Going wild wasn't scary—what was scary was going wild with brains. This kind of move similar to Outrage just looked fierce.

After weathering it, the outcome would be decided.

"Urshifu!"

And weathering it was undoubtedly Coach's "specialty"!

"Garruu!"

Taking a step forward, snow exploded under its feet. Urshifu took a stance and flashed in front of the angry Glastrier, facing its completely unstructured ramming without fear.

Detect!

Blocking with fists, lifting knees, sweeping, crouching—all movements flowed like water in one continuous motion, yet it managed to parry Glastrier's charging and kicking attacks without letting a single one through.

Even.

After becoming familiar with Glastrier's habitual movements and adapting to its attack rhythm...

"Close Combat!"

With Johan's command, Urshifu began counterattacking.

Directly getting up close to Glastrier, parrying while striking back.

Bang bang bang bang—

The sounds of collision were endless.

Bang!!!

With Urshifu's final punch colliding with Glastrier's head charge, Urshifu's feet carved two furrows in the snow, while Glastrier also backed up some distance on all fours.

Urshifu was temporarily in a state where its old strength was spent and new strength hadn't yet emerged, while Glastrier was slightly better, but...

Urshifu wasn't alone—Glastrier was just one!

"Bangi!!"

Tyranitar spread its arms and roared, thick rock pillars piercing up from beneath Glastrier again.

"Bangi?"

Seeing this scene, Tyranitar scratched its head.

Eh?

In this snowy ground... it actually couldn't summon magma?

It had actually wanted to use Precipice Blades, but it turned into Stone Edge instead...

Johan also glanced at Tyranitar, gaining some understanding in his heart.

In the vast snowy sky, extremely cold land, frozen tundra, and high altitude, Tyranitar had deficiencies in this move. This gave them a new direction for strengthening moves and abilities.

So.

Real combat was the best way to test one's shortcomings.

Wasn't this exactly the necessity of battles in certain situations?

Of course, discovering shortcomings was one thing—it wouldn't have too much impact on Johan's command of this battle or his Pokémon's conduct of this fight.

Any one of Tinkaton, Urshifu, Ceruledge, and Tyranitar individually might not be a match for Glastrier in a blizzard without going all out or using Mega enhancements.

But if they couldn't take down Glastrier working together, then in Johan's words...

All these years of training would have been wasted!

The massive resources he'd invested, the enormous effort he'd spent, the dangerous incidents he'd been involved in—wouldn't they all be useless?

Boom!!

Glastrier's Thrash hadn't ended. Its physical defense was indeed strong—after being impacted by Urshifu's Close Combat, Tinkaton's Gigaton Hammer, and Tyranitar's Stone Edge, it could still forcefully rage.

The huge rock spikes shattered with a crash. The furious Glastrier didn't care about anything else and directly locked onto Tinkaton, who was closest to it.

It snorted heavily, large amounts of white mist emerging from its nostrils.

However, at this moment, Glastrier suddenly froze.

Because in that vast blizzard, it saw a spark that suddenly appeared, looking particularly conspicuous in the hazy wind and snow.

That feeling was like suddenly seeing an extremely bright star in the pitch-black night sky—surprising.

Moreover, this spark rapidly grew larger, and a scorching heat arose.

Heat?

In a place like Crown Tundra, there was actually hot air?

Especially in such a blizzard...

Soon, Glastrier understood the reason.

It saw an extremely hot golden-red fireball transform from a small spark in the blink of an eye, instantly reaching its vicinity.

Behind the massive firelight.

Was a Pokémon clad in golden armor, carrying a thick cannon barrel, with fire blazing in its eyes.

Armarouge!

That cannon barrel spewed flames, the heat actually burning a brilliant vacuum zone in the wind and snow!

Heat waves surged forward.

Wasn't Glastrier supposed to have high physical defense in heavy snow?

Try taking this Armor Cannon!

Boom!!

In an instant, the golden-red massive fireball completely swallowed Glastrier. The surrounding snow—both accumulated and falling—didn't even have time to turn to water before only rising white mist and dissipating water vapor remained, as if they were in a desert!

"Neighhhh——!!"

From within the flames came Glastrier's mournful cry.

You... don't play fair!!

The Butterfree, Metapod, and Caterpie on the nearby grassland all stared blankly at Glastrier, which they saw as a fearsome beast, barely able to resist under the siege of these four Pokémon.

When the flames finally dispersed.

Glastrier, lying on the charred ground, still hadn't lost its ability to battle. It neighed and roared, trying to stand up again.

"Outrageous..." Johan shook his head.

It really was outrageous.

Reasonably speaking, after such an unreasonable combination attack from his team, how could an Ice-type Pokémon withstand it?

Even a Champion-level Pokémon would be the same.

But legendary Pokémon... sometimes were just this unreasonable.

Fortunately.

Glastrier's struggling attempt to stand stopped.

Because a black cannon barrel emanating heat was already pressed against its forehead.

"Goka!"

Armarouge's eyes burned with flames, but its expression was quite stern.

Buzz buzz buzz—

Flames gathered in the cannon barrel once again, faintly accompanied by aura power, condensed but not released, looking like it was accumulating an even stronger move.

"Cha!"

Tinkaton shouldered its massive, heavy metal hammer, swishing its twin tails, baring its teeth and grinning as it appeared at Glastrier's side.

Joining it was Urshifu, with sharp eyes, feet positioned front and back, fists raised and elbows bent, its fur flowing upward from bottom to top.

"Garruu!"

"Bangi——!!"

Tyranitar in the distance pounded its chest, and at both its feet and Glastrier's feet, wisps of sand were flowing, as if they could turn into a sandstorm sweeping this place at any moment.

Gulp—

Glastrier swallowed lightly.

A drop of cold sweat slid down its forehead.

This... are they going to finish me off?

Kicked an iron plate?

The last time it was beaten this thoroughly... was probably when Calyrex was still around, right?

Johan looked at the Luxury Ball in his hand and thought... better not waste it.

He walked forward.

Due to the earlier battle, it wasn't so cold here anymore.

He wore a smile on his face, glanced at Ninetales, and Ninetales immediately understood, using its tail to produce an Ice Radish from who knows where.

When it saw the Ice Radish, Glastrier, who had been looking fierce and angry just moments ago, immediately stared wide-eyed, as if it would start drooling the next second.

It completely forgot it had just been beaten up and was currently being "threatened."

No wonder.

Since Calyrex fell asleep and Freezington's residents gradually forgot about worship and forgot about Calyrex, how long had it been since it had eaten Ice Radish?

It had almost forgotten that delicious taste.

Seeing Glastrier's appearance, Johan couldn't help but be amused.

This Glastrier might actually be a foodie...

"We mean no harm..."

Having just said this, facing the pitiful Glastrier, Johan still stopped mid-sentence.

After beating someone up like this, saying such things, even if true, was somewhat inappropriate.

"I represent Calyrex in seeking you."

Calyrex?

Hearing this, Glastrier reluctantly shifted its gaze from the Ice Radish. If not for being pinned down right now, it would have pounced on it to eat.

But regarding Calyrex, Glastrier's feelings were somewhat complex.

"As long as you cooperate with me, I have quite a few more Ice Radishes."

As Johan spoke, Ninetales produced several more Ice Radishes, and Glastrier's eyes immediately became even more focused.

Cooperate?

If before being beaten, asking Glastrier to "cooperate" wouldn't be possible with just a few Ice Radishes.

But after being beaten, then bringing up Calyrex's name, and finally the crowning Ice Radishes...

After Glastrier felt Armarouge and the other Pokémon slightly loosen their restraints, it stood up and snorted loudly through its nose to express some displeasure.

But facing the Ice Radishes...

Under the watchful and wary eyes of the Pokémon, Glastrier ran to Johan and began eating eagerly.

Delicious!

How long had it been since it ate these?

Glastrier felt like its tears were about to fall.

Back then, although following Calyrex meant losing freedom, it also enjoyed endless Ice Radishes under Calyrex's care—eating a hundred or so a day was common.

Glastrier was warlike with a rough personality, unable to resist challenging powerful opponents when facing them.

But when facing truly powerful beings stronger than itself, it would restrain itself, just like when it once submitted to Calyrex.

Isn't this just cooperation?

Should have said so earlier!

Glastrier "comforted" itself in its heart that this was voluntary cooperation, not being beaten into submission, and ate even more enthusiastically.

"Eat up, I have plenty more."

Seeing Glastrier hesitate when reaching the last Ice Radish, Johan said with a smile.

"Neighhhh?"

More?

Glastrier's eyes immediately brightened—this information became the last straw that broke the yak (crossed out) white horse's back.

"Try some other things too."

Speaking, Johan took out several energy cubes made by Ninetales. Under Glastrier's suspicious gaze, after it swallowed them, it...

"Neighhhh——"

Glastrier suddenly reared up on its hind legs, unable to contain its inner joy and excitement.

These energy cubes contained the taste of Ice Radish, plus many other flavors that surprised it. This... was no less impressive than pure Ice Radish?

This human...

Johan showed a serious expression, placed a box of energy cubes and several Ice Radishes on the ground, then stepped back and said:

"Now you have two choices. One is to cooperate with me, and these foods are yours, with more to come in the future. Two is—"

Before he finished.

Gengar, wearing sunglasses and clenching its fists, floated out from behind Johan ready to back him up.

Only to find Glastrier had already lowered its head to eat what was on the ground, completely ignoring the second choice.

Johan laughed despite himself.

Glastrier wasn't stupid.

It was just cooperation, not capture—if Johan had thrown out a Poké Ball just now, it wouldn't have been so compliant. Moreover...

It really was delicious.

Soon.

The energy cubes in the box and the Ice Radishes were swept clean by Glastrier.

It still looked unsatisfied, occasionally glancing longingly at Johan.

Seeing this made Johan's mouth twitch.

This horse absolutely cannot be carelessly fed!

He pretended not to see and walked toward the Butterfree in the grass.

Aura exists within the heart!

"Would you be willing to come with me? I can provide you with a safe, stable, comfortable living environment."

Through aura, Johan conveyed his meaning.

His island was still developing. When it was eventually planted with numerous plants and flowers, it would inevitably need Pokémon like butterflies and bees to help with pollination and such.

The Caterpie didn't understand, and the Butterfree looked at each other, finally turning to their leader.

"You don't need to give me an answer now. I'm not ready to leave Crown Tundra yet either. When I'm about to leave, I'll come find you again."

Speaking, Johan left some energy cubes and food again before waving goodbye.

Give them some time to think.

As for Glastrier...

Bring it along.

Since they could beat it once, they weren't worried about it acting up again, especially since they had a grip on its stomach.

"Ka-kaah?"

On the way back.

Gengar floated beside Johan, looking at Glastrier following not far away with an excited expression.

Why not ride back?

How majestic that would be!

Such a magnificent white horse—what a waste not to ride...

Johan glanced at it and said with suppressed amusement: "You can try."

"Ka-kaah!"

Gengar had been waiting for Johan to say this.

Then it somehow produced an Ice Radish and immediately floated toward Glastrier.

Soon after.

"Ka-kaah!! o(TヘTo)"

Gengar's somewhat piercing cry echoed through the vast blizzard, startling the Ice-type Pokémon in the snow into thinking there was a snow ghost.

It was seen with tears in its eyes, clutching its crotch, diving back into Johan's shadow in a flash.

"Neighhhh——"

Glastrier nearby snorted gloatingly.

Johan and his Pokémon exchanged glances, then couldn't help but burst out laughing.

"Pff—hahaha—"

Glastrier was just cooperating, not captured. Moreover, without "Reins of Unity," it was inherently difficult to capture. Did Johan really not want to experience riding Glastrier?

Even Calyrex needed to rely on "Reins of Unity."

To make Glastrier truly cooperate.

They still needed to craft "Reins of Unity" first.

Returning to Freezington.

Compared to the snowfield, Freezington was much less affected by the blizzard due to its geographical location.

However, because of the blizzard, the already sparsely populated Freezington seemed even more desolate. Johan brought his Pokémon straight to the mayor's house.

"This, this, this is..."

The mayor who opened the door was completely shocked when he saw Glastrier beside Johan.

Freezington had lost the legends about Calyrex, but because Glastrier was still active in the snowfield and had even become a dangerous existence that Freezington had to guard against, the mayor immediately recognized this seemingly harmless white horse as the legendary Glastrier!

"Met it on the road, chatted for a bit, got acquainted, so I brought it back."

"Chat, chatted for a bit?" The mayor stared blankly at the magnificent Glastrier behind Johan.

Glastrier immediately snorted irritably, showing no good face to the mayor, its fierce look flashing briefly.

It was willing to cooperate with Johan because Johan had strength, background, and food.

Johan lightly patted Glastrier's neck twice to calm it.

"Mayor, I have something I'd like your help with," Johan said.

"Oh, oh..."

After the mayor fearfully glanced at Glastrier again, he came to his senses and quickly responded.

"Come, come inside."

"Speaking of which, Mayor, have you seen Flint? The red-haired explosive head who came with me." Johan noticed Flint wasn't at the mayor's house.

Mentioning Flint, the mayor relaxed somewhat, also showing a smile and some helplessness:

"That young man is a good kid. The villagers said there were Pokémon sightings at the village outskirts, and I was going to check it out when he volunteered to go himself."

The blizzard still affected the village, especially with some Ice-type Pokémon that became active during blizzards.

With Flint's personality, the mayor couldn't have stopped him even if he tried.

"I hope nothing serious happens."

Johan understood. "I see."

He waved his hand: "Don't worry, Mayor. That guy... will be fine."

With Flint's strength, even if he encountered Glastrier or Spectrier, he definitely wouldn't be afraid. Ordinary Ice-type Pokémon... couldn't trouble him.

As long as he didn't get lost.

The mayor nodded, seeming to have a new understanding of both their strengths after witnessing Johan bringing Glastrier.

Darmanitan brought Johan a cup of hot water.

"Thank you." Johan smiled and thanked it.

The two sat by the fireplace to warm up.

The old mayor also took a water cup from Darmanitan's hands, saying with some emotion:

"I found this child injured in the mountains and brought it back. I intended to let it leave on its own after healing, but this child refused to go and ended up staying with this old man."

Darmanitan seemed to hear the mayor talking about it, showing an embarrassed smile and scratching its head.

As a result, it scratched down some snow and quickly picked up a broom to sweep it away.

Johan watched this scene with a smile.

Pokémon were just like this—whoever treated them well, they could truly feel it and would repay it tenfold or a hundredfold.

The friendship and bonds between humans and Pokémon were built up bit by bit like this.

The mayor chatted with Johan for quite a while, perhaps because he hadn't had anyone listen to him for so long that he couldn't seem to stop.

Johan didn't interrupt, just listened quietly, occasionally agreeing, which would earn him the elder's simple smile.

"Look at me, didn't you say you needed my help with something earlier?" The mayor finally remembered, slapping his forehead somewhat embarrassedly.

Johan didn't mind, just saying:

"I'd like the mayor to help me make two reins."

"Reins?"

The old mayor was stunned.

Then he slowly said:

"This was originally a craft that everyone in Freezington mastered, but I don't know when people stopped making them. If not for my grandfather's teaching and insistence that I learn, I probably wouldn't know either, and this craft would have been lost..."

He didn't ask Johan how he knew about his ability to make reins.

Actually, he didn't know why his grandfather had insisted he learn to make reins back then—Freezington didn't raise horses either...

He guessed that perhaps Freezington used to have the custom of raising Mudsdale.

However, the old mayor looked troubled again:

"I don't know what kind of reins you want? The village doesn't have many material choices..."

Johan took out two "Radiant Petal" petals.

Then he looked at Gengar, who was huddled by the fireplace, warming its bottom by the fire.

"Gengar."

"Ka-kaah~"

Gengar casually produced a tuft of "Black Mane."

Then it took out scissors, grinning wickedly as it passed through Johan, went through the wall, and floated outside.

This old ghost's crotch wasn't so easily frozen!

Soon.

"Neighhhh!!!"

Glastrier's "pitiful" neighing came from outside.

Then Gengar floated back in holding a tuft of snow-white mane.

Looking at the materials in his hands, the old mayor was stunned.

"These, these, these materials..."

He swallowed and said:

"The reins you want to make, they wouldn't be 'Reins of Unity,' would they?"

"The mayor indeed knows." Johan said.

The old mayor opened and closed his mouth, not knowing what to say. After pondering for a long while, he asked with some disbelief:

"Could it be... the 'Guardian Deity' is real?"

Johan remained silent.

As Freezington's mayor, he no longer knew of Calyrex's existence, only referring to it as the "Guardian Deity."

No wonder Calyrex lamented the changes over time.

However, the old mayor still knew about "Reins of Unity" and had inherited the method for making them. Calyrex should find some comfort in this.

"Thank you for your trouble, Mayor."

# 686: The Dark Horse Prince! (Two-in-One Chapter)

"Cha~Cha~Cha!"

The mayor worked on crafting the "Reins of Unity" while Tinkaton learned beside him, nodding from time to time as if learning something.

It had to be said.

Although Freezington no longer had the custom of making reins, the old mayor's craftsmanship was still quite good. His grandfather must have spent considerable effort teaching him to master it.

"Phew—"

Wiping the sweat from his forehead, the old mayor handed Johan one black and one white rein. "Mission accomplished."

"Thank you, Mayor."

Johan accepted them solemnly.

With these two "Reins of Unity," the problem of Glastrier and Spectrier would no longer be a problem.

However, after receiving the reins, Johan couldn't help but have a thought.

Since Calyrex could use the "Reins of Unity" to command Glastrier and Spectrier, combining the power of two Pokémon together—which was a form of [Fusion]—even changing their abilities.

Could... other Pokémon also gain the power of the two horses by borrowing the "Reins of Unity"?

Even, what if a human held the "Reins of Unity"?

Johan looked at Ninetales and shook his head slightly.

Having Ninetales ride Glastrier would be somewhat difficult for it.

Then he looked at the muttering Gengar, involuntarily imagining the scene of Gengar riding Glastrier from earlier, and unconsciously shook his head again.

Gengar riding Glastrier looked somehow wrong, with a strange art style.

But what if... Gengar rode Spectrier?

If there was a chance, he could let Gengar try it.

"Getting old, sitting for a long time makes my whole body ache." The old mayor stood up with a smile, looking out the window with some worry. "That young man still hasn't returned..."

"Don't worry about him, Mayor."

Flint had managed to survive this long without dying—even if he got lost in Crown Tundra for ten days or half a month, Johan wouldn't worry.

Although Johan always silently "kept score" for Flint in his heart, he still had great confidence in Flint's strength.

If Flint really went all out, only Cynthia in all of Sinnoh could suppress him. He might even rival Champions in the future.

He also glanced out the window.

The blizzard was obviously much smaller than before.

But thick white snow still accumulated on the ground outside Freezington.

Johan stood up, preparing to return to Crown Temple.

First, he'd deliver Glastrier to Calyrex. With Glastrier and the "Reins of Unity," Calyrex should be able to recover some strength.

Whether they then captured Spectrier together or Calyrex captured it alone would be relatively easy. Only then could Johan ask about some things he wanted to know.

The mayor wanted to stop him.

But considering that Johan had already "tamed" Glastrier, he probably didn't need to fear any blizzard. He just told Johan to be careful.

So.

In the somewhat smaller blizzard, while the sky hadn't completely darkened, Johan brought his Pokémon and Glastrier to Crown Tundra's peak again.

Having walked this path once already, this time was much easier, and they didn't encounter any trouble along the way.

Come to think of it, with Glastrier's "dominating presence," any wild Pokémon with a brain wouldn't actively cause trouble at this time.

Before the night completely darkened, Johan arrived at Crown Temple again.

"Neighhhh——"

But upon arriving here, Glastrier became somewhat restless, neighing as if wary of something.

Hmm?

Clop clop, clop clop—

Clear, ethereal hoofbeats echoed within the temple that was covered by ice and snow with only a corner exposed.

"This is..."

"Neighhhh——" Glastrier neighed again.

"Gengar, take out a Black Radish." Johan said softly.

"Ka-kaah?"

Gengar scratched its head with a reluctant expression, carefully taking out a pitch-black radish.

Clop clop, clop clop, clop clop—

The hoofbeats inside the temple suddenly became urgent.

"Neighhhh——!!"

This cry didn't come from Glastrier beside them, but from inside the temple!

Rumble—

With the cry, the snow covering the temple suddenly collapsed partially, revealing more of the temple's structure.

Towering, majestic, ancient, dignified...

Just revealing a corner made one feel the ancient aura rushing toward them, making one imagine how spectacular this temple must have been originally.

A completely black horse with blue mane and a tail burning like blue flames, with energy like soul mist floating around its four hooves, came neighing out of the temple.

It was clearly the other of Calyrex's two beloved horses—the ghost horse, Spectrier!

It was said that after Calyrex fell asleep, both Glastrier and Spectrier lived in the temple.

During the day, Johan had thought that was just what the Pokédex said. With two beloved horses living in the temple, even if Calyrex was weak, could it not sense them?

Since he arrived at Crown Tundra, Calyrex had immediately found him, so he hadn't thought in that direction at all.

Who knew Spectrier really lived in the temple.

From this, it seemed Calyrex was indeed incredibly weak, or for some reason, unwilling to enter or even approach the temple?

No matter what.

Now Spectrier had charged out, targeting the Black Radish in Gengar's hand!

"Neighhhh——"

However, when Spectrier charged out, Glastrier had the biggest reaction—not Johan and his Pokémon—looking excited.

Johan immediately became alert.

Individual Glastrier and Spectrier were manageable, but if Glastrier suddenly turned traitor, that would be somewhat troublesome.

Of course, it was only somewhat troublesome.

Since they could pin down and beat Glastrier once, they could naturally pin it down and beat it twice!

However, Johan thought of some earlier speculations and said:

"Gengar."

This time, let Gengar handle it.

"Ka-kaah~"

Hearing this, Gengar grinned wickedly, naturally understanding Johan's meaning. In front of Spectrier, it slowly picked up the Black Radish and opened its mouth to toss it in with an "awoo."

Crunch crunch—

Fresh and juicy, crisp and sweet.

Delicious!

"Neighhhh!!!"

Seeing this scene—seeing its beloved Black Radish actually eaten by this chubby purple fatty—Spectrier instantly became furious, neighing loudly as a pitch-black orb formed before it.

Shadow Ball!

Unlike Glastrier's extremely slow speed and extremely high defenses.

Spectrier was almost completely opposite—incredibly fast speed but relatively weaker defenses.

Fortunately.

Gengar was also a Pokémon that relied on speed, a nimble little fatty.

When the pitch-black Shadow Ball came flying, it immediately dove down, disappearing from Spectrier's sight and causing the Shadow Ball to miss.

Gengar was still good at drawing aggro.

Look, even though Gengar had disappeared, Spectrier had no intention of attacking Johan and the other Pokémon. Instead, it spread Ghost-type energy, trying to find Gengar's traces.

Thin purple spirit mist spread from Spectrier's feet, as if arriving at a mysterious, eerie forest.

The mist flowed.

Spectrier suddenly turned, discovering Gengar's traces!

It immediately shot out a Shadow Ball.

Bang!!

However, Gengar, which had just appeared, dispersed like a mirage.

Spectrier was suddenly startled.

An illusion?

It quickly turned again, only to find Gengar was still in the original spot, pointing at it mockingly.

"Ka-kaah~(๑•̀ㅂ•́)ノ"

"Neighhhh!!"

Spectrier became angry, neighing as a shadow shot rapidly from its body like a lifelike Spectrier charging straight toward Gengar.

Night Shade!

Bang!

But.

When Night Shade swept past "Gengar," it again dispersed like a mirage.

Still fake?!

At this moment, the first mirage that Spectrier had destroyed quickly solidified, clearly showing Gengar with a successful smirk, slapping Spectrier's rear with a "smack!"

A purple toxic hue immediately spread across Spectrier's body.

Poison!

"Neighhhh——"

Before Spectrier could react, Glastrier behind Johan reacted instead, neighing with a terrified expression, tightening its rear and pressing its tail firmly against its rump.

This was bad.

With Spectrier's speed and natural affinity as a Ghost-type Pokémon, it was still handled like this by Gengar. It didn't know what kind of predicament it would face if confronting Gengar.

"Neighhhh!!"

Spectrier naturally didn't know what Glastrier was thinking, but the pain from the poison and Gengar's "toying" made it neigh again.

Its eyes showed malicious and cunning colors.

Nasty Plot!

Spectrier felt it had encountered the most troublesome enemy of its lifetime. That spine-chilling feeling—before, only its enemies would have such feelings. It never expected it would be its turn this time.

However, as a fellow Ghost-type Pokémon, Spectrier also clearly knew what this type of Pokémon feared most.

That was not playing any "hide and seek" games, but winning through direct attacks and brute force!

While neighing, Spectrier's aura climbed madly.

It stared intensely at Gengar, preventing it from taking advantage of this opportunity to sneak attack.

But Gengar's reaction... left Spectrier very confused.

Not stopping its enhancement?

"Ka-kaah~"

Gengar stood on one foot with the other casually dangling at its knee, as if sitting in midair, one hand picking its nose while the other waved lightly upward.

Come on, work harder, put in more effort—didn't you eat?

Spectrier suddenly had a bad feeling.

This feeling was confirmed when its aura climbed to its peak.

"Ka-kaah~!"

Come here!

Gengar grinned, eyes full of mockery, reaching out to grab. Two bat-shaped forms of black mist immediately flew from Spectrier's body.

Instantly.

Spectrier's rising aura immediately fell back.

While Gengar, holding the "bats," saw its aura climb at an even faster rate.

Its abilities had been stolen?!

How was this possible?

Spectrier's brief daze undoubtedly gave Gengar an excellent opportunity.

"Hex." Johan said softly, and Gengar acted.

A blood-red pupil opened above Gengar's head, staring intently at Spectrier. When Spectrier recovered from its shock and met that blood-red eye, it knew it was too late.

Buzz—

A muffled sound exploded from within Spectrier.

For Spectrier in a "poisoned" state, Hex's power would be doubled!

At the same time, benefiting from its Special Attack boost and the mutual resistance between Ghost-types...

The blow Spectrier suffered was nothing short of a critical hit!

Moreover, it was both physical and mental critical damage.

With this one move, Gengar completely seized absolute initiative.

Moves like Thunder Wave, Lick, Confuse Ray, and many other techniques and methods were used one after another, turning Spectrier into a walking "negative buff display machine."

Gengar also used this to verify the results of its previous training.

After absorbing a mass of complex negative emotional energy from Hoopa Unbound's "Shadow," Gengar seemed to have stronger restrictive effects when applying debuff moves to opponents.

Especially poison.

Spectrier made one wrong move, leading to a complete loss.

So in battles, information was a very crucial thing.

If it had known earlier that Gengar possessed the ability to steal opponent's boosts, it either wouldn't have used Nasty Plot, or even if stolen, it could have reacted in time instead of being briefly stunned and having its weakness exploited.

Information asymmetry could sometimes even make up for huge power differences.

This was also why Gengar could successfully suppress Spectrier without even using Mega Evolution.

In Pokémon battles in the Pokémon world, it was never fixed moves trading back and forth. There would be various variables, and no one could say they were 100% guaranteed not to lose, even Champions facing Elite Four members could still lose.

This was an important joy of Pokémon battles.

"Neigh..."

Glastrier noticed Johan's peripheral glance and immediately lowered its head, snorting softly while clamping its tail, looking like... don't look at me, I'm not a traitor, I definitely won't take advantage of this opportunity to attack.

Originally, Glastrier still felt indignant about Johan using four Pokémon to battle and suppress it. Now...

It suddenly realized.

What a good person!

This was a truly good person!

Not making it face Gengar's set of inexplicable debuff combos was simply the greatest kindness!

Now it understood Johan's "goodwill."

Of course.

While feeling apprehensive, Glastrier couldn't help feeling somewhat gleeful.

Seeing its old rival in such misery...

What lovely weather today.

"Gengar!"

Seeing Glastrier hadn't revealed its rebellious intentions, Johan smiled slightly and threw out a pitch-black rein.

Perfect timing to test this.

"Ka-kaah!"

The long-eager Gengar caught the "Reins of Unity" and appeared behind Spectrier in a flash.

"Neighhhh!!"

Spectrier neighed, seeming to anticipate what Gengar wanted to do.

Unlike the hot-tempered Glastrier that liked fighting and challenging powerful opponents.

Spectrier liked quiet, enjoying solitude and silence. Having finally enjoyed thousands of years of solitude, it had to become a mount again?

But.

No matter what Spectrier thought, it had been beaten by Gengar until it could barely fight back. How could it resist?

The familiar reins were placed around its neck again.

Buzz—

A dark, cold, obscure mist burst from Spectrier, Gengar, and the "Reins of Unity," gradually threatening to envelop both Gengar and Spectrier.

"Is it working?"

Johan, watching the entire process, half-closed his eyes with undeniable surprise.

Could this [Fusion] card really work on Gengar and Spectrier?

However, after this state continued for a while, the obscure mist slowly disappeared. Gengar rode on Spectrier's back, and neither it nor Spectrier seemed to have undergone any major changes.

"As expected."

Johan shook his head.

He wasn't particularly disappointed.

After all, this was the most likely result from his speculation.

If Gengar could really fuse with Spectrier just with the "Reins of Unity," Johan would definitely try riding Glastrier today no matter what.

What if he could really hand-cast "ice spears" or hand-grab "star fragments"?

Unfortunately, this bold fantasy was nipped in the bud starting with Gengar.

But Gengar didn't feel anything was wrong. Holding the reins and riding on Spectrier's back, at this moment it felt like the "general" it had fantasized about—no, the "king" leading troops to war!

So carefree, so mentally satisfied.

"Ka-kaah!"

I am now... the Dark Horse Prince!

Spectrier, on the other hand.

Had shown strong resistance earlier, but after the "Reins of Unity" wrapped around its neck and formed a brief energy and information exchange with Gengar, it actually became obedient.

Though it snorted unhappily, it no longer resisted.

This situation was naturally noticed by Johan and the other Pokémon, including Glastrier.

But Glastrier's current "situation" wasn't good.

It was looking warily at Tinkaton, Urshifu, and... Tyranitar, who had suddenly turned to look at it!

"Neighhhh..."

You, you, you—what do you want? Those looks are so malicious...

Especially Tyranitar.

Big brother, look at your size, look at my size—are you serious?

"Bangi~"

Tyranitar rubbed its palms together, looking eager to try, just short of borrowing the "Reins of Unity" from Johan.

Seeing Spectrier had calmed down and Gengar had "gotten its wish," Johan put away thoughts of further experiments.

"Alright, let's go find Calyrex."

He said.

Since they had captured both of Calyrex's beloved horses, the commission was complete.

The group walked toward the withered tree behind the temple.

Gengar rode Spectrier at the back. Seeing everyone had stopped paying attention to it, it carefully took out a Black Radish and fed it to Spectrier.

Only then did Spectrier snort again, its mood seeming to stabilize further.

Arriving at the withered tree.

Compared to when they came earlier, the withered tree was visibly more shriveled.

It was precisely because of worrying Calyrex wouldn't last much longer that Johan acted so quickly.

Calyrex trusted him and asked for his help. If he really delayed until Calyrex died, even with various reasons and excuses, Johan would inevitably feel guilty and self-reproachful.

Now it was good.

From request to mission completion, it took less than a day total.

He walked forward and placed his hand on the tree trunk, closing his eyes.

Aura exists within the heart!

Soon, he found Calyrex curled up deep in the trunk, its vital signs incredibly weak.

At this moment, Calyrex appeared extremely quiet, curled into a ball, completely lacking its previous kingly aura. It only had the same difficulty as ordinary Pokémon when seriously injured and weak, licking wounds alone.

Johan sighed quietly.

Becoming so weak to protect its subjects.

Fortunately, bringing Calyrex out didn't require breaking the trunk. Calyrex seemed to have fused with this withered tree, and Johan easily lifted it out.

It had to be said.

Calyrex was very light.

Really like a rabbit, equally light.

"You..."

Calyrex seemed to sense something, opening its eyes a crack to see Johan, but couldn't even speak a complete sentence.

Could it really recover just by riding the two horses again in this state?

But there was nothing else to say now. Johan immediately gave his Pokémon a look.

"Neighhhh!"

Glastrier suddenly shivered, looking at the somewhat "unkind" expressions of Johan's Pokémon.

Don't, don't look at me like that—I'm cooperating...

Glastrier could bend and stretch, compromising very decisively.

At least during those years, Calyrex had treated them well, at least providing plenty of Ice Radishes to eat.

So.

Johan personally placed the "Reins of Unity" around Glastrier's neck.

Hmm?

Just as Johan placed the "Reins of Unity" around Glastrier's neck, he suddenly felt a strange sensation.

Man and Pokémon almost instinctively looked at each other, both seeing some confusion in the other's eyes.

In that instant...

Johan had a feeling like undergoing Mega Evolution, directly communicating mentally and spiritually with the Pokémon, even...

He had a feeling that with just one thought, he could make Glastrier lift its hoof.

As if that wasn't Glastrier's hoof, but his own hand.

Commanding like his own limbs—that was probably this feeling?

While Glastrier's feeling wasn't as direct as Johan's, it had a... exactly the same sensation as when it served as Calyrex's mount.

Its own power became part of the other's power, and after being strengthened, could be used freely by the other.

Eh?

Isn't this a human?

Glastrier had a strange thought.

However, Johan didn't think too much about it. After Urshifu helped Calyrex onto Glastrier's back, he handed the reins to Calyrex.

The next second.

Buzz—

The reins automatically attached to Glastrier's neck, fitting perfectly.

A dazzling light like evolution light completely enveloped both Calyrex and Glastrier.

Watching this scene, Johan stepped back and murmured:

"Fusion!"

The light came quickly and disappeared quickly.

When the white light faded.

Calyrex sat upright on Glastrier's back, hands pulling the reins. Glastrier had also resonated with Calyrex, raising its front hooves high while neighing excitedly.

It seemed a power flowed from Glastrier through the reins into Calyrex's body. The huge crown atop its head released a green halo.

Then, its royal cape behind slowly extended, becoming pure white like snow, fluttering majestically in the wind.

Gengar nearby watched the crown-wearing Calyrex on its white horse, then looked down at Spectrier beneath it and itself, couldn't help curling its lip, then took out a pair of large sunglasses and put them on.

"Ka-kaah! (=ω=)"

A moment later, everything returned to calm.

Calyrex released one hand, turned sideways to look at Johan, its expression dignified but kind and friendly, bowing slightly.

"Johan, this king will forever remember your help."

Vigorous energy burst from its body. It seemed... to have reclaimed part of the power that originally belonged to it.

Correspondingly.

The withered tree behind Crown Temple swayed gently, similarly bursting with vitality. The shriveled trunk quickly returned to smoothness, with shoots of energy emerging from those withered branches.

Renewed life!

Indeed, as Johan had guessed.

This ancient tree behind the temple should have countless connections with Calyrex.

Somewhat similar to the Tree of Beginning and Mew.

Johan didn't immediately respond to Calyrex, just turned slightly and said:

"There's also Spectrier."

Speaking, he called to Gengar:

"Gengar, that's enough."

"Ka-kaah..."

Hearing Johan's call, Gengar drooped its ears, pulling the reins with a dejected look, driving Spectrier to slowly approach.

As someone who understood Gengar well, how could Johan not know Gengar was putting on an act again, quite the performer.

This little trick naturally couldn't fool Johan, who knew whether Gengar was going to fart or defecate just by seeing it stick up its rear. But it worked on Calyrex.

"No matter, no rush."

Calyrex's voice was serious yet gentle.

"Ka-kaah!"

Gengar suddenly raised its head, grinning—where was the dejected look from before? Excitedly pulling the reins, it took Spectrier for another ride.

Clop clop, clop clop, clop clop—

Running and running, Spectrier's feet actually began to lift off the ground, as if stepping on spirit mist, gradually running toward the sky.

Woohoo!

Only now did Gengar know Spectrier had this "function," immediately delighted and even more interested.

Johan covered his face, saying to Calyrex somewhat embarrassedly:

"Sorry, Gengar is... quite mischievous."

Calyrex looked at Gengar riding on Spectrier's back, its eyes showing some unusual colors.

It was still... the first time seeing Spectrier so "obedient" under another Pokémon's riding.

And Spectrier and Gengar...

"No matter." Calyrex shook its head slightly.

Though now far from its peak state, it had already recovered a portion.

This was enough.

Even now without Johan's help, after some recovery, capturing Spectrier wouldn't be much of a problem.

"This king originally thought it would take some time... never expected you could be so fast." Calyrex said with emotion.

Johan smiled slightly and briefly described the process of encountering and capturing Glastrier and Spectrier.

"I see..."

Calyrex gently patted the now-obedient Glastrier's neck and sighed softly.

"Unexpectedly, these two horses occupied the temple as their dwelling."

Glastrier snorted softly.

After all, though Glastrier and Spectrier had been tamed by Calyrex originally, they had also been beaten up.

After Calyrex fell into exhausted slumber, the two horses had been free for thousands of years, naturally regaining their wild nature. Not respecting their former master was inevitable.

After all, Pokémon, especially wild Pokémon, also believed in strength supremacy. Without strength, Calyrex naturally couldn't gain the two horses' recognition.

"Johan, would you like to visit Crown Temple with this king?" Calyrex suddenly asked.

Hmm?

Johan was startled.

Then smiled: "Of course."

Subsequently, Johan's group followed Calyrex into Crown Temple.

Though it wasn't the first time coming here, entering Crown Temple was truly the first time.

The temple was extremely large and spacious, and after the long passage of time plus the two horses' "damage," it was already dilapidated.

But from some broken walls and ruins, one could still see this temple must have been very magnificent originally.

Calyrex walked while introducing the temple's furnishings and arrangements to Johan.

"This was this king's favorite place. The cushions were very soft and comfortable then. This king loved lying here to rest."

"This was this king's study, originally filled with books from around the world, unfortunately all rotted now."

"Here are the stables where this king's two beloved horses were kept..."

Like reminiscing about something, and also... mourning something.

Johan could clearly feel Calyrex's emotional changes.

From initial excitement at recovering strength, to emotion at seeing the temple's decay, to melancholy at how things had changed...

Melancholy.

Not just because of time's passage, but because of humans forgetting it. The subjects it once protected had long forgotten it.

Being forgotten by those you most wanted to protect—that would hurt anyone, right?

However, Calyrex soon collected its melancholy expression, leading Glastrier to look at Johan.

"Johan, you came to find this king—you should have something to ask, right?"

Coming all the way from Hoenn to Crown Tundra in the Galar region, and helping with such a big favor, he should need its help with something.

Johan didn't act coy, looking toward the great hall.

His Pokémon were circling around an ancient, decayed, blurred, and incomplete stone tablet in the temple's great hall.

On the tablet, Snivy dangled its feet, looking thoughtful.

Following Johan's gaze, Calyrex also saw Snivy on the stone tablet and was slightly startled.

Then.

In Calyrex's eyes, a strange mystical color arose, countless light and shadow seeming to flow in its eyes.

Calyrex was called the "King of Bountiful Harvests," the "King of Galar" in ancient times, but this didn't mean its abilities were limited to "bountiful harvests."

It was said Calyrex could see all things past, present, and future.

Though somewhat exaggerated, its abilities were naturally very strong.

Calyrex first frowned slightly, then showed understanding, murmuring:

"Blessing of the Forest..."

Blessing of the Forest?

Johan was puzzled.

Calyrex had already withdrawn its gaze, saying to Johan:

"You want it to evolve? This king can do that."

"No." Johan looked at Snivy, saying softly: "Whether to evolve or not is for Snivy to decide. I'm just worried if there's something wrong with its body."

Calyrex was startled.

Let the Pokémon decide for itself?

It showed a gentle smile for the first time.

"Johan, you truly are an excellent trainer."

Johan neither confirmed nor denied this.

Just as he was about to ask Calyrex what the so-called "Blessing of the Forest" was, he heard familiar shouting from outside the temple.

"Ahhh——"

With confusion, Johan and his Pokémon rushed out of the temple, looking up at the sky.

They saw...

A large bird burning with pitch-black flames was flying overhead, and in its claws was the shouting... Flint!

Hmm?

That was...

"So it's that one..." Calyrex said with understanding.

That Pokémon burning with dark flames, surrounded by an evil aura, like the embodiment of evil, was clearly Moltres!

More precisely, Galarian Moltres!

"Too bad it's not a 'walking chicken'..." Johan sighed.
