# 690: Sunken Ship and Treasure! (Two-in-One Chapter)

"Skwo!"

Johan and his group also reached the giant tree at the center of Ballimere Lake's hill.

However, just like Moltres, as soon as they approached, a chubby Skwovet that looked like a ball immediately appeared before them and stretched out its hand to stop them.

With this stance, Johan really wanted to step forward and flick the Skwovet's nose, then arrogantly say—"Still blocking? We're here to collect you!"

But obviously, this wasn't Johan's style. Maybe if it were Flint, it might be about right.

However.

Even Galarian Moltres protected this giant tree so much that it wouldn't start a fight. Johan naturally couldn't casually provoke conflict either.

This tree had nurtured so many wild Pokémon in this area—if something really happened, wouldn't they all rise up against him?

It wasn't that he was afraid, but this went against Johan's principles and original intentions.

Moreover, he just wanted a few tree branches and to try learning more about this giant tree.

So he came over now just to say hello first.

After placing a small box of energy cubes in front of the Skwovet, he said nothing and turned to walk away.

"Skwo?"

The Skwovet tilted its head and scratched the back of its head.

It didn't understand what this human wanted to do.

But soon its sensitive nose twitched, smelling the aroma emanating from the energy cubes. Its eyes immediately lit up as it carefully picked up one cube, hesitated briefly, then licked it.

"Skwo!!"

The Skwovet suddenly shuddered, all its fur—especially the fluffy tail fur—stood on end, revealing some of the berries and treasures it had hidden inside.

It felt as if all the pores in its body had been opened.

Then the Skwovet suddenly reacted, looked around to confirm no one had noticed, then... quickly stuffed the energy cubes into its tail.

But its voice had been so loud earlier—how could other Skwovet and Greedent not notice? A whole row was already standing above it.

"Skwo..."

So this Skwovet had no choice. After secretly hiding two more cubes for itself, it distributed the remaining energy cubes with a "tragic" expression.

Honestly, these energy cubes were the most delicious thing this Skwovet had ever eaten in its life!

And it wasn't the only one feeling this way.

Soon, Johan hadn't walked far when excited exclamations from Skwovet echoed from the giant tree's canopy.

They all asked the original Skwovet where these good things came from.

It immediately pointed toward Johan.

"Teacher Johan, why did you come back?" Flint looked somewhat puzzled at Johan returning to the lakeside from the giant tree hill.

He had thought Teacher Johan would be like Moltres, paying some food as a price to gain permission to enter the giant tree's canopy and investigate.

"Let the energy cubes fly for a while."

Johan smiled.

Entering the canopy and cutting a few valuable branches were two different concepts.

Moreover, compared to the giant tree whose purpose was still unknown, Johan was more interested in the berry trees scattered everywhere.

Most of Ballimere Lake's area was plains, but there were also clusters of berry trees growing densely together.

Unlike Three-Point Pass's sparse berry trees, the berry trees here mostly clustered together.

At a glance, there were abundant fruits everywhere—red, blue, yellow, green...

If Johan hadn't stopped them, his Pokémon would have pounced long ago.

Such dense berry groves also meant many smaller, immature berry trees were "suppressed" under several vigorously growing berry trees.

Light was blocked and soil nutrients were taken—these berry trees were destined never to fully mature.

And these berry trees were exactly Johan's target.

This saved him the trouble of planting seeds and greatly reduced their growth time. With proper transplanting, they could create a decent berry grove back on his island.

At the same time, removing these berry trees that couldn't grow would allow soil nutrients to be better absorbed by mature berry trees, producing bigger, fuller fruits.

It was killing two birds with one stone.

Then Johan picked up a small shovel temporarily forged by Tinkaton and led his little ones to dig up those small berry trees.

Originally, nearby wild Pokémon were still wary, afraid Johan would dig up the berry trees they depended on for survival or take all the berries away.

Later, seeing Johan and his group were digging saplings, which was undoubtedly good for the berry groves, they immediately let down their guard.

Some bolder wild Pokémon even came to help, speeding up the sapling excavation process.

However, while Johan was busy transplanting and digging, some little ones who weren't good at this went off to play on their own.

Like Tyranitar, Urshifu, and Dragonite—these larger ones, or those attracted by certain factors, didn't participate. Gengar was among them too.

What attracted them was the ocean outside Ballimere Lake plains.

This place was at Galar region's southernmost point. A bit further south was the ocean.

However, because Crown Tundra itself had relatively low temperatures, the surrounding waters were more or less covered with ice layers, and the underwater terrain was quite complex, preventing ships from easily approaching.

It had become a natural barrier isolating this place from the outside world.

"Ka-kaah?"

As soon as it approached the sea surface, Gengar seemed to sense something. It pulled the reins tight to stop Spectrier's steps, then loosened them slightly, and Spectrier rose into the air.

Gengar lifted its sunglasses, squinting as it looked down at the sea surface from above.

Its eyes suddenly brightened as it called out.

"Ka-kaah!"

Speaking, it immediately headed toward the seabed despite Spectrier's somewhat unwilling expression.

Dragonite and Urshifu exchanged glances and both jumped into the sea. The piercing seawater didn't make them feel cold but instead invigorated them.

"Bangi!"

Tyranitar stood on the cliff, looking at the vast ocean with hands on its hips, but didn't jump in with them.

So frustrated!

It could only sit helplessly on the cliff, casually digging up some hard rocks and "fiercely" gnawing on them.

At this moment, Tyranitar had decided it absolutely had to learn the move "Surf"!

Meanwhile, Gengar, Dragonite, and Urshifu who had jumped into the ocean soon discovered an old, decaying sunken ship at the bottom of the deep sea.

Just looking at the ship's style, you could tell it definitely had some age—it was even an old-fashioned sailing ship.

The same thought immediately popped into all their minds—treasure!

They excitedly swam toward the sunken ship on the seabed.

Gurgle gurgle—

Bubbles churned underwater.

Some wild Pokémon living near the sunken ship scattered after sensing Spectrier's aura, disappearing in the blink of an eye.

Some wild Pokémon swam away and hid nearby to watch, not knowing what these sudden intruders wanted to do.

The closer they got to the sunken ship, the more Gengar could feel ghostly aura rushing toward them.

Sunken ships and ghosts often went hand in hand.

The little ones weren't surprised by this.

"Ka-kaah~"

Gengar waved its hand, and Urshifu and Dragonite immediately swam toward the bow and stern respectively, while Gengar led Spectrier straight to the ship's cabin.

Their task distribution was so skilled, their coordination so seamless, that even Johan would probably be secretly amazed if he saw it.

How many "missions" had Gengar's "outlaw squad" been on?

Bang!!

Soon, sounds came from the bow direction.

It turned out Dragonite had encountered Dhelmise living on the sunken ship when approaching the bow!

A Ghost and Grass-type Pokémon that looked like a ship's wheel and anchor combined, wrapped with green seaweed and having gauge-like eye structures.

Despite being Ghost and Grass-type, its ability was "Steelworker," similar to Regidrago's "Dragon's Maw"—when using Steel-type moves, power increased by 50%.

Dhelmise was said to be a Ghost-type Pokémon formed when seaweed drifting on the seabed absorbed parts of sunken ships and was reborn. Its chain-like seaweed could extend hundreds of meters like iron chains, making it quite troublesome in the ocean.

Any sunken ship with some age inevitably had Dhelmise inhabiting it.

Additionally.

Dhelmise had very close relationships with Mareanie and Dragalge. Where Dhelmise existed, there was usually a high probability that Mareanie and Dragalge lived there too.

Sure enough, as soon as Dragonite conflicted with Dhelmise, two Dragalge rushed out from tangled seaweed.

However, obviously not all Pokémon could be like the Skwovet on the giant tree, having strength to face legendary Pokémon directly.

Although Dragonite's injuries hadn't fully healed, dealing with this Dhelmise and two Dragalge was still very simple.

Urshifu, who entered from the stern, also encountered a bit of trouble.

It met two Cursola.

Being Ghost-type Pokémon was somewhat constraining for Fighting-type Urshifu.

But the impact wasn't major.

After all, they came here to treasure hunt, not to go on a killing spree.

Only Gengar and Spectrier, because of Spectrier's presence, had no wild Pokémon dare approach them, entering the sunken ship very smoothly.

Even because both were Ghost-type Pokémon, Gengar and Spectrier had immediate reactions upon entering the sunken ship.

"Neighhhh——"

Even the normally silent Spectrier showed some excited emotional fluctuations.

In the dilapidated cabin, with seaweed and wood pieces floating everywhere, following the decaying stairs down, Gengar acted very cautiously, getting off Spectrier and leading it down step by step on tiptoe.

It wasn't afraid of anything, but rather...

Since this was treasure hunting, in such a suitable environment and atmosphere, naturally they should act like treasure hunters.

Immersion—understand Gengar's sense of immersion?

They encountered nothing along the way. After several twists and turns and taking a few wrong paths, they finally reached the sunken ship's lowest cabin.

"Neighhhh——"

Spectrier's thick dark purple mane spread in the water as it gently snorted toward a corner box covered in moss.

Strangely, despite being underwater, Spectrier could still snort.

Gengar's attention was immediately drawn to a round table in the cabin's center.

It was also covered with seaweed, and the entire round table was wooden, looking like it would crumble at a touch.

But on the round table sat what appeared to be an exquisite pink tea set—a teapot and two cups!

All pink.

You could tell at a glance they were valuable.

"Gulp—"

Gengar swallowed, its eyes gleaming with stars.

"Ka-kaah! (´∀`)"

Treasure!

Heaven knows, after so many treasure hunts, it had finally found proper treasure in a proper treasure hunt!

So difficult!

Gengar immediately reached out, black shadows extending from its hand to grab the entire tea set.

A tea set!

And it looked like porcelain too.

This was perfect for it!

Gengar was already imagining using this tea set to brew Energy Root tea.

Just thinking about it was wonderful!

Spectrier couldn't help glancing at Gengar.

Wait, as a ghost, couldn't you sense what these teapots and cups actually were?

But it didn't say anything. After all, Gengar didn't need to fear ghosts. It just gently turned its head, tugging the reins to indicate Gengar should look at the corner box.

"Ka-kaah~"

At this moment, Gengar had already put on swimming goggles. Regarding the box Spectrier pointed to, it naturally wasn't completely oblivious—that rich Ghost-type aura was the most concentrated place in the entire sunken ship.

Gengar had just been attracted by the tea set on the table first.

It approached and gently patted the moss-covered box, immediately producing dull metallic sounds.

At the same time, as it patted, waves of Ghost-type energy poured out, as if trying to envelop Gengar.

But Gengar opened its mouth wide and, along with seawater, swallowed all this Ghost-type energy in one gulp.

Then.

The box went quiet.

"Ka-kaah?"

Gengar scratched its head, looking at Spectrier.

Spectrier turned its head away with an expression of "don't look at me, I don't know either."

"Draaa?"

"Garruu~?"

Dragonite and Urshifu arrived one after another.

They had searched around but couldn't find anything valuable.

"Ka-kaah!"

Move it!

Gengar immediately waved its hand grandly.

Better not open it in the sea—if there were good things inside and seawater rushed in to destroy them, they should move it up first.

Dragonite and Urshifu exchanged glances and immediately grabbed the box from left and right.

It was quite heavy.

At least much heavier than they had expected.

Then Gengar's group didn't linger in the sunken ship and swam toward the surface.

After they left, the previously frightened wild Pokémon slowly returned.

They seemed to sense that the cold, eerie aura that had been constantly disturbing them from the ship's depths was gone, and these wild Pokémon immediately became cheerful and happy.

Such good people...

Clang!

The metal box landed heavily on the ground.

Johan's head was full of question marks as he looked at what Gengar and the others had suddenly brought out, momentarily confused.

He had just finished the first batch of sapling excavation and sat down to rest when Gengar and the others gave him this "big surprise."

"What is it?"

"Ka-kaah~Ka-kaah~"

"Draaa~Draaa~"

"Garruu~"

Then Gengar, Dragonite, and Urshifu, one by one, chaotically described their previous sunken ship treasure hunting experience.

Fortunately, Johan was used to his Pokémon's cacophonous style and quickly extracted useful information, then arranged and combined it himself.

Sunken ship?

Johan was stunned.

With Crown Tundra's surrounding thick glaciers, how could ships navigate here?

But thinking about it.

Without sinking a few ships, how would ancient people know this place was inaccessible?

Hearing Dragonite mention encountering Dhelmise and Dragalge, and Urshifu mentioning Cursola.

"Cursola... sunken ship..."

Johan couldn't help thinking of the ghost pirate Pokémon hunter group he'd encountered during the Sea Temple incident, whose bearded leader had a Cursola.

Following that lead revealed some connection to the Galar region.

Now thinking about it...

Ships could hardly approach here, but if it were submarines, that would be different.

However, Johan didn't think deeply about it, finally looking back at the seaweed-covered metal box before him.

Violent disassembly would be simplest, but what if there were really good things inside?

"Open it and see," Johan said.

"Ka-kaah~"

Gengar stepped forward, stuck a finger into the box's keyhole, pouted its lips and twisted left and right. When it pulled its finger out, it had already formed into a key shape.

Then Tinkaton stepped in.

"Cha~"

Using Gengar's current finger-key as a template, with Ceruledge providing charcoal fire to heat metal and Tinkaton swinging its hammer.

Soon.

A brand new key that fit this treasure box was forged.

"So, so skilled..." Flint nearby sighed.

Johan's cheek twitched slightly.

Understand what professionalism means?

Was Gengar's "outlaw squad" called that for nothing?

Infiltration, lockpicking, violent entry, etc.—they had it all.

Click—click—

Gengar rubbed its palms together, inserted the key into the keyhole, and gently turned it a few times. With mechanical sounds, the box opened.

"Holy crap!" Flint was the first to exclaim in shock.

Even though Gengar and the others had some guesses, they now stared wide-eyed with mouths agape.

Even Johan stood there amazed, looking at that box more than half full of... gold coins!

"Teacher Johan, we're, we're rich," Flint murmured.

There had to be at least three or four hundred gold coins in that box!

Underwater sunken ship treasure hunting could be this profitable?

Flint couldn't help looking at his Infernape.

"Ku! (▼皿▼)"

Infernape glared fiercely at Flint with a menacing expression.

Me, diving?

And you're a Fire-type trainer!

Flint sheepishly looked away.

However, after Johan's initial surprise, he noticed these gold coins' special characteristics.

He stepped forward and casually picked one up.

Heavy.

Definitely gold coins.

But...

"These are Gimmighoul Coins," Johan said.

Gimmighoul Coins?

"Ka-kaah!"

Gengar suddenly understood, sticking out its tongue to reveal an almost identical "Gimmighoul Coin."

This was one they'd obtained before.

"Gimmighoul?" Flint asked puzzledly.

"A special ancient Pokémon."

Ding—

Johan flicked his finger, tossing the gold coin back into the box.

Gimmighoul was a Pokémon registered in the Paldea region's Pokédex, lurking in various corners of the Paldea region. It was said that when people approached, it would use Ghost-type energy to drive them to help search for gold coins.

Gimmighoul needed to collect 999 such coins to evolve into Gholdengo!

A Steel and Ghost-type Pokémon, a regular in competitive battling.

However.

The coins being "Gimmighoul Coins" was correct, but that didn't mean they had no value.

Setting everything else aside, these were gold coins!

And gold coins with historical value.

If they encountered collectors, their value would undoubtedly be even higher.

When they were truly down and out with empty pockets, selling these gold coins wouldn't be a bad way to supplement household expenses.

"Put them away first."

Since they were "Gimmighoul Coins," Johan wasn't surprised Gengar had found them.

Just as he finished speaking, seeing Gengar not only didn't move but also showed a smiling expression indicating there were more treasures, Johan asked with some surprise:

"There are more good things?"

"Ta-da ta-da ta-da~!"

Gengar didn't hide anything and immediately produced the tea set it treasured!

A pink teapot and two pink cups.

"Sinistea and Polteageist?" Johan was stunned.

"And they're all shiny?"

Looking at them in water seemed exquisite, but taking them ashore revealed these tea items all had chips.

Those two broken teacups had obvious eye and mouth-like strange patterns, with thick purple liquid flowing in the middle like slime. Looking carefully, you could see it was still flowing in spiral patterns.

"Gengar, did you just brew tea?" Flint looked at the purple liquid with curiosity.

Johan's expression was strange.

Looking at the teapot.

Its patterns were similar to the teacups, obviously belonging to the same "set," just without eye and mouth-like outlines.

The teapot's lid had some cracks and chips, and its wall had a medium-sized gap plugged by the same purple liquid-like substance inside.

This was exactly Sinistea's evolution, Polteageist!

Just as Flint picked up a teacup to take a small sip, and Johan was observing Polteageist, the pot's lid suddenly opened. A small purple creature cautiously poked its head out to look around.

Just as it met Johan's gaze, it immediately shuddered and retracted.

Like a hermit crab.

"Ka-kaah?!"

Gengar's voice immediately rose several octaves.

Earlier it had focused more on the tea set's appearance, plus interference from the Ghost-type energy released by a box of "Gimmighoul Coins," so it hadn't carefully examined this tea set.

Now seeing the purple, slime-like little figure emerging from the teapot, if it still couldn't react, it wouldn't be Gengar.

These were actually three Pokémon?!

Gengar was greatly shocked.

"Pfft—"

Flint suddenly spat out a mouthful, his face turning pale as he stared at the teacup in his hand.

"So, so bitter!"

Johan glanced at him, confirming Flint only found it bitter and hadn't been invaded by anything that drained his energy, then relaxed and said:

"This is Sinistea, a Ghost-type Pokémon. You weren't drinking tea—you were drinking its body."

"Ah, ah?!"

Flint stood there dazed.

Didn't this mean... he had eaten a Pokémon?

Johan saw his thoughts and couldn't help laughing: "Drinking a little is fine. If it were Sinistea's trainer in a good relationship..."

"It would taste good?" Flint interjected.

"No, you just wouldn't have your energy drained. No one can swallow Sinistea's tea," Johan couldn't suppress his teasing tone.

Flint: "..."

"As for Polteageist."

Johan picked up the teapot, gently shaking it. The purple little figure inside immediately poked its head out again.

"The black tea brewed by Polteageist has a unique taste and aroma. The flavor and scent are very distinctive. Many people are quite enthusiastic about it, though drinking too much inevitably causes diarrhea and stomach discomfort, yet some people still enjoy it."

Of course, this was also under the premise of establishing a good relationship with Polteageist.

Johan held the teapot overhead, looking underneath, and found a small stamp.

At the same time, under the Sinistea in Flint's hands, he also saw a stamp. The remaining Sinistea was the same.

"Wow, they're all authentic?" Johan said.

"Authentic?"

Flint imitated Johan, picking up the teacup to look at the stamp underneath.

"Sinistea and Polteageist are somewhat like hermit crabs—it's the purple substance entering cups and teapots that becomes these Pokémon."

Johan began explaining.

"So many people specially prepare special teacups and teapots, waiting for them to become Sinistea and Polteageist."

For Sinistea to evolve into Polteageist, the purple liquid in the cup had to crawl into a prepared teapot to complete evolution.

"But among so many teacups and teapots, there are naturally authentic and counterfeit ones. Those with stamps underneath are authentic, with extremely high collectible value."

"Though as Pokémon, there's actually not much difference."

But one Polteageist and two Sinistea, all authentic and all shiny—this rarity was obvious!

Combined with the box of "Gimmighoul Coins" Gengar and the others had found.

This sunken ship probably didn't belong to ordinary people—it was likely some ancient noble or even royal vessel.

Flint caught the key point in Johan's words and asked quietly:

"Teacher Johan, what if that purple liquid didn't enter teacups or teapots but entered a toilet instead?"

"Pfft—"

Infernape, who had just taken a sip of water, sprayed it out.

It gave Flint a look that said "you're unbeatable."

Johan's expression was strange. After being stunned by Flint for two seconds, he finally said quietly:

"I suggest you try that in the future, Toilet King."

The Pokémon world was full of wonders. Even Nincada could evolve and split into Ninjask and Shedinja.

Could such things be explained clearly?

Flint scratched the back of his head, feeling like his brain was about to grow.

Johan returned all the Sinistea and Polteageist to Gengar. "Keep them."

He wasn't planning to release them back to nature.

Or rather, Sinistea and Polteageist didn't really have a "return to nature" concept.

Whether Sinistea or Polteageist, both hoped to be drunk, which is why so many people deliberately set up tea sets waiting for them to transform.

So compared to the dark, underwater sunken ship, taking them away was actually helping them.

"Ka-kaah!"

Gengar wasn't scared off by Flint's earlier spitting or Johan's explanation.

As a ghost, it didn't fear having its energy absorbed.

Moreover.

Sinistea's tea might be bitter, but didn't Johan say Polteageist's brewed tea would be more flavorful?

Besides, Sinistea was only bitter because of the purple liquid inside. If you poured more tea into it, would it still be bitter?

It treasured the teapot and teacups.

Finally, its painstakingly developed "Energy Root tea" had obtained worthy tea sets!

Polteageist cautiously poked its head out again, only to see a sinister, cold, terrifying big face grinning wickedly. It immediately shuddered and quickly retracted, the pot lid and body colliding with crisp, pleasant sounds.

Gengar's smile grew wider.

This "shell withdrawal" technique was quite skilled.

It happily stored all the tea sets in its shadow.

Being fellow Ghost-type Pokémon, its shadow was an excellent resting place for Polteageist and Sinistea.

Night fell.

The previous liveliness quieted with nightfall. Except for the faint sounds of waves lapping the shore and some rustling small movements, Ballimere Lake plains suddenly became exceptionally quiet.

Wild Pokémon living nearby gradually returned to their nests to rest, waiting to fall asleep in this especially safe environment.

In such a wonderful place, not camping and cooking outdoors would feel like a waste of the environment.

So Johan immediately set up tents, assembled his various miscellaneous equipment, and built a campfire.

Flint was single and borrowed a tent from Johan, then sat eagerly by the campfire waiting for Johan to prepare dinner.

Tonight's dinner was curry.

Johan used to dislike curry quite a bit, but after contact and making it himself a few times, he discovered it wasn't that he disliked it—he disliked others making it.

Curry made according to his own taste was actually quite good.

The key point was.

Curry paired with everything. For such a large family, cooking one big pot of curry solved everything.

If that wasn't enough, just add more potatoes, carrots, and such—win through quantity.

See.

Not only were his own Pokémon attracted by the curry's aroma, even the group of Greedent and Skwovet from the giant tree were drawn over by the curry's scent.

Pairs of small eyes watched that whole pot of fragrant curry, carefully swallowing their saliva.

Johan smiled slightly.

He had already calculated this group of Skwovet into his plans.

Not just them—any nearby wild Pokémon bold enough to come out wanting to eat, he could share some with them.

As for whether there was enough...

Not enough? Just make another pot—it wasn't a big deal anyway.

During the day, quite a few wild Pokémon had helped dig saplings together.

At this time.

Flint, holding his bowl and waiting, suddenly raised his hand, pointing at the night sky.

"Teacher Johan, look quickly—shooting stars!"

Looking in the direction of the sound.

Two crimson beams were seen streaking across the sky, falling toward them.

Johan raised an eyebrow.

These weren't shooting stars at all.

They were clearly... Galar particles!

# 691: Ghost-Horse Unity! Miraculous Berry! (Two-in-One Chapter)

"Is that Dynamax?!"

After a brief moment of surprise, Flint quickly reacted.

A few days ago, he had encountered and battled a Gigantamax Copperajah in the distance from Freezington.

"And there are two of them!"

Two Galar particles inevitably meant two Pokémon would be affected and enter an uncontrolled Dynamax state.

Johan was also somewhat puzzled.

"Have the Galar particles in the Galar region already gotten out of control to this extent? Could Eternatus have already awakened?"

With two Galar particles appearing at once like this, it was hard not to suspect something had happened with Eternatus.

Or perhaps...

Was Chairman Rose doing this deliberately?

Providing more training and battle opportunities for Leon, who was in his final sprint phase?

Or creating more momentum for Leon so his future Champion title would be more resounding?

Leon's peak strength was unquestionable—he was very strong. But before he reached his peak, his reputation as the "undefeated Champion" was already quite loud. Chairman Rose had definitely put considerable effort into this.

"What?" Flint didn't catch Johan's muttering.

"Nothing." Johan shook his head and complained: "I told you that you're a 'jinx.'"

Flint really wanted to use his usual retort of "maybe it's Teacher Johan's problem."

But thinking about it...

This time it really seemed like he had first encountered the Gigantamax Copperajah, and now two Galar particles had come again.

Could it really be my problem?

Flint was confused.

While Johan and Flint were teasing each other, those two crimson Galar particles streaked across the night sky, falling vertically with no way to resist them.

One fell into the dense canopy of the giant tree.

The other fell not far in front of Johan and the others, onto the leader Skwovet!

Rumble rumble—

Intense energy surged momentarily. Red clouds appeared in the sky, swirling with faint thunder. Two fierce auras wildly churned.

Sensing these two auras, nearby wild Pokémon all ran out of their nests, then were so frightened by this scene that they immediately retreated.

The Skwovet and Greedent chattered nonstop, seemingly not understanding what had happened to their leader.

However, before the leader Skwovet changed, an extremely fierce cry came from within the giant tree's canopy.

"Caw——!!!"

A large bird wreathed in black flames emerged from within, flapping its wings. Then, surrounded by red clouds, its form expanded at an exaggerated speed.

It was clearly—Gigantamax Galarian Moltres!

The next moment.

"Skwo!!"

A deep cry, and the Skwovet's form also rapidly climbed, bathed under red clouds and Galar particles, its size rivaling the clouds.

Seeing this scene, the Greedent and Skwovet nearly craned their necks at ninety-degree angles, mouths agape as they looked at their leader.

How did it suddenly... get so big?!

Did the leader hit a second growth spurt?

Gigantamax Skwovet!

In an instant, two powerful Pokémon completed Gigantamax, their strength surging!

Witnessing Gigantamax again, Flint wasn't as shocked, just asking:

"What do we do, Teacher Johan?"

What to do?

Johan adjusted his glasses and said irritably:

"Fight, obviously."

Speaking, he quickly instructed:

"Try for a quick victory to minimize impact, keep the commotion as small as possible. Also, absolutely don't affect that giant tree!"

They had to win quickly while controlling the commotion.

Otherwise, even if they won, it would definitely be a disaster for this region and the wild Pokémon living here.

"You handle this Skwovet."

With that, Johan quickly ran toward the Gigantamax Moltres direction, simultaneously following his glasses' anti-slip chain to grab the Key Stone embedded at the end.

It was already glowing brilliantly.

Since they needed a quick victory while minimizing commotion, they couldn't use this to train his Pokémon, nor could they hold back much strength.

"Gengar!"

Gengar, who had already mounted up, heard the call and immediately grinned, pulling the reins.

"Neighhhh——"

Spectrier neighed, raising its front hooves high as spirit mist appeared beneath its feet, taking to the air.

"Mega Evolution!!"

Gengar's body immediately burst with rainbow light, completing Mega Evolution while riding Spectrier.

Sharper spikes, a strange golden eye on its forehead, an unchanged smile, and even more surging Ghost-type energy.

"Neighhhh!!"

Spectrier seemed affected by Gengar's Mega Evolution too. The reins around its neck fit even better as it reared its front hooves, neighing in midair.

Hmm?

Even Johan felt something strange.

Why did it feel like...

He suddenly had four extra legs?

Mega Evolution was a process where the bond between trainer and Pokémon became substantial, with wills and consciousness connecting.

Johan and Gengar had undergone Mega Evolution countless times. They knew each other's states and post-evolution changes like the back of their hands.

But this time... there was something different.

Calyrex and Glastrier's "fusion" relied on the "Reins of Unity" and the bond already established between Calyrex and Glastrier.

If Calyrex, Glastrier, and Spectrier had relationships like the "Tao trio," that would be understandable. But the problem was that Calyrex and the two horses... were originally gradually compatible through acquired means.

So with Gengar plus Spectrier plus "Reins of Unity" plus the so-called "power of bonds" brought by Mega Evolution, wouldn't that mean...

Otherwise, what was this feeling of having four extra feet yet controlling them like limbs?

Moreover, Gengar and Spectrier's types were quite compatible.

"Caw!!!"

While Johan and Gengar were both somewhat surprised by the changes, the Gigantamax Moltres wasn't being idle.

It flapped its enormous wings, an indescribable powerful malice bursting from its body. With its cry, that Dark-type energy erupted like a volcano.

Max Darkness!

This was the Max Move that Dark-type moves became after Gigantamax.

Besides increased range, it also carried the special effect of Max Moves—lowering all opposing Pokémon's Special Defense.

The overwhelming Dark-type energy couldn't be dodged.

"Gengar!"

Johan and Mega Gengar had also collected their various thoughts, focusing on the collision ahead.

Buzz—

Spectrier snorted, spirit mist representing Ghost-type energy surging from its body, enveloping both it and Gengar before they vanished!

Shadow Sneak!

And the falling Max Darkness was met by moonlight full of life energy.

"Oowoo!!"

Ninetales!

Its four limbs pressed to the ground, the abundant life force of this plain, especially the giant tree on the hill, rustled its leaves as if responding to Ninetales' earth control.

Nine tails spread like fans. The bright moon in the clear night made Ninetales' Moonblast spread to maximum range.

Boom!!

The roar exploded, dust scattered.

The Gigantamax Moltres's Max Darkness was blocked by Ninetales' Moonblast, causing no damage to the plain, the Pokémon on it, or the giant tree.

At the same time.

Gengar and Spectrier appeared in the air behind Gigantamax Moltres.

"Ka-kaah!"

With a somewhat playful cry, just as Gigantamax Moltres turned around, it saw Gengar raising its spike-covered palm.

Star-like light points constantly appeared around its and Spectrier's bodies, then quickly gathered toward Gengar's palm.

At that moment, even the moon in the night sky seemed to dim. The light points around Gengar and Spectrier were like vast, brilliant stars.

Seeing this scene, Johan's heart jumped.

He remembered what Calyrex had told him before.

"When this king rides Spectrier, this king's psychic energy flows into Spectrier through the reins, enhancing its power. In an instant, countless spirit starlight can be created. When we gather these starlight's power, this move is called——"

Astral Barrage!

This move itself belonged to Calyrex's "enhancement" of Spectrier's power, with the key being Spectrier!

At this moment, Gengar's palm was like the most brilliant star in the night sky.

With its low shout and Spectrier's neigh.

Swinging its palm.

Falling stars!

Astral Barrage!

Boom!!!

An incredibly terrifying Ghost-type energy exploded on Gigantamax Moltres's back. The impact was so strong it directly knocked Gigantamax Moltres from the sky.

"Caw!!!"

Moltres cried out in pain.

"Ka-kaah..."

Gengar looked down at its own palm, seemingly surprised by the move it had just used.

That feeling... was a bit strange.

"Neighhhh!!"

Spectrier looked back at Mega Gengar on its back and couldn't help curling its lip.

The power was much less than when with Calyrex, but... being able to use it still surprised Spectrier.

Moreover, unlike Calyrex, who as a Psychic-type Pokémon injected psychic energy, Gengar injected pure Ghost-type energy.

Of course, the consumption for Gengar wasn't small either.

Watching those falling brilliant stars, Johan clicked his tongue.

"Gengar got an epic buff..."

But this kind of "rider-horse unity," two Pokémon combining—no, Gengar couldn't even be called "fusing" with Spectrier—just two Pokémon definitely couldn't appear on official League tournament stages.

Probably even the "Champion's Path" wouldn't allow it.

What a pity.

Johan sighed internally.

Otherwise, with Gengar "fusing" with a legendary Pokémon, they might have been able to steamroll the Champion's Path, since borrowing the "Reins of Unity" for cooperation provided much greater benefits than simple addition.

No, no, no.

Perhaps this should be called Ghost-Horse Unity?

"Caw!!"

The falling Gigantamax Moltres barely stabilized, flapping its giant wings as it ferociously charged toward Gengar and Spectrier.

"Shadow Ball!"

"Ka-kaah!"

Gengar took a deep breath and instantly condensed a massive Shadow Ball.

If the previous "Astral Barrage" was Gengar lending power to Spectrier, using Spectrier's power to execute,

Then this Shadow Ball was Spectrier lending power to Gengar, executing through Gengar's methods.

At least Gengar still mastered the "Ghost Legion" technique.

So even without the so-called "Astral Barrage," Spectrier and Gengar were still an epic enhancement.

The Shadow Ball struck.

Boom!!

The massive impact dispersed part of the dark red mist surrounding Moltres.

"Caw——!!"

Then Moltres struggled and cried out, not attacking again but trembling its wings in place.

Seeing this, Johan immediately understood Moltres's condition.

Although Eternatus was strong, forcing a legendary Pokémon of considerable strength like Galarian Moltres to completely lose its reason with just one Galar particle wasn't easy.

After two heavy blows from Gengar and Spectrier destroyed part of the Galar particles on it, Moltres began to struggle.

"Caw!!!"

Crying out again, dark red energy like particles scattered from Moltres's body.

At the same time, Moltres's form visibly shrank until it returned to normal.

The red cloud vortex above its head dispersed as it slowly landed, breathing heavily.

Johan glanced at Moltres, confirming it had broken free from the Galar particles' control and had no intention of continuing to attack, then immediately signaled Gengar to change direction and assist Flint.

"Cha..."

Tinkaton, holding its hammer, reluctantly lowered it and scratched its head with a regretful expression.

What a pity, such a big bird...

It had thought this would be another big battle where it would definitely get to fight.

Who knew Gengar would only use two moves before Moltres broke free from the Galar particles and recovered.

The clash between Gigantamax Skwovet and Flint had already entered a heated phase.

Skwovet dared to face Moltres directly not just because of the giant tree and its clan, but more importantly because of its own strength.

Combined with the enhancement from Gigantamax and Johan's instruction not to make too much commotion or cause too much destruction, Flint and his Pokémon were somewhat restrained.

But even so, the commotion was still considerable, and there was a faint trend of it getting out of control.

After all, Flint was the type who forgot everything once he started fighting, and he and his Fire-type Pokémon were typical "terrain destroyers."

On professional battle venues it was fine, but in the wild, trying not to cause too much destruction was indeed difficult.

Fortunately.

Johan resolved the Moltres trouble at an unexpectedly fast speed and rushed over.

"Neighhhh——"

Spectrier, carrying Mega Gengar, hovered before Gigantamax Skwovet.

With experience dealing with Gigantamax Moltres, Johan and Gengar acted very decisively.

"Hypnosis!"

After successfully attracting Gigantamax Skwovet's attention, Gengar swayed its arms, using Hypnosis.

Gigantamax Skwovet's eyelids immediately began fighting, its massive body starting to sway.

Then dark red particles began separating from Gigantamax Skwovet's body.

Gigantamax and Terastal were essentially quite similar in nature.

Both relied on partial power from some incredibly powerful Pokémon, applied and transformed to act on Pokémon, granting certain enhancement effects.

So after experiencing Terastal and Gigantamax Moltres, Johan and Gengar had gained some understanding.

This method of forcibly injecting Galar particles to force Gigantamax was ultimately too crude compared to using a Dynamax Band.

"Skwo..."

The giant Skwovet's body tilted backward while its form rapidly shrank.

Thud—

When it actually hit the ground, it had returned to its original size, not causing too much destruction or commotion.

"Phew—"

Flint immediately breathed a sigh of relief.

Honestly.

This kind of restrained fighting... really made him uncomfortable and unsatisfied.

But his reaction made Johan suddenly think that perhaps he could give his Pokémon some "weighted" training?

For example, limiting the methods, habits, and practices his Pokémon were most skilled at and familiar with, making them strengthen from another dimension through certain discomfort.

Like energy control.

His Pokémon were even more famous "terrain destroyers" than Flint.

But destroying terrain, except for certain situations like Earthquake, mostly came from energy not being concentrated enough—energy or power waste.

Not requiring complete avoidance of terrain destruction, but if they could master and more concentratedly drive some originally dissipated power, wouldn't move power get some enhancement?

The divergent thought flashed by. Johan silently noted it, deciding to try it after returning home with his Pokémon's approval and permission.

Looking at the unconscious Skwovet leader.

As it fell, its fluffy tail immediately scattered many things.

Mostly berries, plus some strange items that all looked impressive at first glance.

Even just the berries were very high-quality, rare berries, some Johan didn't even recognize.

Good heavens, this tail could store so much?

It was almost comparable to his Gengar!

No wonder so many wild adventure trainers liked targeting Skwovet, especially when short on food—they were praised as "wilderness survival emergency rations."

Speaking of Gengar...

"Gengar!"

Johan immediately called out to the purple fatty carefully and stealthily approaching the Skwovet.

This ghost was treating it like monster-hunting for loot!

And right in front of so many Greedent and Skwovet.

Called by Johan, Gengar immediately smiled sheepishly, pausing its movements.

But soon it picked up a dropped berry from the ground and placed it beside the sleeping Skwovet.

"Ka-kaah~"

I'm helping here, I'm not that kind of ghost~

Speaking, it grinned, showing white teeth.

Johan rolled his eyes. He naturally didn't believe Gengar's ghost words, but... the Greedent and Skwovet believed!

Returning lost property—this was returning lost property! Wasn't this a proper "good person"?

Combined with earlier giving energy cubes, sharing curry, and helping "calm" the Skwovet leader, the Greedent and Skwovet looked at Gengar and Johan's group differently.

Snap—

Gengar lightly snapped its fingers, waking the sleeping Skwovet.

"Skwo?"

The Skwovet sat up sleepily, showing its two big front teeth as it yawned long.

Seeing the big ghost face before it, it jumped up from the ground with a start.

Then it discovered its "treasures" scattered on the ground.

Its eyes immediately widened. Not caring about Gengar, it hurriedly lowered its head to quickly and skillfully stuff those things into its tail one by one.

Hard to imagine Skwovet's tail could store so many things.

The already fluffy tail, bigger than its body, swelled more than double after storing all the ground "treasures."

"Skwo——"

After confirming nothing was missing, Skwovet sighed in relief, gently wiping its forehead.

"Skwo?"

Then it looked puzzled, completely forgetting what had happened earlier.

Not until several Skwovet and Greedent vividly described the earlier process, using exaggerated gestures to demonstrate and simulate, did the Skwovet leader understand the situation.

The Skwovet looked at Gengar, who was eyeing its tail, jumped over a meter high, and gently patted Gengar's shoulder, nodding continuously.

"Skwo~Skwo!"

Little guy, not bad, not bad!

"Ka-kaah?"

Little guy? Me? This old man?

Gengar pointed at itself, looking stunned.

This was the first time someone had called it that.

Watching Gengar and Skwovet start arguing about who was calling whom little, Johan smiled and shook his head.

Although things happened quite suddenly, fortunately they didn't cause too much impact.

"Right! My curry!"

Johan suddenly reacted.

He'd been busy dealing with those two Galar particles' Gigantamax and forgot there was still curry cooking in the pot!

Crown Tundra, Crown Temple.

Calyrex, leading Glastrier, was slowly clearing the temple ruins, especially cleaning out the stables.

It suddenly looked up.

Frowning.

Two red particle beams streaked across Crown Tundra's sky.

As an "old opponent," Calyrex knew this was the power of that meteorite from outer space—Eternatus.

Just after awakening, it had already sensed that the entire Galar region was filled with Eternatus's energy, just not as concentrated as these two dark red beams.

"This king's subjects..."

It didn't know if its subjects were affected by Eternatus, whether they lived in dire straits.

But halfway through this sentence, Calyrex smiled self-mockingly.

No one remembered it anymore—where were its so-called "subjects"?

The Galar particles streaked past, falling on the distant giant tree hill.

"Neighhhh——"

Glastrier suddenly became restless, hooves pacing back and forth, seemingly sensing Spectrier's power, and...

"Indeed."

Calyrex's eyes also brightened slightly.

"Johan's Gengar can indeed control Spectrier and gain part of Spectrier's power."

It had actually noticed early on the possibility of "fusion" between Gengar and Spectrier.

This was why it wasn't eager to reclaim Spectrier and let Johan and Gengar take Spectrier out together.

On one hand, it wanted to repay Johan and Gengar for their help.

On the other hand, it wanted to verify its inner speculation.

Facts proved its guess was correct.

"Teacher Johan, what do you think those falling red beams were? Doesn't the Galar League say you need a 'Dynamax Band' to Gigantamax? And it has to be in specific locations..."

Flint asked while eating curry rice, accompanied by clanking sounds of spoon hitting plate.

"Probably some situation we don't know about occurred," Johan said vaguely, too lazy to explain.

"Oh~~"

Flint nodded thoughtfully.

Eternatus was crucial to Chairman Rose's Macro Cosmos Corporation.

And Macro Cosmos Corporation was omnipresent throughout the Galar region.

Almost every corner and aspect of the Galar region had its shadow—from regional energy and Gigantamax stadiums to daily life's food, clothing, housing, and transportation, all had Macro Cosmos Corporation's involvement.

Although its reputation wasn't as great as Silph or Devon, its scale was definitely no smaller. After Chairman Rose became Galar League Chairman, Macro Cosmos Corporation could even be considered half a League industry.

In this situation, unless Eternatus completely awakened and escaped Chairman Rose's control, anyone who provoked it might be labeled as hostile to the Galar League.

Either wait for Leon to become Champion and investigate this as Galar Champion with his position and reputation.

Anyway, it wasn't Johan and Flint's turn.

"You two, stop posing. Do you want more or not?"

Johan looked aside and asked.

He saw Gengar riding Spectrier, standing in moonlight wearing sunglasses with an aura mixing righteousness and evil.

Beside it was the Skwovet leader, hands behind its back, gazing at the giant tree with an aged, worried-about-the-country expression.

Hearing this.

"Ka-kaah!"

"Skwo!"

The two's long-held poses instantly collapsed as they rushed toward Johan with their eating utensils.

Gengar held its exclusive bowl, while the Skwovet leader produced a wooden bowl obviously gnawed by its big teeth—super large, looking like it could sleep inside.

They excitedly ran to Johan's big pot, holding bowls and waiting.

Johan, making his third pot, smiled and shook his head.

He gave them large half-bowls of rice, then covered them with thick curry.

Only because he could store many things in Gengar's shadow when going out could he manage this curry meal with just rice.

After a feast where even bowls were licked clean, Johan approached the Skwovet leader.

He expressed wanting to enter the giant tree's canopy to look around.

And possibly wanting to cut a few branches from the central area for transplanting.

Hearing Johan's request, Skwovet naturally waved grandly at entering the canopy, but for cutting branches from the central area...

"Skwo!" (Ask it yourself!)

The Skwovet leader scratched its butt, sniffed at its nose tip, and said casually.

This familiar action...

Johan looked at Gengar nearby, seeing his purple fatty also scratch its butt and carefully sniff at its nose tip.

Noticing Johan's gaze, it grinned.

"Ask it?" Johan looked back at the giant tree, withdrawing his gaze.

From Skwovet's tone, could this giant tree have self-awareness?

Xerneas?

"Skwo~"

The Skwovet leader waved its hand, indicating Johan and the others should follow.

Speaking, it walked toward the giant tree with hands behind its back, swaying.

Johan and his Pokémon followed behind, somewhat anticipating the giant tree's canopy interior.

Only Gengar stared at Skwovet's tail with burning eyes.

This was a big treasure!

Walking under the giant tree, they saw Moltres standing beside the tree, silently licking its wounds. Noticing Johan and the others approaching, it showed no particular reaction.

Johan stepped forward, ignoring Moltres's reaction, and placed some status-recovery energy cubes before it.

Then, under Moltres's somewhat complex gaze, he followed Skwovet into the giant tree's canopy.

Honestly.

Viewing from outside and entering the canopy interior were completely different feelings. Though it was very dense canopy, after entering they found... the space was surprisingly large and spacious.

Though it was night with dense leaves blocking moonlight, the canopy's interior lighting wasn't poor.

Many unknown firefly-like light points emitted weak fluorescence, illuminating the entire canopy interior with a feeling of...

Being under a vast starry sky.

Rustle rustle—

Gentle breeze passed, leaves like waves rustling.

The Skwovet leader was obviously extremely familiar with this place, recognizing the way with eyes closed, leading Johan and the others to the canopy's very center.

Don't know why.

Approaching the canopy's center, Johan felt a... vibrant life aura. Simple breathing seemed to open all his body's pores.

Life force?

Having experienced Xerneas's blessing baptism, Johan was quite sensitive to "life force."

Ninetales and Tinkaton's reactions confirmed this.

"Ka-kaah~"

Gengar tugged Johan's clothes, pointing toward the canopy center where three fruits of varying ripeness hung.

Berries?

Johan was stunned.

This tree was also a berry tree?

How had he never heard of such a berry tree?

Wait.

Elder Fukuji's "Complete Berry Guide" seemed to mention...

Johan frowned, recalling.

Gradually, his eyes brightened.

"Miraculous Berry?!"

The raw material for making "Rare Candy"!

"Rare Candy" wasn't something Johan had never obtained—he still had three left.

And "Rare Candy" wasn't like in games where any level, any strength Pokémon could level up by eating one.

Specific effects varied with the consuming Pokémon's specific situation.

But anyway, they were definitely good things.

According to the League, "Rare Candy" was now almost impossible to make. What existed were stockpiles—use some, lose some.

Many researchers in the League were still trying to replicate "Rare Candy."

For example, in the Advanced Generation anime, a doctor named "Gordon" developed a special candy similar to "Rare Candy."

But possibly because it wasn't fully perfected, this fruit could enhance some Pokémon's strength but caused side effects like body enlargement and deformity.

In Pokémon Special, there were also scenes of "Rare Candy" use. Besides raising Pokémon levels, it could also grant massive short-term strength increases.

Elder Fukuji's "Complete Berry Guide" mentioned information about "Miraculous Berry," but according to him, this berry tree seemed unfindable.

Fukuji speculated it might be because the berry tree had extremely high environmental requirements and nutritional needs, making it very difficult to grow.

He guessed it might exist in some special, enclosed spaces, ruins, or secret realms, and possibly near the Tree of Beginning.

Didn't expect to encounter it here.

"No wonder..."

Johan somewhat understood.

No wonder the Skwovet living on this tree generally had relatively high levels, with average levels even exceeding forty—much higher than other wild Skwovet.

Let alone that Skwovet leader who could face Moltres directly.

Originally thought it was due to rich natural conditions, possibly including this giant tree and its fruits.

No wonder even the temperamental Galarian Moltres restrained itself when facing this giant tree.

This might already be one of the few "Miraculous Berry" trees left in the world.

Unprocessed "Miraculous Berry" probably couldn't match "Rare Candy" in effect, but likely wasn't far off.

"But this way... having berries means seeds, right? Or like Sitrus Berry and others, cutting and transplanting would work better?"

Johan thought while, at Skwovet leader's indication, going to pick the ripe berry.

According to its indication, any Pokémon entering the canopy who encountered ripe berries could pick one.

This was the "Tree God's" will.

"This might be how this berry tree reproduces."

Like dandelions using wind to spread seeds, some used Pokémon eating and excretion for reproduction—all for reproduction.

This giant tree used this method.

The three legendary birds of Galar returning every few decades might also help this giant tree reproduce?

After reading some books and notes at Elder Fukuji's, Johan had gained new understanding and knowledge in this area.

Grasping the deep purple fruit with light pink spots, one palm could just hold it. The feel wasn't particularly different from ordinary berries.

Crack.

A light crisp sound, and the berry fell into his hand.

His Pokémon all crowded around with envious eyes.

"Don't know if with Groudon's lava soil, 'King of Bountiful Harvests' Calyrex's power, plus some Grass-type Pokémon like Applin, all these buffs stacked together, could grow this..."

# 692: Island Construction (Two-in-One Chapter)

The next day.

"Haha!"

Johan excitedly pulled up his fishing rod, looking at the Arrokuda hanging from the hook with a satisfied smile.

This was a Pokémon discovered and registered in the Galar region's Pokédex. It looked like a dart, hence its name, with three tail fins that resembled a propeller.

Arrokuda was a Rush Pokémon with pure Water-type attributes. It had extremely fast speed in water, and its evolved form Barraskewda could exceed 100 knots in speed.

However, Arrokuda had very poor eyesight, so their hunting mostly relied on luck.

At the same time, although Arrokuda were fast, it was only their straight-line speed. If they had to turn corners, they would become very slow, making them one of the Pokémon that Cramorant most enjoyed swallowing and spitting out.

"Although not particularly precious, at least it's not Magikarp."

Johan was overjoyed.

Good luck!

"This water area indeed has very abundant resources."

Before he could finish his thoughts, Johan caught a second Arrokuda, then a third, fourth, fifth, sixth...

"No way."

Johan didn't believe it and cast his hook again.

He had thought it was beginner's luck in the early morning, but had he actually hit an Arrokuda nest?

On the other side.

Gengar sat under a tree with its complete tea set arranged on the table, the kettle bubbling with hot steam.

"Ka-kaah~Ka-kaah~"

Humming a little tune, it leisurely began boiling and brewing tea.

Of course, the main attraction was the newly acquired tea set—Polteageist and two Sinistea.

Regarding this, Polteageist and Sinistea appeared quite calm, or rather, even a bit excited.

They couldn't even remember how long they had been in that sunken ship, only knowing it had been ages since they had experienced the "baptism" of tea water.

They were looking forward to it...

Soon, Gengar fulfilled their expectations.

Gengar tossed Energy Root with a slightly bitter taste into Polteageist, then poured in boiling water. Immediately, the characteristic bitter and astringent aroma of Energy Root filled Polteageist completely.

Tap tap tap tap—

The pot lid suddenly started shaking as the purple figure inside Polteageist seemed to realize something was wrong and struggled to escape.

This wasn't tea! This was Energy Root!

Gengar calmly pressed its finger on the lid, silently counting the time.

"Ka-kaah!"

About right!

Gengar confidently picked up the teapot and poured it into the Sinistea.

Soon, two steaming cups of Energy Root tea were brewed.

The purple fatty gently moved its finger, pushing one cup in front of the Skwovet leader.

"Skwo?"

Skwovet looked at the tea with interest. Gengar had already picked up the other cup and gently blew on it.

Blow—

Then it slowly took a sip.

Smack smack smack... hmm?

It seemed quite tasty, apparently better than before!

Seeing Gengar had already taken a sip, Skwovet immediately put away its suspicious expression, held the teacup and imitated Gengar's actions, blowing once, then taking a sip...

"Skwo... Skwo!"

Skwovet's eyes widened as it wanted to spit it out, but met Gengar's teasing gaze and forcibly held it back.

Then you could see Skwovet's face gradually change from its original reddish-brown to white, then slowly to green, and finally to gray. Its eyes rolled back as it collapsed on the table, foaming at the mouth, with its little feet still twitching.

"Ka-kaah~" Gengar curled its lip.

Still a leader? Acting tough in front of this old man? You're not up to it~

It blew on the tea again and took another sip, feeling it tasted better and better the more it drank.

This treasure was truly worth finding~

"What happened to it?"

Johan gave up fishing and walked back with his rod, seeing the Skwovet leader collapsed on the table foaming at the mouth.

Gengar gestured toward the Sinistea on the table.

"Normal-type Pokémon are immune to Ghost-type moves, aren't they?" Johan looked puzzled.

Sinistea shouldn't be able to cause any harm to Skwovet, right?

Moreover, these two Sinistea and even Polteageist combined probably didn't have levels as high as this Skwovet.

Gengar shrugged.

"Ka-kaah~"

Exactly~

Speaking, it brewed another cup for Johan, handing over the Sinistea.

Johan's expression immediately changed as he waved his hand:

"Cough, I'll pass. I still need to dig trees and try to bring back as many berry trees as possible at once."

Whether it was Sinistea's tea that tasted bad and drained energy, or Polteageist's brewed tea that was supposedly very flavorful, Johan had no interest in trying either.

How to put it...

Wasn't this like drinking Sinistea and Polteageist's "bath water"?

He wasn't Lance—he wasn't into that.

As they say, light fishing brings joy, heavy fishing harms the body. After catching more than ten Arrokuda, Johan gave up and dove back into the berry grove on the plains, huffing and puffing as he started digging saplings.

Worth mentioning.

In the Pokémon world, work efficiency was indeed high.

With Pokémon assistance, in just two short days, they had organized the originally chaotic berry grove quite well.

They obtained many berry saplings of various sizes, plus one extremely rare "Miraculous Berry."

Considering that berry sapling transplantation should be done sooner rather than later, Johan bid farewell to the wild Pokémon of Ballimere Lake plains and the Skwovet in the afternoon, returning to Crown Tundra.

"When you have time, go to Slumbering Weald."

Calyrex took Spectrier's reins from Gengar's hands.

These past few days had been quite enjoyable riding it, and it didn't insist on taking Spectrier back.

At worst... when it needed help in the future, it could just call Spectrier to assist, right?

Calyrex still had part of its original power remaining in Spectrier that it hadn't taken back. Only by gathering both its beloved horses could Calyrex's power return to normal.

As for its peak... that would probably be difficult to see again.

Without sufficient "faith power," Calyrex's strength could hardly return to when it was the King of Galar.

"Slumbering Weald?" Johan raised an eyebrow.

Slumbering Weald was located in the southern mountain forests of Crown Tundra, but was blocked by continuous mountain ranges and glaciers. Even flying there from Crown Tundra would be very difficult.

Because Slumbering Weald wasn't just in the mountains—it was perpetually shrouded in thick fog, famously easy to get lost in.

The only relatively good route into Slumbering Weald was through Wedgehurst.

Others might not know what was in Slumbering Weald, but Johan knew clearly.

The two legendary heroes of Galar, Zacian and Zamazenta, slumbered in Slumbering Weald.

Combined with what Calyrex had told him about its deeds...

When Eternatus created the "Darkest Day" back then, it probably allied with Zacian and Zamazenta.

Now asking Johan to visit Slumbering Weald when he had the chance...

Was it sensing signs of Eternatus awakening?

"Yes, for your Tinkaton..." Calyrex looked at Tinkaton nearby: "It should be quite helpful."

Tinkaton?

Johan also looked at his hammer girl.

The little one was holding her hammer like a detector, looking around with her head raised, seemingly wondering if a big bird would appear in the sky.

This was about having hammer girl "hammer" the rusty sword and shield?

Johan seemed to understand Calyrex's meaning.

In Pokémon Special, the protagonist Souji, as a master blacksmith, had significant connections to the rusty sword and shield.

Moreover, both Zacian and Zamazenta were Steel-type Pokémon.

"If I have the chance, I'll go." Johan nodded without much hesitation.

For things beneficial to his Pokémon, now that his strength had improved, he was willing to try.

After all, he'd experienced the Hoopa incident and seen so many legendary Pokémon. As long as he didn't encounter those super-scale legendaries like Eternatus or Necrozma, Johan had some confidence.

Even with Eternatus...

As long as he could find the rusty sword and shield and awaken Zacian and Zamazenta, dealing with Eternatus shouldn't be a big problem.

As for now...

He needed to go back first and plant those hard-won berry saplings before the success rate of transplantation decreased over time.

"If you have the chance, you can also visit Hoenn." Johan extended an invitation.

If Calyrex could visit his island, the resource growth on the island would probably get a super boost.

Regarding Johan's invitation, Calyrex didn't refuse.

However...

Leading Spectrier, it sighed softly.

"Although this king's subjects no longer remember this king, this king still considers itself their king. Protecting them is a king's responsibility."

Seeing Eternatus becoming increasingly active, with Galar particles even reaching Crown Tundra, how could Calyrex be willing to leave the Galar region that needed it most at this time?

Hearing this, Johan sighed inwardly, somewhat admiring Calyrex's sense of responsibility.

Indeed, this cabbage head was worthy of being the King of Galar.

After bidding farewell to Calyrex again, Johan found the Butterfree colony they had previously agreed upon.

After several days of consideration, the Butterfree had also made their decision.

They entrusted Johan with taking away three Butterfree, five Metapod, and seven Caterpie, while the Butterfree leader and the remaining Butterfree, Metapod, and Caterpie chose to stay in the land that had born and raised them.

This was the classic strategy of not putting all eggs in one basket.

Although they had witnessed Johan's strength and felt his goodwill, they still felt some apprehension about unknown places.

Johan didn't force them and stated that he might return next time, bringing the Butterfree that had lived with him for a while. Then they could make another choice.

With that...

Johan, with abundant gains, returned to Hoenn with Flint and his Pokémon.

August 3rd, sunny weather.

After getting off the plane and resting briefly at the café, he took his Pokémon and his "laborer" Flint straight to the island.

Although he'd only been away for a few days, the island's appearance had changed significantly.

The originally barren island was now covered with a thin layer of green grass.

Lush and green.

From a distance, you could feel the vigorous life force emanating from the island.

"Excellent." Johan looked pleased. "The Gogoat and Dugtrio have worked hard."

The scene before him proved that the island had completed its most basic transformation and was now suitable for vegetation growth.

The ground left by solidified lava was rich in minerals but too hard, obviously unsuitable for plant roots to grow. With the Dugtrio's diligent cultivation, these solid lava stones had become extremely nutrient-rich soil.

If this weren't the Pokémon world, completing such transformation would undoubtedly be very troublesome and difficult. But in the Pokémon world, not only was the transformation completed, it also seemed not very difficult.

The Gogoat covering the entire soil with grass further verified the island's current soil environment.

Besides the grass...

The pit previously dug by Dragonite and the others in the island's center was now filled with a pool of fresh water.

This way, the most basic water source needed for living was satisfied.

By releasing some gentle Water-type Pokémon into the pond, they wouldn't have to worry about stagnant water.

Getting off the aircraft.

Johan took out all his "gains" from this Crown Tundra trip.

This included Pokémon: three Butterfree, five Metapod, seven Caterpie, six Applin, and of course the tea set "conquered" by Gengar—one Polteageist and two Sinistea didn't count.

Adding the two Dugtrio and two Gogoat already here...

The number of Pokémon living on the island had broken into double digits and exceeded twenty!

Besides Pokémon, there were also numerous plants, especially berry tree saplings.

Specifically: one "Miraculous Berry," five Oran Berry saplings, two Pecha Berry saplings, seven Rawst Berry saplings, ten Oran Berry and Sitrus Berry saplings each, three Nanab Berry saplings, five each of Pinap, Razz, Bluk, Nanab, and Wepear Berry saplings.

Plus mature berry trees dug from his own garden: three each of Oran, Rawst, Pecha, Persim, Lum, and Leppa Berries.

In total, they would plant eighty berry trees!

"Big project!"

Watching Gengar take them out one by one from its shadow, Johan couldn't help sighing.

But besides sighing about the big project, Johan felt more joy and satisfaction.

Finally...

Finally, he was really farming!

Eighty berry trees weren't large by farm standards.

Many farms had berry trees counted in the "hundreds."

Like Elder Fukuji's farm, the berries were said to be counted in the "thousands."

That was a truly large farm.

Only such farms could support high-consumption trainers like Johan.

However, although it couldn't compare to those large farms, these eighty berry trees, once fully mature, would produce enough berries to greatly reduce Johan's financial burden.

Moreover, the island was so large that they could continue planting and expanding. One day, the island's berry production would not only satisfy his and his Pokémon's needs but even have surplus to sell.

This was always a very good start.

"Gengar, move 'Calyrex' to the lakeside in the island's center."

Johan began directing everyone to action.

"Ka-kaah~!"

After Calyrex recovered part of its strength, the power it applied to the wood carving had also become stronger.

Now, even placing the carving in the island's center, the power from the "King of Bountiful Harvests" could cover the entire island even across great distances.

Gengar picked up the carving from the cultivated farmland and placed it beside the lake.

Then, while Johan called everyone to start planting trees, he walked to the island's center.

Not far from Calyrex's carving, he dug a pit and took out the "Miraculous Berry."

According to Elder Fukuji's knowledge, for berries with high nutritional and environmental requirements, planting the entire fruit would be a good choice.

As for processes like drying seeds, soaking, and germination, the special nature of berries allowed skipping these steps.

"Hope it can grow."

After gently stroking the "Miraculous Berry," Johan placed it in the pit and covered it with soil.

Then he took out his prepared Squirtle watering can and sprinkled some water, moistening the soil.

Whether it could grow depended on whether the island's conditions could satisfy its growth factors.

"Calyrex, please watch over it." Johan smiled and spoke to the carving.

Hum—

The Calyrex carving faintly glowed with crystalline green light, as if saying—as you wish.

After planting the most important "Miraculous Berry," Johan turned and joined the berry sapling transplantation.

It was now summer with high temperatures and strong sun, honestly not a good time for transplantation.

However, these problems could be overcome to some extent.

Sapling transplantation was much simpler than digging, at least without worrying too much about root damage.

Even...

With help from Calyrex's carving and the Gogoat, several berry saplings in good condition had their originally withered leaves recover at visible speed.

While planting, Johan also comforted the Pokémon who were somewhat uncomfortable with the environment.

Especially the six Applin.

The Butterfree group, although in a new environment, had been briefed by Johan in advance, so they calmed down quickly.

But the six Applin, facing this island with fertile soil but still looking somewhat barren despite having eighty berry trees planted, seemed somewhat cramped and afraid.

They huddled together inside their apples.

Anyone not knowing would think they had harvested a pile of apples.

Fortunately, Johan was professional in communicating with and comforting Pokémon.

Combined with food temptation, a safe environment, and Johan's kind guidance, the six Applin finally slowly ended their disguise and tentatively observed their surroundings.

Johan had already checked—among these six Applin, four had the "Ripen" ability, while the other two had the "Gluttony" ability. None had hidden abilities.

Because the "Gluttony" ability meant relatively high food demands.

So Johan had decided that if conditions allowed future Applin evolution, the four with "Ripen" would evolve into Flapple and Appletun, maintaining the "Ripen" ability.

The other two with "Gluttony" would evolve toward Dipplin and Hydrapple.

They could serve as the main force for breeding Applin colonies while taking on certain island protection duties.

With berry saplings planted, it was foreseeable that when these saplings matured and began bearing fruit, they would inevitably attract coveting from some wild Pokémon.

Whether flying in the sky or swimming in the sea, both were possible.

Johan couldn't stay on the island long-term as a guard—his teaching duties and Champion goal wouldn't give him such ample time.

By then, the island would need certain self-defense capabilities.

Butterfree could be one choice, and future Hydrapple would be another good option. He might invite more wild Pokémon to live on the island in the future, gradually expanding.

However, one thing was certain.

Before the island was completely self-sufficient, he would need to invest more resources and funds.

But once they got through this "development" period, the pressure would drop sharply.

"The question is how to survive..."

Even if he wouldn't train the island's Pokémon like Gengar and Ninetales, basic diet still needed to be satisfied, right?

Twenty-plus Pokémon, even just basic daily meals, would be a considerable expense each day.

"I originally wanted to raise some Miltank, Mareep, and such to expand into animal husbandry, but now it seems I'll have to wait."

If the burden was too heavy, he couldn't handle it either.

He just didn't know how long his current savings would last.

Pushing aside complex thoughts, he planted another berry sapling, covered it with soil, and sprinkled water.

Johan clapped his hands and wiped sweat from his forehead.

Looking around...

He saw Snivy standing silently by the lake.

With gentle breeze, the lake surface sparkled.

Vaguely, Johan seemed to see some special connection forming between Snivy and the "Miraculous Berry" just planted at its feet.

Hmm?

Aura spread.

Johan could see that connection more clearly.

It seemed that from Snivy's body, a Grass-type energy was flowing through root tendrils extending from its feet, gradually injecting into the just-planted "Miraculous Berry."

At the same time, energy was slowly emanating from the "Miraculous Berry" and being absorbed by Snivy's root tendrils.

This was somewhat beyond Johan's understanding.

What was this doing?

Establishing a connection with the "Miraculous Berry" or future "giant tree" in advance?

Because of Snivy's "Blessing of the Forest"?

However, seeing that Snivy wasn't losing out and was even benefiting, Johan didn't interfere.

Although the "Miraculous Berry" and its future tree might be rare and precious, compared to his own Pokémon... that seemed insignificant.

Besides, Johan didn't think Snivy's actions would cause him much loss. This seemed more like mutually beneficial cooperation.

Both sides could benefit.

The only difference was that Snivy might experience some fatigue in the short term.

But probably sleeping would restore it.

"Could this be why these 'Miraculous Berry' trees are so difficult to cultivate?" Johan felt he was vaguely grasping something.

This could be a research direction.

"Wait."

However, before Johan could be happy long, he suddenly realized.

"Never mind other things, this way... Snivy's demand for energy, more precisely for food, has increased?"

Great.

You two have mutual benefit and mutual promotion, but the one paying is my wallet!

Johan pouted. After observing for a while and confirming Snivy was fine, he decided out of sight, out of mind.

"Right! My curry!"

Johan suddenly reacted.

He'd been busy dealing with those two Galar particles' Dynamax and forgotten there was still curry cooking in the pot!

Crown Tundra, Crown Temple.

Calyrex, leading Glastrier, was slowly clearing temple ruins, especially cleaning the stables.

It suddenly looked up.

Frowning.

Two red particle beams streaked across Crown Tundra's sky.

As an "old opponent," Calyrex knew this was the power of that meteorite from outer space—Eternatus.

Just after awakening, it had sensed that the entire Galar region was filled with Eternatus's energy, just not as concentrated as these two dark red beams.

"This king's subjects..."

It didn't know if its subjects were affected by Eternatus, whether they lived in dire straits.

But halfway through this sentence, Calyrex smiled self-mockingly.

No one remembered it anymore—where were its so-called "subjects"?

The Galar particles streaked past, falling on the distant giant tree hill.

"Neighhhh——"

Glastrier suddenly became restless, hooves pacing back and forth, seemingly sensing Spectrier's power, and...

"Indeed."

Calyrex's eyes also brightened slightly.

"Johan's Gengar can indeed control Spectrier and gain part of Spectrier's power."

It had actually noticed early on the possibility of "fusion" between Gengar and Spectrier.

This was why it wasn't eager to reclaim Spectrier and let Johan and Gengar take Spectrier out together.

On one hand, it wanted to repay Johan and Gengar for their help.

On the other hand, it wanted to verify its inner speculation.

Facts proved its guess was correct.

Whoosh—

A large sailing ship rode the wind and waves, approaching the island.

Drake, wearing a wide captain's coat, looked at the transformed island with some surprise in his eyes.

This island... Johan had really developed it? And so quickly planted so many things?

"Salamence!"

Riding Salamence, Drake came to the island.

Stepping on the soft soil covered with thin grass, smelling the faint floral fragrance, Drake's surprised expression grew stronger.

"Johan, you really have the potential to be a farm owner." Drake laughed loudly, walking toward the busy Johan.

Johan, who had long noticed the ship approaching, smiled without stopping his work: "Yes, Elder Fukuji said I'm naturally suited for this work. He even regretted not meeting me earlier, otherwise he would have passed down his legacy to me."

This made Drake laugh even louder.

"Flower cakes?" Seeing the items on the table, his eyes lit up.

He casually grabbed one and stuffed it in his mouth, while taking out four red and white Poké Balls.

Looking at those Poké Balls, Johan immediately put down his work and asked with some surprise:

"Lotad?"

Gulp—

Drake swallowed the flower cake and drank several sips of freshly squeezed berry juice before saying with satisfaction:

"Right. What you applied for—I got them for you immediately."

Johan immediately threw out the Poké Balls.

Four Lotad appeared on the ground.

Being Pokémon bred in League breeding houses, they weren't shy. After observing for a while, they happily ran toward the pond in the island's center.

Lotad were Water and Grass-type Water Weed Pokémon with blue bodies and bright green lily pads on their backs.

This was a species that greatly preferred clean water and also had certain water purification functions. The lily pads on their backs had anti-pollution properties, reducing dust entering the pond.

Upon entering the water, the four Lotad immediately floated leisurely, looking very satisfied.

Seeing this, Johan smiled with satisfaction and looked at Drake again.

"However, having a Four Kings member like you make a special trip for such a small matter?"

Then another person squeezed over.

"Teacher Johan, save some for me." Speaking, he reached out to grab several flower cakes and picked up a cup of berry juice.

"Who are you?" Drake asked.

"Me?" After eating the flower cake, "I'm Flint!"

Drake looked at the dark-skinned Flint, that still familiar red explosive hair, and immediately understood that Flint had been working as Johan's laborer. His mouth twitched: "Nonsense, Flint isn't as handsome as you."

"Really?" Flint touched his cheek, believing it: "Hey, I just got a bit tanned recently."

Johan pressed his lips, holding back laughter.

These past few days, Flint had indeed contributed considerably.

Drake wasn't so considerate, laughing heartily until Flint was confused.

After laughing, he answered Johan's earlier question.

"It's not a special trip, I just happened to be nearby."

Pausing, he became more serious: "But I'm also here representing the League to tell you—preparations are about ready. Choose a time soon and begin."

Preparations?

The Champion's Path!

Johan understood.

But seeing Drake's expression more eager than his own...

Drake, even if I clear the "Champion's Path," you still can't retire.

----------
